Dean, UBC Sauder School of Business  
RBC Financial Group Professor of Entrepreneurship

## Welcome from Dean Darren Dahl

As a family member or guardian of a UBC Sauder student, you are a vital part of the school’s community\.

We believe your support and engagement in your student’s academic life plays a huge part in their success\. This Parent & Family Network page is designed to equip you with easy access to some of the tools, resources and information you need to champion the student in your life\.

We’re committed to building a collaborative and respectful environment where everyone can thrive\. We’re advancing our progress in equity, diversity and inclusion to create an even greater culture of belonging\. Our hope is that our students will carry these values forward into their professional and civic lives\.

We are excited to work together with you to help our students explore their interests, discover their many talents and reach their full potential\.

**Welcome to the UBC Sauder community\.**

title: Hey UBC Sauder!
content_markdown:
[Image](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/slide-extralarge/public/slideshow-images/69983826_1676507602484191_3809844009703047168_o_1676507595817525.jpg?itok=q3dJi6Ed&timestamp=1649719551)

Do you want to help welcome new students to the UBC Sauder community? We're hiring students for Imagine Day and The Spark 2026\!

### We're looking for individuals who:

-   embody the UBC Sauder Spirit
-   are passionate about making sure every new student feels welcome in the UBC Sauder community
-   exemplify UBC Sauder’s core values of rigour, respect, and responsibility
-   know how to have responsible fun with a good sense of judgement
-   love being a UBC Sauder student\!

### What orientation programs are happening?

We are planning to deliver a fun orientation experience\. Help welcome 600\+ new\-to\-Sauder students this orientations through Imagine Day and The Spark\!

#### [Jump Start \(September 2 \- 4, 2026\)](https://you.ubc.ca/jump-start-vancouver)

-   More information can be found on: [you\.ubc\.ca/jump\-start\-vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/jump-start-vancouver/)
-   For all newly admitted first\-year students
-   Students will participate in group components to help them make friends and feel prepared to start their academic journey at UBC

#### [Imagine UBC \(Tuesday, September 8, 2026\)](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc)

-   For all newly admitted first\-year and transfer undergraduate students
-   Students will meet a faculty member and other new UBC Sauder students, be officially welcomed by the Dean, participate in a pep rally, and learn about involvement opportunities across campus
-   Applications have closed for Senior Orientations Leaders  
    
-   Hiring open for Orientation Leaders\! Applications Close May 3

#### [The Spark \(Friday, September 11, 2026 and Saturday, September 12, 2026\)](https://www.ubcsauderspark.com/)

-   For all new\-to\-UBC students which includes students admitted to Year 1 and transfer students
-   We are planning for an in\-person experience in which students will be in groups with others in their cohort, participating in fun games and small group activities\.
-   Check out [The Spark 2025 Recap Video](https://youtu.be/aeb_HzxrZlU?si=WHqX50jv28OFNF0y)
-   The Spark Hiring Timeline 

-   More hiring information about The Spark can be found [here](https://www.ubcsauderspark.com/) 
-   Applications have closed for Spark Exec Team[https://www\.ubcsauderspark\.com/spark\-exec\-hiring\-2026](https://www.ubcsauderspark.com/spark-exec-hiring-2026)
-   Hiring open for Spirit Leaders\! Applications Close May 3
-   [Hiring open for Spark Volunteers\!](https://www.ubcsauderspark.com/volunteers) Applications Close in August

Do I need to be an extrovert to be an OL or Spark Volunteer?

Absolutely not\. We understand that orientations can seem like a loud, outgoing event, and admittedly, there is cheering\. That being said, we have many different types of students coming to UBC Sauder, and many types of Orientation Leaders\. We want orientation to be welcoming to all\! We are looking to hire a team that is balanced and representative of the UBC Sauder community, with all energy levels represented\.

How are leader hiring decisions made?

Applications will be reviewed against the job description, the goals of Imagine UBC, and UBC Sauder values\. Participants will be invited to a group interview, where our team will assess candidates around scenarios and general fit for the role

What if I'm already a Jumpstart Leader?

Starting 2025, Jumpstart Leaders can also be UBC Sauder Orientation Leaders\!

title: Reimbursement Instructions for Student Experience Grants
content_markdown:
### Personal experience

If you are claiming funding to offset expenses for a personal experience such as volunteer/service learning or attending a competition or conference\.

**After your experience:**

**Receipts:**

-   Collect all of the receipt\(s\) for the expenses you are claiming\. Compile into a single PDF document and save with the naming convention **firstname\_lastname\_receipts**
-   Screenshots are not accepted\. Please make sure to submit a complete confirmation of payment document \(PDF or email confirmation\)\.
-   Please make sure receipts have an itemized breakdown \(showing tax amount and how much each item cost\)
-   All receipts will need to show detailed payment information, such as credit card used and your full name\. If this is not possible, students should additionally submit a credit card statement\.
-   What if someone else on the team made the purchase for me? Or I only paid for a portion of the costs?
-   Make sure you submit a screenshot or confirmation of the etransfer to show that you have paid for your portion or someone paid you back for their portion

**Letter of Impact:**

-   Prepare a letter of impact to the OSAS, explaining the impact this experience and funding has had on your personal, professional or academic experience\. Save as a single PDF document with the naming convention **firstname\_lastname\_letter**
-   If you have taken photos during your experience, please upload them as well

**Once you have those things ready:**

-   Complete the online [**Student Experience Grant Acceptance Form**](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dmR0Fp61wpUux4q "https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/sv_87b6cnddxdpvmhn") and upload your receipts and letter by the deadline indicated in the email\.

title: COMM_V 386T - Indigenous Peoples and Economic Development
content_markdown:
The business community in Canada is striving to build stronger economic relationships with Indigenous communities\. Exposing undergraduates to this subject will provide them with an understanding of the complexities and importance of Indigenous engagement, and better prepare them for roles in the private sector\. While the focus will be on Indigenous engagement in Canada, the tools and frameworks presented will be applicable to cross\-cultural business practices in many environments\. This course will support these priorities by presenting:

-   A high\-level review of political, legal, cultural, and historical contexts;
-   Case studies on the private sector's engagement with Indigenous peoples;
-   Frameworks that present best practices and tools for enduring and successful economic relationships\.

### Learning objectives

-   Identify and understand the historical, legal, cultural and political contexts that make engagement with Indigenous communities both challenging and important\.
-   Appreciate the unique role the private sector can play in promoting economic reconciliation with Indigenous peoples in Canada\.
-   Understand the business best practices that can support successful and enduring economic partnerships with Indigenous communities\.
-   Apply these business best practices to cases from across various economic sectors, including real estate, forestry, energy, forestry, and tourism\.

Note: COMM 386T is open to all undergraduate students in Year 3 or 4\. No prerequisites required\. COMM 386T will not be offered in 2026W\.

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 386U - Social Media Strategy
content_markdown:
Social media is changing how business is done around the world in almost every industry\. The marketing and business worlds are undergoing fundamental changes in how consumers interact with brands and each other\. Social media has helped give consumers a voice and connect them with their friends and other like\-minded consumers, and it has also opened up numerous new communication channels available for marketers and brands to connect with current and potential customers\.

This course is designed to help you understand how marketing has \(and has not\) changed due to the rise of social media and changes in various underlying contextual factors, such as dramatically increased speed of information dissemination across consumers and brands\. The overarching goal is to obtain a clear perspective on what’s really going on in digital/social/mobile marketing so that you can begin to appreciate its true value to consumers, to managers, and to other corporate stakeholders\. It will equip you with the relevant knowledge, perspectives, and practical skills required to develop marketing strategies that leverage the opportunities inherent in social media and consumer\-to\-consumer social interactions for achieving business and marketing goals\.

### Learning objectives

Upon completion of this course, you will be able to:

-   Understand what social media is and how this new type of media and communications technology influences how business and marketing is done
-   Understand key principles of “connected consumers” from psychological and sociological perspectives, and how these principles can be leveraged when developing social media marketing strategies
-   Develop skill in using the predominant social media tools currently available for business/marketing communication 
-   Discover innovative uses for social media in a variety of business areas and processes \(e\.g\., new product development and service management\)
-   Understand how to use various social media channels to publish and disseminate relevant branded content in order to engage consumers and to increase social impact, influence, and value
-   Develop a strategic plan for identifying opportunities for using social media in a company

Prerequisite: [COMM 296](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/5225)\.

Course credits:

3

### Check back in September to apply for Term 1 Student Experience Grants\!

If you have any questions, please reach out to Stanley Turner Fowler at stanley\.turnerfowler@sauder\.ubc\.ca

## Overview

## What is the Student Experience Grant? 

OSAS provides funding to students to help you participate in experiential learning opportunities and create new student\-led initiatives\. 

## What can I use the Grant for? 

Grants are available to partially offset expenses for a variety of experiential learning opportunities, including but not limited to:

-   Participating in a volunteer or service learning program
-   Competing in a case competition
-   Attending a conference
-   Organizing a new event, program or service that benefits other BCom students

## Who is eligible to apply?

###### Students currently registered in the DAP Program, BCom program or BUCS program \(Combined Major in Business and Computer Science\) at the time of application\. 

## Application Process

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Application Deadline** | **When you will be notified of funding** |
| Term 1 | October 4, 2026 | October 16, 2026 |
| Term 2 | January 31, 2027 | February 12, 2027 |

If granted funding, individual applicants and clubs/services are not permitted to apply for funding again for a minimum of 2 academic years\. For example, if funding is granted in the 2025\-2026 academic year, the same student will not be considered for funding until 2027\-2028\.   

Successful applicants will be required to submit a photo of the experience/event and a letter of impact outlining the skills they developed through the funded experience, along with an overview of the experience/event\. 

BCom Students are encouraged to apply to Student Experience Grants, [CUS Competition and Conference Fund \(CCF\)](https://linktr.ee/CCF.CUS), and [Commerce Student Initiative Fund \(CSIF\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/ugogrant) and can accept funding from all 3 funding sources, as long as they meet the specific eligibility criteria for funding\. The maximum amount of funding students are allowed to receive in total cannot exceed their total expenses\. 

I went on my experience already, can I apply now and get some reimbursement?

  
Yes\! If you have already participated in the event, but didn’t apply to the Student Experience Grant, you can apply now to get 1/3 of your eligible costs reimbursed\.

Please see below for what the Eligible Experiences and Funding Guidelines are\.

## Past Recipients

Unsure about what kinds of experiences to pursue? Here's how a past recipient used their grant to develop their professional skills and enhance their learning\.

-   Carman Cheung
-   Jeffrey Low
-   Maggie Tomlinson
-   Mariia Radaeva
-   Yuting Dai & Ciro Wei

##### Carman Cheung

Carman Cheung received funds to attend the Harvard Social Enterprise Conference

[Image](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/resize/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/6_0-374x281.jpg?itok=GIlEeIEu)OSAS Student Experience Grant recipient, Carman Cheung

OSAS Student Experience Grant recipient, Carman Cheung

**How did the experience impact you?**

Thanks to the UBC Sauder Student Experience Grant and UBC CUS CCF, I spent the weekend of March 23\-24, 2024 attending the Harvard Social Enterprise Conference held by Harvard Business School and Harvard Kennedy School\. At this conference, I learned so much about the relationships between businesses and sustainability\. The most impactful panel I learned from was the Gender\-Lens Investing: The Next Decade\. At this panel, I heard from powerful, experienced, and smart women who shared their experiences in impact investing, micro\-investing, and as women investors\. It was so refreshing to see these women and hear the lessons they learned throughout their journey in investing\.

I came out of this conference weekend inspired and feeling more motivated to change the world in the ways that I can\. The Social Enterprise Conference made me more optimistic about the future of businesses and allowed me to see the world more optimistically\. A large part of the conference was the vast network and how many passionate and successful individuals there were\. I got the opportunity to speak with CEOs, activists, and government officials\.

##### Jeffrey Low

[Jeffrey Low](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/resize/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/dsc05624_0-414x276.jpg?itok=RHSRjfgA)

UGO Student Experience Grant recipient, Jeffrey Low

  
Jeffrey Low received funding to host a new event, Soar Startup Pitch Competition, designed to showcase entrepreneurial talent and innovative ideas in Sauder\.

**How did the experience impact you?**

I am profoundly grateful to have had the opportunity to lead Soar and for the immense support of the Undergraduate Office, through generously providing the $1,500 Student Experience Grant\. At the time of organizing Soar, UBC Startups was not an AMS affiliated organization, so we relied on the financial support of the UGO Student Experience Grant to host the event for the community\.

As an aspiring startup founder, it is paramount that I develop a track record of successful projects I can demonstrate my ability to build and innovate\. Soar was the greatest test of my entrepreneurial ability so far because it was the largest event we have hosted\.

It is heartwarming to know that my vision for UBC as a hub in North America for student entrepreneurship is becoming a reality\. By bringing $15,000 in external funding to fuel student\-run startups and creating a platform that challenges them to strive for excellence, I firmly believe this event will help spark the next wave of innovation on campus\.  
  

##### Maggie Tomlinson

Maggie received funding to host the first ever Indigenous Business Conference, in partnership with the AMS Indigenous Business Association\. 

[Photo of Maggie Tomlinson](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/resize/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/maggie_tomlinson_-_iba_1-332x221.jpeg?itok=plGJCHQX)

UGO Student Experience Grant recipient, Maggie Tomlinson

**How did this experience impact you?**

OSAS Student Experience Grant provided an invaluable opportunity not only for me but also for over 30 BCom students to actively participate in a day dedicated to economic reconciliation\. This funding marked a significant milestone for our club, serving as the initial support we received for the conference and igniting hope that our vision of hosting such an event could be possible\. We had the chance to connect, learn, and meet Indigenous panel speakers, Indigenous high school students, and firm representatives\. There were 3 rounds of panelist speaker focusing on Indigenous perspectives on economic reconciliation and highlighting the impactful work of these individuals\. The Indigenous Business Association anticipates organizing more successful conferences, with the aim of engaging a broader audience of both Indigenous and non\-Indigenous students interested in gaining insights into Indigenous business practices\.

##### Mariia Radaeva

[Photo of Mariia Radaeva](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/resize/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/dsc03687_0-341x227.jpeg?itok=YQ7GLy3D)

UGO Student Experience Grant recipient, Mariia Radaeva

Mariia received funding to host a new event, the Innovation Fair, in partnership with Innovation OnBoard\.

**How did the experience impact you?**

The experience of organizing the Innovation Fair has profoundly impacted my personal and professional development\. It sharpened my leadership skills, teaching me the nuances of event management, teamwork, and effective communication\. On a personal level, it was a journey of growth, filled with learning opportunities from mentors and peers alike, which ignited a deep\-seated passion for innovation within me\. Professionally, this experience has enriched my resume and provided a compelling narrative for job interviews, showcasing my ability to lead, innovate, and inspire\. The skills and confidence gained have opened new doors and have been pivotal in shaping my career path\.

##### Yuting Dai & Ciro Wei

[Photo of Yuting Dai &amp;amp; Ciro Wei](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/resize/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/yuting_dai_ciro_wei-340x227.jpg?itok=R_qsNHN2)

UGO Student Experience Grant recipients, Yuting Dai & Ciro Wei

Yuting and Ciro both received funding to participate in the AIESEC Canada National Congress 2024\.

**How did the experience impact you?**

Yuting: it was my first time being in the capital of Canada, and I got to meet some of the most inspiring young leaders from across the country \(TMU, U of Calgary, U of T, etc\.\)\. We shared our personal stories, our AIESEC journeys, our new ideas for this organization and eventually why we stay and connect with the AIESEC values — cross\-cultural understanding and leadership\. It gives me chills everyday meeting people who are similarly passionate about creating a real impact on people and the world, and seeing how our passion is translated into actions and operations numbers  
  
Ciro: The National Congress was a transformative event where I had the privilege of not only participating but also being recognized with the prestigious National Contribution Award in AIESEC in Canada, sponsored by RBC Future Launch\. This acknowledgment of my year\-long dedication and growth within AIESEC was immensely gratifying, reinforcing my commitment to furthering my impact while leveraging AIESEC's partnership with RBC Future Launch\. Professionally, the conference provided a platform for me to hone essential skills such as pitching, public speaking, and leadership\. Through various sessions and activities, I had the opportunity to practice and refine these skills, equipping me with valuable tools for my future endeavors\.

## Frequently Asked Questions \(FAQ's\)

Are entrepreneurial pursuits eligible for funding?

This fund is not intended to finance start up businesses\. For this type of funding, please look into opportunities at [entrepreneurship@UBC](https://entrepreneurship.ubc.ca/)\.

Am I eligible for academic concessions?

If you find that an event is creating a conflict between coursework or an exam, you may be eligible for academic concession if the circumstances meet the criteria outlined in the academic concession policy for *conflicting responsibilities*\. We encourage you to review the information here before submitting your petition\. [https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/academic\-concession](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/academic-concession "https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/academic-concession")\.

Please know that these concessions will be evaluated in the same manner as all other petitions for academic concession, and are not automatically approved because they are related to the Student Experience Grants program\. 

Am I able to fund my Go Global/Exchange experience?

This grant is not to be used to fund any experiences for which BCom students will receive credits that count towards their degrees, thus Go Global is ineligible for funding\. Go Global does typically offer financial subsidies however\. For more information, see here: [https://goglobal\.ubc\.ca/go\-global\.](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/exchange) 

I’m attending a Case Competition/Conference that is outside of the lower mainland\. How many nights am I able to request funding for?

Funding is available for accommodation for a total nights: **\# of conference days \+ 1**

I’m attending a Case Competition/Conference\. What elements of my experience are eligible to be included in my budget request?

Reimbursement is available for: major travel \(airplane/trains\), cost of hotel/AirBnB, and event registration fees\. Funding is not eligible for minor travel \(taxi/Uber/transit\) nor food/grocery costs\.

I’m applying for the grant for a team activity, but my teammate paid for everything\.

Your team is still able to be reimbursed, however the reimbursed amount would go to the person whose name is on the receipts\. The person whose name is on the receipts must be a BComor DAP student\. Your team would then coordinate payments between team members on your own terms\. This is not the responsibility of UBC Sauder\.

I am applying for the grant on behalf of my club/team\. Does this mean my entire team is ineligible to apply for further grant funding for the next two academic years?

If the grant is used to fund a student led event or initiative, or case competition/conference, the club/team will not be eligible for funding for the next two academic years\. However, the individual members are still eligible to apply for personal grants in the future\. 

If the committee decides to fund my application, however I do not accept, would I still have to wait two academic years before applying again?

No – The two\-year rule would only apply to applicants who received/were reimbursed for any amount of funding from the grant\.

As an applicant for a Student Led Initiative, what should I be cognizant of in my application?

The Student Experience Grant is looking to fund opportunities where applicants: \(1\) are proposing a new, innovative, and clearly defined program to fill a niche not already being filled for current BCom or DAP students\. \(2\) have a clear funding breakdown of how the funds will be spent\. \(3\) are able to provide justification and rationale for how they plan to implement the initiative, at scale\.

How will I receive funding from the OSAS Grant?

For individuals attending Volunteer/Service Learning/Case Competition/Conferences, once all of the purchases have been made, please submit all receipts through the funding acceptance form by the term deadline\. Only then will UBC Sauder Finance reimburse these costs\.

For organizers of Student Led Initiatives, if you are applying on behalf of an organization, your organization will invoice the OSAS Grant and UBC Sauder Finance will pay the invoice\. If you are an individual organizing an initiative, we will reimburse receipts after they have been purchased or you may direct your partners to invoice UBC Sauder directly\. The OSAS Grant does not pay invoices from individual students\.

### Have a quick career question? Peer Career Advisors are here to help\! 

We look forward to seeing you\!

Peer Career Advisors are a team of **senior BCom students** from different options who can offer a unique viewpoint on campus involvement and work experiences\.

They are trained by BCom Career Strategists on many aspects of the **job search and application** **process**\. As senior students who have been in your position before, Peer Career Advisors can point you in the right direction\. If you’re feeling stuck, **they’re here to help\!**

## The Canaccord Learning Commons & David Lam Management Research Library

**The Canaccord Learning Commons \(CLC\) and David Lam Management Research Library is a hub for UBC Sauder students\.**

The Canaccord Learning Commons and [David Lam Library](https://lam.library.ubc.ca/) provides support for all UBC Sauder School of Business students – including BCom’s, MBA’s, MBAN’s, MM’s, B\+MM’s, PhD’s, DAP, and all other degree programs – with learning support services, resources, and opportunities to hone the skills that will make them successful in the classroom and in the working world\.

Sauder students, check out our announcements, and access additional information, on the [CLC: Online](https://canvas.ubc.ca/courses/51980)\. You can use our [self\-serve online booking system](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/) to sign up\.

### Reasons to visit the CLC and Library

-   Access research help from business librarians, writing consultations, and subject specific support
-   Find and borrow print books and course reserves
-   Borrow equipment, including laptops, cameras, projectors, and chargers
-   Find group and silent study spaces or reserve a bookable group study room
-   Access ebooks and business databases
-   Browse the "Great Reads" collection of popular business books
-   Use specialized software in the Digital Media Lab, the Leith Wheeler Investment Research Lab, and the Wayne Deans Investment Analysis Centre
-   Use printers, photocopiers, scanners, desktop workstations, and dual display stations

##   
Booking with CLC & FAQs

### Sign Up for a Review Session, 1:1 Help, or a Workshop

The CLC offers support around Commerce, Math, and Econ courses\. We also offer Writing Consultations, Professional Communication, and help with learning to use Financial Databases, Digital Media Software, and more\. [Please use our self\-serve online booking system](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/) to sign up\.

[Sign\-Up Here\!](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/) 

Jane Privacy Statement

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    ###### Your personal information is collected under the authority of section 26\(c\) of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act \(FIPPA\)\. This information will be used for scheduling of Academic support workshops\. If you prefer not to use [Jane\.app](http://jane.app/) for booking, or have any questions about the privacy or security and/or disclosure of your personal information, please contact [clchelp@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:clchelp@sauder.ubc.ca)\.

### Jane Sign\-Up FAQ's 

**How can I sign up for a session?**

 You can book directly through the **[CLC Booking Page](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/)**\. 

-   Click on the session you want to book\. 
-   Choose the available timeslot on the “Book an Appointment” page\. 
-   When the confirmation pop\-up appears, click “I’m Done” or “Book More”\. 
-   You’ll be taken to the “Thank You for Booking” page — you’re all set\! 

**How can I join a waitlist for a certain session?**

 If a session is fully booked, you can join the waitlist\. 

-   Complete the **[CLC Booking Waitlist Form](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/wait_list/new?discipline_id=1&treatment_id=1)** \(also accessible through the CLC Booking Page\)\. 

-   Ensure Staff or Discipline matches the session\. 
-   Select the dates and times you wish to be notified about\. 
-   Choose SMS or Email notifications\. 

-   You’ll be redirected to **[“Your Account” page](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/account)**, where your waitlist request will appear\. 

⚠️ **Please Note:** When a spot opens, everyone on the waitlist is notified\. Appointments are filled on a first\-come, first\-served basis\. 

**How do I cancel or reschedule an appointment?**

You can manage your appointments from **[“Your Account” page](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/account)**  

-   Access it via the link at the bottom of your confirmation email, or  
-   Click on the “My Account” button in the top\-right corner of the booking page after signing in\. 
    

Under Upcoming Appointments, select the appointment you want to cancel or reschedule\. 

⚠️ **Please Note:** We ask that you cancel at least 48 hours in advance\. When you cancel, waitlisted students are automatically notified\. 

**How do I find the location of my session?**

Locations are listed at the top of the session description in the **[CLC Booking Page](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/)**, and in your booking confirmation/reminder emails \(denoted with ‼️\)\.

⚠️ **Please Note:** Be sure to note the specific room number or Zoom link, not the general CLC address shown on the booking site or calendar event\. 

**How do I add appointments to my preferred calendar software?**

  
Appointments can be synced automatically to your calendar

-   Go to **[“Your Account” page](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/account)**:

-   Access it via the link at the bottom of your confirmation email, or
-   Click on the "My Account" button in the top\-right corner of the booking page after signing in\.

-   Click "Subscribe to your calendar"\.
-   You will be redirected to a new page "Calendar Subscriptions"\. Choose an option or manually embed the \.ics subscription link into your preferred calendar app\.

**How do I manage email and text reminders?**

  
By default, you'll receive reminder notifications for:

-   Changes to your booked appointments\.
-   Waitlist openings \(only for sessions that you've joined the waitlist\)\.
-   A reminder 48 hours before your session\.

To update your preferences:

-   Go to **[“Your Account” page](https://canaccordlearningcommons.janeapp.com/account)** 

-   Access it via the link at the bottom of your confirmation email, or 
-   Click on the "My Account" button in the top\-right corner of the booking page after signing in\.

-   On the side bar, click "Notifications & Reminders"\.
-   Adjust your notification settings\.
-   Click "Save Preferences"\.

**Who do I contact if I have questions or need help?**

  
Please reach out to [clchelp@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:clchelp@sauder.ubc.ca)\. We will get you connected right away during regular business hours\. 

##   
Other Resources

### [Study Spaces](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/know-sauder/learning-commons-and-library/study-spaces)

The Canaccord Learning Commons offers a variety of study space options to individuals and groups\. Try out our different spaces to see which one suits you and your study style\.

[Learn More](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/know-sauder/learning-commons-and-library/study-spaces)

### [Book and Equipment Borrowing](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/know-sauder/learning-commons-and-library/book-and-equipment-borrowing)

The Library and CLC have a variety of books, e\-books and course reserves available to all students\. Students are also able to borrow a variety of equipment including chargers, presentation clickers, and laptops from our equipment pool\.

[Learn More](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/know-sauder/learning-commons-and-library/book-and-equipment-borrowing)

### [Printing and Photocopying](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/know-sauder/learning-commons-and-library/printing-and-photocopying)

The Learning Commons and Library offers a variety of options for printing, photocopying, and scanning\.

title: Requesting Documentation
content_markdown:
Your UBC transcript and diploma are official documents issued by the university to affirm your academic record and completion of degree program, respectively\.

On occasion, you may be asked by a third\-party to provide additional documentation regarding your studies at UBC, such as when applying to extend your study permit or proving your credentials to a potential employer\. This is typically provided in the form of a letter from the school which may, for example, confirm:

-   your status as a registered, full\-time student
-   your expected program completion date
-   your completion of degree requirements
-   conferral of your degree 

You can download some of these letters on demand from the Workday Student \(WDS\), but others must be requested from the Office of Student Academic Services \(OSAS\)\.

Proof of enrolment \(WDS\)

##### What is it?

A standard letter proving your enrolment in a given academic session\.

##### When do I need it?

-   to extend your study permit or apply for a temporary resident visa
-   to prove you are a full\-time student

##### [How to request your proof of enrolment on WDS](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/)

Note: This letter will reflect your current year standing\. If you need a letter with an estimated completion date, please refer to *Proof of enrolment with additional information \(OSAS\)*\.[https://workday\.students\.ubc\.ca/student\-documents/downloading\-your\-confirmation\-of\-enrolment\-letter/](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/)

Proof of enrolment with additional information \(OSAS\)

##### What is it?

A letter with detailed information about your academic enrolment, specifically your academic progress and expected completion date\. It may contain additional information—if requested—such as:

-   expected promotion to the next year level of the program \(month and year\)
-   registration in final credits/session before graduation

##### When do I need it?

-   to extend your study permit, apply for a new study permit after a break from studies, or apply for a temporary resident visa in non\-standard situations \(e\.g\., your studies are taking longer than expected, you took a break from studies due to health or personal reasons, military service, etc\.\)
-   to confirm your anticipated completion date

##### How do I request it?

Complete the request form\.

[Request form](https://sauder.jotform.com/team/ugo/requesting-documentation)  

Letters are issued within 5 business days to the email address listed on your WDS account\.

Program completion before your degree is conferred \(OSAS\)

##### What is it?

A letter confirming the successful completion of your program requirements once you have completed all of the required courses prior to your graduation application status updated to “Approved” or “Conferred\.”

Note: To check your graduation application status on the WDS, please review the ["Viewing your Graduation Application or Program Completion Status"](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/viewing-your-graduation-application-or-program-completion-status/#:~:text=Once%20in%20your%20Academics%20app,tab%20in%20the%20top%20menu.) guide\.

##### When do I need it?

-   to apply for post\-graduation work permit after you complete your program
-   to prove to a prospective employer that you have successfully completed your degree requirements

##### How do I request it?

Complete the request form\.

[Request form](https://sauder.jotform.com/team/ugo/requesting-documentation)  

Letters are issued within 5 business days to the email address listed on your WDS account\.

Program completion after your degree is conferred \(WDS\)

##### What is it?

A standard letter automatically generated to confirm the completion of your program requirements once your graduation application status on the WDS has been updated to “Conferred\.”

When do I need it?

-   to confirm you have completed your degree program

Note: If you are applying for your post\-graduation work permit before your graduation ceremony, please refer to *Program completion before your degree is conferred \(OSAS\)*\.

##### [How to request your program completion letter on WDS](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-program-completion-letter/)

[https://workday\.students\.ubc\.ca/student\-documents/downloading\-your\-program\-completion\-letter/](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-program-completion-letter/)

Request for authorized leave for international undergraduate students \(OSAS\)

##### What is it?

A letter requesting authorized leave for continuing UBC international undergraduate students to show they have formally requested and have been approved to take time away from their studies\. International undergraduate students can use this letter for immigration purposes such as maintaining the conditions of their study permit and eligibility for the post\-graduation work permit program\. This option is for continuing international students in good academic standing who withdraw from all their courses during Winter Term 1, Term 2 or both terms\. 

##### Who is eligible?

Students shall be eligible to be considered for an international undergraduate student leave who are:

-   International students according to the UBC Academic Calendar,
-   Eligible to register in the term\(s\) to which the leave applies,
-   Enrolled in a program which allows leaves under the Academic Leave Policy\.
-   Enrolled in a diploma, certificate or degree program to which graduate student leave policies do not apply and
-   Requesting such a leave\. Students may request such a leave on or before the last day to drop without a W standing \(without a W\); or on or before the last day to drop with a W standing \(with a W\)\. Late withdrawals are not in scope for this procedure\.

International student immigration policy allows students who take breaks from studies to retain certain privileges, including eligibility for the post\-graduation work permit and a possible future in Canada, but only if their institution grants them an authorized leave\.

##### How do I request it?

1.  Consider carefully whether you will take Term 1, Term 2 or both terms away from studies\*\. Check your **[program requirements](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/1792)**, tuition refund deadlines and any **[immigration implications](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international)** thoroughly\.
2.  It is strongly encouraged that you talk to an academic advisor before withdrawing from your courses\. Book an online advising appointment at **[mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/ugo\#bookadvising](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/ugo#bookadvising)** or visit our **[virtual office](https://bit.ly/3u8j6Hh)**\.
3.  Withdraw from all courses in Term 1, Term 2 or both terms on or before the **[last day to drop courses with a “W](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?page=deadlines)”** standing\.
4.  After you withdraw from all courses in Term 1, Term 2 or both terms, complete the request form below\.

[Request form](https://sauder.jotform.com/team/ugo/requesting-documentation)  

Letters are issued within 5 business days to the email address listed on your SSC account\. The leave will not appear on your transcript\. Include the authorized leave letter with future IRCC applications as needed\.

\* If you will be on leave for more than 150 days and will be in Canada during your leave, carefully review your **[study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/study-permits)** and **[post\-graduation work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit)** obligations\. For more information, please read **[students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/taking\-time\-away\-school\-international](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international)** and the **[FAQs for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-immigration-health-insurance-faq-covid-19#leave-of-absence)**\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/letters)

### How do I order an official transcript?

You can request copies of your transcript for a fee through the Student Service Centre or in person at Enrolment Services in Brock Hall\. Additional options are available for same day pick\-up, electronic transfer, and shipping by courier\.

[Learn more about costs and processing times](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript)

title: COMM_V 324 - People Analytics (formerly COMM 386H)
content_markdown:
This course introduces students to analytics and data management in the Human Resources \(HR\) field\. Given the increasing significance of and the interest in data\-driven decision\-making in organizations, this hands\-on course will equip students with the analytical skills to understand, evaluate, and address strategic HR/People decisions\. As such, students will learn how to apply descriptive statistics and the statistical inference to decisions in core HR areas, including recruitment, selection, compensation, training, and performance management using organizations’ HR data and human capital metrics collected from employee surveys\. Students will use data and statistical tools to evaluate and make recommendations for HR policies and practices, while connecting these analyses to the business strategies and goals\.

### Learning objectives

Upon completing this course, students will be able to:

-   identify relevant data and metrics appropriate for solving HR problems and making informed decisions in the field of HRM\.
-   utilize R to manage and prepare large personnel and employee datasets for statistical analysis\.
-   apply statistical analysis to contextualize and inform HR solutions\.
-   identify and evaluate the limitations of data analysis towards ensuring responsible decision\-making\.
-   accurately interpret and effectively communicate HR analytic results so they can be used in actionable decisions\.
-   explain the basics of Machine Learning and its applications in HRM \(Human Resources Management\)\.
-   assess the advantages and disadvantages of AI and Machine Learning in HR decisions\.

Note: Formerly numbered COMM 386H and titled HR Analytics: Data Metrics for HR Professionals\. If you've completed the course as COMM 386H, you are not permitted to take it again as COMM 324 \(you cannot receive credit for the same course twice\)\.

Prerequisite: All of [COMM 191](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/5220) \(formerly numbered as COMM 291\), [COMM 203](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-203), and [COMM 205](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-205)\.

    ###### \[3\] Approval to take Law courses is at the discretion of the Peter A\. Allard School of Law and subject to your academic readiness and available space in courses\. See below for instructions on how to request registration\.

### Taking LAW courses offered by the Peter A\. Allard School of Law

Courses offered by the Allard School of Law are academically rigorous\. They will require you to devote significant time and effort to do well\. Be aware that your performance in these courses can impact a future application to law school and your ability to secure related employment opportunities\. 

Completion of a Law course cannot be applied toward any future Allard Law degree \(i\.e\., credits cannot be double counted\)\.

#### Law course schedule

Law courses at UBC are administered by the Peter A\. Allard School of Law\. Courses and timetables offered for 2024/25 are posted on the **[Allard Law website](http://www.allard.ubc.ca/student-resources/jd-academic-services/registration-advising-exams/courses-exams)**\. 

#### Law course availability and request process

Juris Doctor \(law\) students will register for most of their courses during the first two weeks of July\. LAW\_V 459, LAW\_V 316, and LAW\_V 334 are popular among law students\. Only after law students have registered will students in other programs be considered for any remaining seats, if any\. 

To request registration you must complete and return to Allard Law a **[Permission for a Non\-Law Student to Register in a Law Course](https://allard.ubc.ca/student-portal/policies-procedures-and-forms)** according to the instructions in the form and by the deadlines for each term as specified\.

The form must also be signed by an academic advisor in OSAS before you submit it to Allard Law\. Advisors will only approve forms for students in Year 3 or above\.

With the form you are required to attach a separate page on which you briefly indicate \(i\) your reasons for taking the course and \(ii\) why you feel academically prepared to take the course\. By completing and submitting this form, you are allowing UBC Law to access your UBC academic record\.

The Law Associate Dean, Academic Affairs, will review all requests after the submission deadline\. If your request is approved, Allard Academic Services staff will register you in the LAW course\(s\) and notify you by email on the first day of the term in which the class will be held\.

#### Law course examinations and grading rules

BCom students are subject to the same **[Allard Law Examination and Grading rules](https://allard.ubc.ca/student-portal/policies-procedures-and-forms)** as law students\.

Allard Law Academic Services internally schedules and manages all Allard Law examinations\. Because law exams are not scheduled by Enrolment Services, they will not be published with your other final exams\. The Law December and April exam schedules will be posted on the [Allard website](http://www.allard.ubc.ca/student-resources/jd-academic-services/registration-advising-exams/courses-exams) well before Enrolment Services schedules exams for other courses\. **If you have an exam conflict with a Law course and a non\-Law course, you are expected to write the Law exam as scheduled**\. You must make arrangements to write the non\-Law course exam at another time\. If you have a conflict, please report it to the **[Office of Student Academic Services](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/1888)**  immediately so that we can assist you with alternate exam arrangements\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/business-law-concentration)

### Will the Business Law concentration appear on my transcript?

Yes\! Successful completion of the Business Law concentration will be noted on your transcript after graduation\.

title: UBC Sauder Hiring Data: Job IQ Explorer
content_markdown:
### Explore real UBC Sauder hiring outcomes to guide your career planning

**Discover where UBC Sauder students land opportunities and how they got there\.**

**Job IQ Explorer** in the **UBC Sauder Career Hub** gives you exclusive access to real, anonymous hiring data from UBC Sauder students and recent alumni\. Explore employers, salary ranges, hiring trends, offer timing, and more to make informed career decisions\. 

[Access Job IQ Explorer](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/job-analytics/post-graduation) 

##### *\(CWL login required\)*

### Why use Job IQ Explorer? 

**Use real UBC Sauder hiring data to help guide your career planning and job search\.** 

-   **Explore employers****:** See which organizations hire UBC Sauder students and graduates
-   **Compare salaries****:** View salary ranges by employer, role, industry, and location
-   **Plan your job search****:** See when students typically receive offers
-   **Discover job search strategies****:** Learn which activities and resources helped students secure opportunities
-   **Explore career paths****:** Discover employment trends across different industries, degrees, and graduation years

> ## Career & Personal Exploration
> 
> -   [Personal Development Resources](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-resources/personal-development-resources)
> -   [Career Exploration Resources](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-personal-exploration/career-exploration-resources)
> -   [What Can I Do With My Degree?](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/what-can-i-do-with-my-degree)
> -   [UBC Sauder Hiring Data](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-resources/seat)
> -   [Navigate Your Career Journey](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/my-unique-career-journey)
> -   [Graduate Studies](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-options/graduate-studies)

### See where the BCom Class of 2025 landed jobs\!

[Click to download the full infographic](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/6858/download?token=d1pBx5oR)

### How to access Job IQ Explorer

1.  Log in to the **UBC Sauder Career Hub** using your CWL\.
2.  Select **Job IQ Explorer** from the left navigation menu\.
3.  Select **Internship** or **Post Graduation** to explore the corresponding data\.

[Access Job IQ Explorer](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/job-analytics/post-graduation)

*\(CWL login required\)*

[Image](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/job_iq_explorer_homepage_for_promo.jpg?itok=kv4QPAdM)

### What can you explore?

Job IQ Explorer includes several interactive dashboard tiles that allow you to dig into internship and post\-graduation data by program, industry, function, employer, grad year, and more\.

By default, you’ll see UBC Sauder data only, but you can adjust the filters to also explore employment outcomes from participating Canadian, U\.S\., and European business schools\.

**Job IQ Explorer Tiles:**

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Hires by Location \(Map\)** | See where UBC Sauder students and alumni are working across Canada and around the world using an interactive hiring map\. |
| **Job Details** | Select the different tabs in the tile to explore **Hires or Base Salary** by: **Industry, Function, Employer, Location\.** |
| **Compensation Summary** | Adjust the filters at the top of the dashboard to explore different aspects of compensation, including: **Base Salary, Signing Bonus, Guaranteed Bonus\.** |
| **Offer Timing** | See which **months** students typically receive their internship, and full\-time **job offers** to help plan your job search\. |
| **Offer Trends** | Explore **Hires and Compensation** trends to see how hiring and pay evolve **year over year\.** |
| **Job Source** | See how most students found their opportunities, including job boards, networking, and events\. |

> ### Want more instructions?
> 
> Review the "[**Career Hub Guide**](https://bit.ly/careerhubguide)" for more tips\.
> 
> ### Want help interpreting the data? 
> 
> Not sure how to use the information in Job IQ Explorer to guide your own career planning? Book a **[career coaching & advising](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching)** appointment on the Career Hub for personalized 1:1 support\. 
> 
> [Book on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments/)
> 
> \(*CWL login required\)*

### Where does the data come from?

Job IQ Explorer uses anonymous internship and post\-graduation employment outcomes shared by UBC Sauder students and recent alumni through the Career Hub’s **Internship and Post\-Sauder questionnaires\.**

The database includes outcomes from undergraduate and graduate students, across UBC Sauder’s programs, including: BCom, MBA, Master of Management \(MM\), Master of Business Analytics \(MBAN\)\.

To protect students' and graduates' privacy, all information is kept confidential and only reported in anonymous and aggregate form\. Results may not appear when there aren’t enough responses for specific attributes\.

### Help grow Job IQ Explorer

Every internship and **post\-graduation outcome** shared in the Career Hub helps improve the **Job IQ Explorer** for future UBC Sauder students\.

Throughout your degree, you'll be invited to report your:

-   Internship/Co\-op experiences
-   Post\-Sauder plans \(within 6 months of finishing your program\)

You can update your information at any time as your plans change\.

**Report your Internship/Co\-op or Post\-Sauder plans:**

1.  Log in to the **Career Hub**\.
2.  On your homepage, scroll to locate the **Jobs and Job Offers** tile\.
3.  Select **\+ Report Status**\.
4.  Complete the applicable short questionnaire\.

[Report now on the Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/)

*\(CWL login required\)*

### Hiring Data FAQs:

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    1\. ***How is my privacy protected?***
    
     All responses submitted through the Internship/Co\-op and Post\-Sauder questionnaires are kept confidential and reported only in anonymous, aggregate form to protect your privacy\.

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    2\. **Why does UBC Sauder collect this information?** 
    
    **Your responses help:**
    
    -   Power Job IQ Explorer with real UBC Sauder employment outcomes 
        
    
    -   Support current and future students with career planning 
        
    
    -   Contribute towards the School’s accreditation: The UBC Sauder School of Business is required to collect employment information from every graduating student in accordance with our **[AACSB](https://www.aacsb.edu/)** \(Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business\) accreditation\. These accreditations are very important for the School and for our global reputation\. The Business Career Centre reports this data at an aggregate level\. 
        
    
    -   Inform the Business Career Centre’s programming and services 
        
    
    -   Inform prospective students about the UBC BCom program via promotional materials that use aggregate hiring data

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    3\. **Will someone contact me after I report?**
    
    If you report your status as "**Seeking Employment"** in the Post\-Sauder questionnaire, a Career Strategist may contact you via email to offer job search support\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    (empty)

### Questions? 

Contact ***[careercentre@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:careercentre@sauder.ubc.ca)*** for support with the Career Hub or Job IQ Explorer\.

#### **Did you know?**

According to the [**Economist Intelligence Unit’s \(EIU\)**](https://www.vancouverisawesome.com/local-news/vancouver-ranks-fifth-globally-on-major-livability-index-7181622) 2023 Global Liveability Index on the most livable major cities in the world, **Vancouver ranks \#5** while **Toronto ranks \#9**\.

**Option\-specific Insights**  

-   Most Canadian **consulting** and **finance** opportunities are in Toronto, which is Canada’s largest financial hub
    
-   Most **new grad leadership programs in business analytics** take place outside of B\.C\., mainly in Toronto—however, there are opportunities in Vancouver
    
-   According to CPABC, it's estimated that by 2029 BC will create almost 40,000 new **accounting** jobs
    
-   Due to the cost of living and availability of talent, **marketing** salaries can vary between cities in Canada\. Generally, adjust average base salaries as follows:

-   Vancouver: \+3%
-   Toronto: \+3\.2%

### International Students Working in Canada

If you’re an international student, whether or not you intend on staying in Canada after graduation, getting work experience in Canada can help you advance your career\.

Attending [**Launch Your Career in Canada**](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/launch-career-canada#:~:text=Launch%20Your%20Career%20in%20Canada%20is%20UBC%27s%20annual%20networking%20experience,alumni%20and%20industry%20professionals%20alike.) is a great starting point while you are at UBC\. This annual networking experience, open only to UBC international students, is dedicated to supporting their career development\. Launch Your Career in Canada provides an opportunity to hear from and connect with alumni and industry professionals each year\.  

#### **Work Permits**

As an international student, you can do several types of work in Canada, including on and off\-campus employment, Co\-op work terms, and jobs after graduation\. Some require specific work permits

Refer to [**UBC Student Services' Working in Canada**](https://students.ubc.ca/career/working-canada) page for information about the different work permits required to work in Canada and additional related information\. You can also get more information from the [**Government of Canada's Immigration and Citizenship website**](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/immigration-citizenship.html)\.

#### **Questions?**

Connect with [**International Student Advising**](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/international-student-advising) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

### Working Abroad

[working abroad\-pexels\-aksonsat\-uanthoeng](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/working_abroad-pexels-aksonsat-uanthoeng-1078850.jpg?itok=rQqAfP59)

Working abroad builds **independence, initiative, and adaptability** – important traits employers always value\.

An international work placement will help you get work experience directly related to your field\. It will also enhance your global perspective and professional network\.

#### **Eligibility & documentation requirements**

Most intentional positions require at least a bachelor's degree, but there are still many options if you haven’t completed your studies\.

**Research the required documents and conditions to work in foreign jurisdictions before applying**\. For example, if you want to work in France, you should know that all Co\-op work terms and internships require a “convention de stage,” which is currently not a document that UBC Sauder provides students\.

If you want to work abroad, you’ll need to apply for a work permit from the country where you want to work\. This can take time to organize, so plan\. Contact the appropriate embassy or consulate to find out what’s required\. If you have dual citizenship \(e\.g\., a parent or grandparent born in your destination country\), contact the embassy and begin the paperwork as early as possible\.  
  
[**SWAP**](https://swap.ca/) is an excellent resource if you want to pay for help arranging visas and/or locating work overseas\.

####   
**Resources**

-   **UBC Sauder Alumni:** Tap into our global network of over 37,000 accomplished business professionals in 75 countries\. Find UBC Sauder alumni on **[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/school/ubcsauder/people/)**
-   **[Government of Canada: Living Abroad](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/living-abroad):** Everything you need to know how to prepare to leave Canada to live in a foreign country\.
-   **International Youth Programs**: Travel the world and earn money\! The Government of Canada has negotiated reciprocal temporary work permits with nearly 40 countries for Canadians between the ages of 18 and 35\. **Check out** TransitionsAbroad\.com for a helpful [**Student Internship and Work Abroad Checklist  
    **](https://www.transitionsabroad.com/listings/work/internships/articles/shorttermworkabroadchecklist.shtml)

#### **International job postings**

-   [**OverseasJobs**](https://www.overseasjobs.com/): features overseas jobs and international employment opportunities for professionals, expatriates, and adventure seekers
-   [**Jobaroo**](https://www.jobaroo.com/) \(Australia\): for working holidays and sponsored professionals

**Remember, before making your career move, do your research\!**  
  
Explore [**Job IQ Explorer**](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/ubc-sauder-alumni-job-data) for UBC Sauder new grad job data—find data on salaries, employment locations worldwide, employers hiring grads, and more\!  
  
You can also check out [**Numbeo**](https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/) for a better gauge of how your current cost of living compares to where you’d like to move\.

title: Career Coaching & Advising
content_markdown:
[Students with laptop](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/level_1-_career_coaching_advising.jpg?itok=PI1OPnJT)

At UBC Sauder, **you don't have to navigate your career alone**\.

The Hari B\. Varshney Business Career Centre \(BCC\) offers a range of coaching and advising options, whether you're feeling stuck and unsure, or know exactly what you want to do\.

### What is career coaching & advising?

Career coaching & advising involves talking with Career Strategists and/or trained Peer Career Advisors about different aspects of your career journey\.

You’re in charge\! These conversations are for and about you and can dive into any career\-related topic you want support with, including:

-   Job application reviews
-   Career exploration
-   Job search strategies
-   Feeling stuck \(see a Career Strategist for these conversations\)

### Who can you meet with?

In 1st year, meet with Peer Career Advisors at Drop\-in or book 1:1 appointments through [**UBC Sauder Career Hub**](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments)\. Beginning in 2nd year, you can also book appointments directly with Career Strategists\.

Registered Co\-op students have access to a team of knowledgeable Co\-op Career Strategists to help guide them throughout their Co\-op experience\.

### [BCom Career Strategists](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/bcom-career-managers)

[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/career\-experience/career\-coaching/bcom\-career\-managers](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/bcom-career-managers)

[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/career\-experience/career\-coaching/bcom\-career\-managers](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/bcom-career-managers)[Image](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/slide-small/public/general/career_manager_stock_photo.jpg?itok=mHEhY1aL&timestamp=1685741210)

1:1 personalized career support to help you thrive and land the job you want\.

[LEARN MORE](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/bcom-career-managers)

### [Peer Career Advisors](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/career-peer-advisors)

Drop in or book coaching appointments with senior BComs who have been in your position\.

[LEARN MORE](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/career-peer-advisors)

### [Co\-op Career Strategists](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/co-op-managers)

[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/career\-experience/career\-coaching/co\-op\-managers](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/co-op-managers)

[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/career\-experience/career\-coaching/co\-op\-managers](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/co-op-managers)[Co\-op Manager](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/slide-small/public/images/teaser-widget/co-op_manager_stock_photo.jpg?itok=g2gcMZuH&timestamp=1685991769)

Dedicated career support for students registered in the Co\-op program\.

[LEARN MORE](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/co-op-managers)

### What topics do students usually talk about?

BComs most commonly book appointments for

-   **Job Application Review**: get guidance on your resume and cover letter
-   **Career Exploration/Navigation**: learn tactics to discover jobs, industries, and employers that align with your interests and goals
-   **Job Search Strategies**: find advice on how you get started and find meaningful work experience opportunities
-   **I’m Feeling Stuck**: share what’s making you feel stuck, and we’ll help you create a path forward
-   **Interview Prep & Strategies**: practice answering interview questions and get tips for success

Find a complete list of coaching & advising appointment types on [**UBC Sauder Career Hub**](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments)\.

### How long are coaching & advising appointments?

You can book 15, 30, and 45\-minute appointments—depending on your program and your topic\.

### Where are appointments held?

**Virtual**: Zoom—you will be emailed a Zoom link ahead of your appointment

**In\-Person with BCom Career Strategists/Co\-op Career Strategist**: In the BCC \(HA 155\)

**In\-Person with Peer Career Advisors**: They will be back in September 2026\.

### How to book an appointment?

1.  Log in to the UBC Sauder Career Hub using your CWL 
2.  Select **Appointments** from the left navigation menu 
3.  Filters appointments by **location, Career Advisor\***, or **appointment type** 
4.  Select an available time under a Career Advisor's name, then choose **View Available Slots** 
5.  Enter your appointment details and select either **virtual** or **in\-person** location type 
6.  Select **Book Appointment** 

\*Career Strategists are labelled Career Advisors in the Career Hub\.

[Log into UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments) 

Need help to find an appointment or have questions? Contact the BCC at 604\.822\.6479 or [**careercentre@sauder\.ubc\.ca**](mailto:careercentre@sauder.ubc.ca)\. If you're calling from out of town, our toll\-free number is 1\.877\.777\.6479\.

### Navigate Your Career Journey

Trying to figure out what type of work interests you? Or maybe you're wondering what resources can help you achieve your goals? No matters where you are in your unique career journey, you can use our career development model to help navigate your personal and professional goals at UBC Sauder and beyond\.

title: BCom Career Strategists
content_markdown:
### What's next? We're here to help you find the answers

Through the Hari B\. Varshney Business Career Centre \(BCC\), all UBC Sauder BCom students have access to a team of **dedicated and knowledgeable Career Strategists**\.

This team offers a variety of coaching and advising appointments you can book to **get personalized, 1:1 support**\.

Your Career Strategists will work alongside you throughout your degree to help you take action and thrive in both your personal and professional life\.

### Talk to a Career Strategist About:

-   **Job Application Review**: get guidance on your resume and cover letter, including tips on how to tailor your resume for specific roles and how to craft accomplishment statements
-   **Career Exploration/Navigation**: get support and learn tactics to find out the types of jobs, industries, and employers that align with your interests and goals
-   **Job Search Strategies**: find advice on where to get started and how to find meaningful work experience opportunities
-   **I'm Feeling Stuck**: share what's making you feel stuck, and we'll help you create a path forward
-   **Interviewing Prep & Strategies**: practice answering questions and get tips for succes

Find a complete list of coaching & advising appointment types on **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments)**\.

### Meet your BCom Career Strategists\!

> ## Career Coaching & Advising
> 
> -   [BCom Career Strategists](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/bcom-career-strategists)
> -   [Peer Career Advisors](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/peer-career-advisors)

Career Strategist, BCom Careers

[david\.edwards@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:david.edwards@sauder.ubc.ca)

##### **About David:** I graduated from the University of Victoria with a BSc in Geoscience, before working in mining exploration, aerial survey, IT, and satellite imagery\. I went on to complete my MA in Counselling Psychology here at UBC, where my research focus was in employment transitions and the changing context of work\.

##### **Best piece of career advice David ever received:** Follow your heart, but don’t forget your head\.

##### **Fun fact:** I’ve spent a lot of time living in a tent in the Yukon\.  
**Let's chat about:** BTM, BUCS, Accounting, Consulting, and Entrepreneurship\.

### Jesse Grimaldi \(He, Him, His\)

Career Strategist, BCom Careers

[jesse\.grimaldi@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:jesse.grimaldi@sauder.ubc.ca)

##### **About Jesse:** I graduated from Queen’s University with an MA in Sociology\. After exploring different career options, I began working as a recruiter, where I discovered my passion for giving back to students supporting their job pursuits and career development\.  My professional background spans working in public, semi\-public, private, and non\-profit sectors\. 

##### **Best piece of career advice Jesse ever received:** “Success is liking yourself, liking what you do, and liking how you do it\." – Maya Angelou

##### **Fun fact:** My first career goal was playing in the NBA\. Spoiler alert: it didn’t quite work out  
  
**Let's chat about:** Accounting, Marketing, Operations & Logistics, Human Resources, and Graduate school

### Misa Zhang \(She, Her, Hers\)

Career Strategist, BCom Careers

[misa\.zhang@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:misa.zhang@sauder.ubc.ca)

##### **About Misa:** I have a background in education with experience supporting diverse student groups, including international students\. I previously worked for two U\.S\. universities, mainly supporting business and computer science students' career development\.

##### In my role at the BCC, I'll focus on supporting students to explore career opportunities in finance and will lead the **[Finance Mentorship Program \(FMP\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/mentorship-specialty-programs/finance-mentorship-program)** and [**Financial Modelling & Interview Prep Program \(FMIPP\)**\.](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/mentorship-specialty-programs/financial-modelling-and-interview-prep-program)

##### **Best piece of career advice Misa ever received:** Sometimes “no” only means “not now”\. Rejection can be transformed into redirection\.

##### **Fun fact:** I have visited all 12 Disney Parks in the world\.

##### **Let’s chat about**: Finance, Financial Designations, FMP, FMIPP

### Michael Clarke \(He, Him, His\)

Associate Director, BCom Careers & Work Integrated Learning

[michael\.clarke@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:michael.clarke@sauder.ubc.ca)

##### **About Michael:** I joined the Sauder School of Business in September 2015, bringing over 10 years of experience in facilitating and coordinating career exploration and job search programs\. I continue to look for ways to empower individuals in their choices while they are looking to explore their options, transition into opportunities, and succeed in chosen career paths\.

##### **Best piece of career advice Michael ever received:** First, find a place that likes you for who you are\! Secondly, understand that regardless of your career path, you must prepare yourself to deal with ambiguity, uncertainty, and change\. 

##### **Fun fact:** For over two years I had the opportunity to travel the world while working on cruise ships\!  
  
**Let's chat about:** Accounting, BTM, Marketing, Entrepreneurship, Finance, General Business Management, Operations & Logistics, OBHR, and Real Estate\.

### How do you book an appointment with a BCom Career Strategist?

To make a 1:1 appointment with a BCom Career Strategist, take the following steps:

1.  Log in to the UBC Sauder Career Hub using your CWL 
2.  Select **Appointments** from the left navigation menu 
3.  Filters appointments by **location, Career Advisor\*****,** or **appointment type** 
4.  Select an available time under a Career Advisor's name, then choose **View Available Slots** 
5.  Enter your appointment details and select either **virtual** or **in\-person** location type 
6.  Select Book Appointment \*Career Strategists are labelled Career Advisors in the Career Hub\. 

[Log in to Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments) 

### Questions?

If you have any issues making an appointment or have further questions, contact the Business Career Center at 604\.822\.6479 or **[careercentre@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:careercentre@sauder.ubc.ca)**\. If you're calling from out of town, our toll\-free number is 1\.877\.777\.6479\.

### How Career Strategists Help

"The Career \[Strategists\] at UBC Sauder provided me with the support and confidence I needed to kick\-start my career\. The one\-on\-one coaching appointments allowed for a tailored experience where they continuously worked alongside me to help tackle whatever career\-related obstacles I was facing\. With the support through follow ups, resources, and connections, I knew they cared about me both as a student and as a future business leader\." \- Cheryl Y\., OBHR Student
