Research support

Strengthen your work\! Take advantage of the highly resourceful information and professional research support from the David Lam Management Research Library, located in the Canaccord Learning Commons\. 

[Find research supports](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/get-better-grades/research-support)  

Generative AI and ChatGPT

Discover how generative AI creates text, images, and other content, as well as its limitations in understanding meaning and verifying facts\. This resource explores key evaluation strategies, including the SIFT and ROBOT tests, and highlights challenges like hallucinated citations and model collapse\. Find guidance from UBC Library and the Centre for Teaching, Learning and Technology on using generative AI responsibly\. 

Please review **[the UBC Sauder Artificial Intelligence Policy](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/media/ai_policy_at_ubc_sauder_.pdf)** before using AI for academic purposes\.

[Learn more](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/EvaluatingSources/GenerativeAI#s-lg-box-16711531)  

Academic integrity

Academic integrity means that you are honest and accountable in your work as a scholar\. Understand plagiarism and how you can avoid it by learning about student integrity and ethics\.

[Learn more about academic integrity](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/resource-guides/understand-academic-integrity/)  

Additional resources:

-   [UBC Academic Integrity website](https://academicintegrity.ubc.ca/student-start/)

Additional reading:

-   [UBC Life blog: Academic integrity](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/academic-integrity)

### Exams

Exam preparation

Tests and exams will always be a hurdle you'll encounter as a student\. Know how to prepare well in advance and gain confidence in test\-writing by visiting the Exam Toolkit below\.

[Access the Preparing for Exams Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/preparing-for-exams/)  

Additional reading:

-   [UBC Chapman Learning Commons: Expert Tips to Ace Your Exams](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/expert-tips-to-ace-exams/)
-   [UBC Life blog: Your exam season resource guide](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/exam-season-resource-guide)
-   [UBC Life blog: What to expect for your first finals season](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/what-expect-first-finals-season)
-   [UBC Science Distillation blog: How to Deal with Final Exams](https://science.ubc.ca/students/blog/final-exams-how-to-deal?utm_source=Website&utm_medium=timely&utm_campaign=2022)
-   [UBC Science Distillation blog: Making a Final Exam Study Plan, Step by Step](https://science.ubc.ca/students/blog/making-final-exam-study-plan-step-step)

[https://science\.ubc\.ca/students/blog/making\-final\-exam\-study\-plan\-step\-step](https://science.ubc.ca/students/blog/making-final-exam-study-plan-step-step)

[Types of exams](https://science.ubc.ca/students/blog/making-final-exam-study-plan-step-step)

There are many different types of exams and you're more than likely to encounter multiple choice tests and essay\-based exams\. Know how to tackle these types of exams and successfully answer these types of questions:

-   [UBC Life blog: How to tackle essay\-based exams](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/tackle-essay-based-exams)
-   [UBC Life blog: How to tackle multiple choice based exam](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/tackle-multiple-choice-tests)

Although, these two types of exams or a mix of the two are popular with instructors, you could also encounter exams with questions that require answers in the following responses: true/false, fill in the blanks, quantitive or problem solving, or short answers\. Exams can also be online, oral, open book, or take home\. Instructors may also develop an exam in a format not listed above\. In any case, try to give yourself enough time to study the materials and get a good night's sleep the day before so that you are prepared for any questions that may come your way\.

Additional reading

-   [UBC Chapman Learning Commons: Strategic Test Taking and Preparation](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/zorah-bp/)
-   [https://learningcommons\.ubc\.ca/zorah\-bp/](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/zorah-bp/)[UBC Life blog: What to do when you're stumped on an exam](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/what-do-when-youre-stumped-exam)

### Time and self\-management

Time management

Wasting a lot of time online? Pulling too many all\-nighters? Time management is key to achieving all your goals whilst finding time for yourself, which is especially important as a university student\. Learn how you can manage your time effectively and learn about the different methods you can adopt to make the most out of your time\.

[Access the Managing Your Time Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/managing-your-time/)   

Additional reading:

-   [UBC Life blog: Pinpointing and perfecting your productivity zone](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/pinpointing-perfecting-productivity-zone)
-   [UBC Science Distillation blog: 80/20 \- How to Increase Your Productivity by Doing Less](https://science.ubc.ca/students/blog/how-to-increase-your-productivity-by-doing-less)

Concentration and focus

Believe it or not, finding focus is a skill that one can improve on\. It's easy to get distracted, especially with everything that goes on in a student's life\. Learn how you can avoid these distractions and settle yourself into a rhythm of focus, so that you can study, absorb material, and perform better in school\.

[Learn about strategies to help you focus better](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/cultivating-the-ability-to-focus/)  

Motivation

Wondering how to build motivation and discipline throughout the school year? Check out this resource guide for tips and helpful resources to stay on track\!

[Read the Motivation Guide](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/resource-guides/motivation-resource-guide/)   

Additional reading

-   [UBC Science Distillation blog: Struggling to Find the Motivation?](https://science.ubc.ca/students/blog/struggling-find-motivation)

Procrastination

It's easy to fall off track and get stuck in a pattern of procrastination\. To avoid the stress and anxiety that follows, here are some strategies to help get you started and trick yourself into taking action\! Below are some of the best practices you can try out:

-   Pomodoro technique: do uninterrupted work for 25 minutes, take a 5 minute break, then repeat 3 times and take a longer 20 minute break
-   5 minutes: You can do almost anything for 5 minutes\. Start an assignment, start reading a chapter, review your lecture notes, etc\. You’ll find that after 5 minutes, you either want to keep plugging away at it, you’re almost done whatever you set out to do, or you’re really not into it\. But at least you took action for those 5 minutes\.
-   Sounds silly, but put your phone somewhere you can’t get to it: give it to your neighbour in residence, charge it across the room, or turn it off so it’s more challenging to check it\. At least keep it out of arm’s reach\.

[View strategies to help with procrastination](https://academicservices.engineering.ubc.ca/2021/03/11/procrastination-why-do-we-do-it-and-what-can-we-do-to-stop/)  

Additional reading:

-   [UBC Life blog: A chronic procrastinator's guide to independent projects](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/chronic-procrastinators-guide-independent-projects)
-   [UBC Life blog: Procrastination: It's not what you think it is](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/procrastination-its-not-what-you-think-it)

Sleep

In order to perform at your best in university, it's important you take care of yourself and how you sleep\. Despite how easy it is to stay up late to study or do homework, you should set aside time for your brain to process the information you're learning\. Access the Sleep and Academic Success Toolkit by the Chapman Learning Commons, a 3\-video series on how you can apply techniques to improve your sleep and studies\.

[Access the Sleep and Academic Success Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/sleep-and-academic-success/)  

Additional reading:

-   [UBC Life blog: How to get your sleep schedule back on track—now](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/sleep-schedule-back-tracknow)

Stress

Stress is a normal part of the human experience\. However, everyone experiences stress differently and stressors are unique to each person\. Find information on recognizing signs of stress, managing the stress response, and understanding different types of stressors\.

[Learn about strategies on how to manage stress](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/understanding-stress)  

Additional reading:

-   [UBC Life blog: Quick ways to de\-stress this exam season](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/quick-ways-de-stress-exam-season)
-   [UBC Life blog: Turn panic into power: How to use stress to your advantage](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/turn-panic-power-use-stress-advantage)
-   [UBC Life blog: Navigating burnout in my last term at UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/navigating-burnout-my-last-term-ubc)
-   [UBC Life blog: Stress: What it really is and how to handle it](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/stress-what-it-really-handle-it)
-   [UBC SVPRO: Grounding exercises booklet](http://scs-svpro-2021.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2021/09/Grounding-Exercises-V.02-01_10_21.pdf)

### Assignments and class participation

Group projects

Working with groups can be stressful\-\-and rewarding\! We’ll show you how to make the most of any project\.

[Learn more about working in groups](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/working-in-groups/)  

Additional reading:

-   [UBC Life blog: How to survive group projects as an introvert](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/survive-group-projects-introvert)
-   [UBC Life blog: 4 tactics to get to great ideas in group projects](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/4-tactics-great-ideas-group-projects)
-   [https://students\.ubc\.ca/ubclife/4\-tactics\-great\-ideas\-group\-projects](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/4-tactics-great-ideas-group-projects)[UBC Science Distillation blog: Tips for starting a successful study group](https://science.ubc.ca/students/blog/study-groups)

Presentations

Nothing causes anxiety in students quite like presenting\. Throughout your university journey and beyond, you'll be faced with tasks that require you to give a presentation, whether that's a quick elevator pitch or lengthy speech\. Learn how you can deliver effective presentations and successfully communicate your message to your audience with the Presentation Skills Toolkit:

[Access the Presentation Skills Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/presentation-skills/)  

Additional resources:

-   [Presentation coaching for COMM 395](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/get-better-grades/presentation-coaching)

Addtional reading:

-   [UBC Life blog: How to develop & deliver a riveting presentation](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/develop-deliver-riveting-presentation)

Participation

At UBC Sauder, participation is a key component to almost all of your courses and can really make the difference when it comes to your final grade\. Find out some tips on how to find your voice and make the most out of your classroom experience\.

[Read the blog post on how to improve class participation](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/finding-voice-classroom)  

### Being a university student

Transition to university

Transitioning to university can be one of the biggest changes in someone's life and it's completely normal to get swept up in the emotions that come with it\. Especially for a first year or transfer student, the challenges you face may seem insurmountable and you'll be uncertain navigating your way through university, so just know you're not alone\! Read about what you should expect and some advice on your transition, from a fellow student\.

[Learn more about what to expect in university](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/what-you-may-feel-first-year-prep)  

Additional reading:

-   [UBC Student Services: Introduction to UBC classes](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes)
-   [CUS: First year survival guide](https://www.cus.ca/guides/)
-   [https://students\.ubc\.ca/ubclife/what\-you\-may\-feel\-first\-year\-prep](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/what-you-may-feel-first-year-prep)[UBC Life blog: What to expect from a university lecture](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/what-expect-university-lecture)
-   [https://students\.ubc\.ca/ubclife/what\-expect\-university\-lecture](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/what-expect-university-lecture)[UBC Life blog: What are university classes like?](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/what-are-university-classes)

Academic Essentials

Before you begin your first term at UBC Vancouver, prepare for your classes and the university learning experience by taking part in Academic Essentials\. These free online courses will help you develop the skills you’ll need to succeed at UBC and give you a solid academic foundation to build on in September, all at your own pace\.

[Register for Academic Essentials before arriving on campus](https://you.ubc.ca/academic-essentials/)  

Overcoming challenges

It's completely normal for a student to face learning challenges in university and what's important is learning how you can overcome them\. In this article, learn about the five most common challenges you may face as a student, from failing a course to keeping up with class, and what steps you can take to combat them\.

[Learn more about overcoming challenges](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/tutoring-and-advice/learning-challenges/)  

Do you know of any other academic resources and supports on campus that might be useful to BCom students? Let us know by emailing [bcomquestions@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:bcomquestions@sauder.ubc.ca)\. 

> ### [Math & Econ Coaching](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/get-better-grades/math-coaching)
> 
> 1:1 or small group appointments to help your comprehension of difficult topics in first\-year calculus and economics courses\.
> 
> [Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/get-better-grades/math-coaching)
> 
> ### [Study spaces](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/tutoring-studying/study-spaces/)
> 
> Looking for a study space on campus? Check out the link below for the best places to study on campus\.
> 
> [Find study spaces](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/tutoring-studying/study-spaces/)
> 
> ### [Peer Assisted Study Sessions \(PASS\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/get-better-grades/pass)
> 
> PASS is offered by the Canaccord Learning Commons \(CLC\) and are academic support sessions for students taking historically\-difficult courses\.
> 
> [Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/get-better-grades/pass)
> 
> ### [CMP review sessions/packages](https://www.facebook.com/ubccmp)
> 
> The Commerce Mentorship Program \(CMP\) offers midterm and final review sessions and packages for BCom students\. Courses they cover include COMM 190, COMM 204, COMM 205, COMM 293, COMM 295, COMM 393, ECON 101, and MATH 100\.
> 
> [View CMP's Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/ubccmp)

### UBC Student Life Blog

No one knows students better than other students\. Stay connected with students from other faculties and learn about the stories happening around you at UBC\. Visit the UBC Student Life blog for study tips, student experiences, and general lifehacks, written for students, by students\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife)

### Additional resources and supports

Determine who to contact if your situation is preventing you from completing your coursework\.

### [Equity & Inclusion Office](https://equity.ubc.ca/)

The Equity & Inclusion Office works with campus partners to create a university community in which human rights are respected and equity is embedded in all areas of academic, work and campus life\. The website also includes information about Human Rights advising and religious accommodations for students\.

[Learn more](https://equity.ubc.ca/)

### [Centre for Accessibiliy](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility)

Accessibility Advisors can help if you have a disability or ongoing medical condition that you think will impact your academics or any other aspect of university life\. Advisors can answer your accessibility questions and assess and facilitate accommodations to support all parts of your academic life, including exams, assignments, and classroom access\. Appointments are available in person, over Zoom, and on the phone\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility)

### [UBC Counselling Services](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/mental-health-and-wellbeing)

If you're feeling persistently stressed, anxious, or sad, you can book a virtual, phone or in\-person initial or follow\-up appointment with UBC Sauder Counselling Services\.

[Learn more](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/mental-health-and-wellbeing)

> ### [Health and wellness supports](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/support)
> 
> Positive mental health and wellbeing are important to your academic success\. Find resources and supports to help you thrive\.
> 
> [Access resources and supports](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/support)
> 
> ### [Indigenous student resources](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/indigenous-student-resources)
> 
> If you're an Indigenous BCom student, there are resources available that can enhance your experience through exclusive programs, awards, and learning spaces\.
> 
> [Find Indigenous student resources](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/indigenous-student-resources)

### Submitting a petition for academic concession

If you feel that a specific circumstance is affecting your studies and health, you may be eligible to submit a petition for academic concession\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/academic-concession)

title: COMM_V 490A - Directed Studies
content_markdown:
An investigation and report on a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and a senior student\. Directed Studies allow you to receive course credit for an independent study/project completed under the supervision of a Faculty member\. Once you have found a professor who has agreed to supervise your project, download the Directed Studies form at [mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/files/directed\-studies\-form](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/comm_490_directed_studies_application_form.pdf)\.

The BCom Capstone is an event to help 4th year students integrate learnings from the BCom degree and connect with a diverse group of alumni\. Hear real\-life experiences and gain insights on how your degree fits into the larger picture of your first 3\-5 years after graduation\.

title: COMM_V 451 - Climate-Focused ESG Reporting and Analysis (formerly COMM 486E)
content_markdown:
Course Description

This course will provide students with the background to understand the importance of ESG reporting to investors and other stakeholders\. Environmental, Social, and Governance factors will be considered, but the main focus is on climate\. Topics covered will include the current and evolving climate regulation, reporting frameworks and standards, and best practices\.  In addition to corporate reporting, the investor perspective will specifically be considered and topics such as ESG ratings, shareholder engagement, investment strategies, and vehicles to facilitate the financing of climate mitigation, adaptation, and transition plans will be covered\. The course will also enable students to analyze information from corporate ESG disclosures and other sources to estimate the impact on corporate cash flows, cost of capital, and, in turn, on corporate valuation\. 

The course incorporates an experiential learning component where students work with a small business to calculate their carbon footprint\. For more information, see the [UBC Sauder SME Climate Clinic](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/climate-centre/sme-climate-clinic)\.

**Eligibility:** This course is open to BCom students in Years 3 and 4; non\-BCom students in Years 3 and 4 and UBC graduate students\. 

### Learning Objectives:

Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the knowledge and skills to:

-   Apply knowledge gained on carbon accounting and GHG emissions to a small business and understand climate disclosures of large corporations or organizations\.
-   Use their knowledge of current ESG disclosure frameworks, standards, and best practices to evaluate corporate ESG disclosures\.
-   Determine what the material reporting issues are for different industries and corporations and evaluate the maturity of a corporation based on the level of ESG integration in their business\.
-   Differentiate between the main reporting frameworks and describe the TCFD framework and its four main thematic focus areas and how disclosure along these themes can benefit corporations\.
-   Describe the basic science behind the need to achieve net zero by 2050 and the relative importance of certain industries in this goal, with a specific focus on the role of financial institutions in financing transition plans\.
-   Differentiate between the main ESG ratings and describe how methodologies used differ and can result in a disparity in ratings\.
-   Apply fundamental ESG analysis to valuation and determine how to adjust a valuation model for climate and other ESG factors\.
-   Describe the financing vehicles available to uniquely address climate issues and finance transition\.
-   Differentiate impact investing from other ESG investment approaches and describe the strategies that can be used to hold corporations accountable to achieve targets and to execute transition plans\.

**Prerequisite:** Third\-year standing or above\.

Note: COMM 451 was formerly numbered COMM 486E\. The content has not changed\. If you've completed any course under its previous number or title, you are not permitted to take it again \(you cannot receive credit for the same course twice\)\.

title: COMR_V 186A - Personal Finance
content_markdown:
This course teaches the basics of personal finance to students who have little or no exposure to finance\. Personal finance is an extremely valuable skill that helps us invest and borrow responsibly, spend wisely, and plan appropriately\. The course will cover a broad range of topics, including budgeting, investing, purchasing real estate, taxes, as well as the basics of how our financial system works\.

### Learning objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

-   Understand the differences between saving and borrowing, know when it is optimal to do each or neither, and know how a typical person may differ from recommended\.
-   Understand time value of money and risk to be able to compare the attractiveness of various investment products accounting for transaction costs\.
-   Understand the basic infrastructure of our financial system and know the roles of commercial banks, investment banks, central banks, mutual funds, pension funds, insurance companies, hedge funds, private equity funds, and venture capital funds\.
-   Know basic accounting, be able to create a balance sheet for herself or read a balance sheet of a firm, be able to create a budget for herself or a small business\.

Note: This course is open to students at all year levels, with the exception of BCom students completing the Finance option\.

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 386C - Climate Literacy for Business
content_markdown:
Climate change is the most pressing issue facing humanity and the private sector is playing an increasingly important role in responding rapidly and comprehensively to this challenge\. The science of climate change is incredibly complicated and often poorly understood outside the scientific community\. Business solutions to climate change are set against a backdrop of national and global regulatory frameworks ranging from the EU Emissions Trading Scheme to the Clean Energy Act in the US to the UNFCCC Paris Accord\. Citizens, investors and communities are also creating enormous pressure on companies to take action to reduce their emissions and develop climate change solutions\. Business leaders have to respond to this various pressures under conditions of economic, social and scientific uncertainty\.

The purpose of this course is to provide students with a basic foundation in the science of climate change, the global regulatory responses to the issue including multinational agreements and specific policy instruments such as carbon taxes, scenario methods\.

The course will describe the major elements of the climate system including the carbon and hydrological cycle and will describe the main areas of scientific uncertainty\. Current climate change trends will be presented in the context of global temperature changes including the conditions under which fossil fuel reserves were formed\. Students will learn about the energy transition and transformation associated with industrial revolution and the key drivers of growing energy service use over the last 250 years\. Using an ecosystem services framework, the course will explore the value of positive externalities provided by natural and geological systems\. In particular, the course will examine the role of natural assets including forest and ocean based ecosystems, which have the potential to mitigate up to 40% of carbon emissions\. Focusing on the six key greenhouse gases, the students will explore the major sources of emissions and the broad impact anticipated from global temperature increases\.

The course will examine the major global policy initiatives that have sought to manage GHG emissions and the intragenerational and intergenerational equity dilemmas these negotiations have surfaced\. The course will describe the relative performance of the CDM and EU ETS systems and the major policy commitments under the Paris Accord\. The course will examine the relative successes of renewables in the stationary power sector and the challenges of displacing liquid fuels in the transporation sector\.

Finally the students will examine corporate commitments to carbon reductions and net zero through a range of emissions reduction pathways described in various scenario based studies, including the IPCC and the Shell Scenarios\. 

### Learning objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

-   Describe the main elements of a global circulation model\.
-   Explain the relative importance of the major elements of the carbon cycle\.
-   Describe the key areas of scientific uncertainty in the climate systems as the relate to business decision making\.
-   Analyse the emissions and energy profile of countries at different stages of economic development\.
-   Describe the major global policy initiatives to mitigate and adapt to climate change\.
-   Identify harder to abate emissisions sources\.
-   Analyze the benefits and costs of various climate policy measures from the perspective of a global company\.
-   Apply scenario methods to support the development of a company strategy that is resilient in the face of uncertainty\.

Note: COMM 386C will not be offered in 2026W\.

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 486K - Project Finance
content_markdown:
This course provides a presentation of the current state of project finance, and the use of the project finance to approach multivariate situations covering projects in Canada and abroad\. Project finance is an approach where debt is typically borrowed on a non\-recourse or limited\-recourse basis in which the cash flows generated by the project, and the assets of the project, serve as the collateral for the lenders\. This course will allow students the opportunity to engage with a number of case studies that illustrate the use of project finance\. This course will cover quantitative & qualitative project finance techniques and students will engage with the role of investors, lenders, government, key stakeholders \(including Indigenous parties\) and be introduced to financing considerations they will not have encountered in other courses\. The techniques referred to will include exposing students to the structuring considerations required for project finance; specifically focusing on risk allocation across the “7\-Axes Framework” which we will introduce in the course\. These techniques will benefit students in their careers and in their formation as they cover considerations such as: commercial contracts, leverage, hedging, insurance, hybrid equity structures, amongst others\.

content_markdown:
### Resources to help you reflect, set goals, and grow\!

[Student outside UBC Sauder on laptop](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/level_2_-_personal_development_resources_0.jpg?itok=wFEUUA0r)

**Personal development is a lifelong journey** to discover who you are, what truly matters to you, and how you can become the best version of yourself \(in your personal life and career\)\.

Taking time to reflect and understand your areas for growth is essential as it helps **develop self\-awareness** and **clarity** with your next steps\.

While working on your personal development is something to do throughout your life, it’s also **a great starting point** for your career journey\.

### Ways to get started

#### Self\-guided toolkits designed for UBC Sauder students

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### [https://sauder\-ubc\-csm\.symplicity\.com/students/app/resources/document\-library/content/b3e6d7a9879ae088b14adb92e72cb02a](https://sauder-ubc-csm.symplicity.com/students/app/resources/document-library/content/b3e6d7a9879ae088b14adb92e72cb02a)[Strengths, Values, Motivators Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/strengths_values_motivators_1.png?itok=zt-BKrX8)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **Strengths, Values, Motivators Toolkit**
    
    The first step to developing a fulfilling career is understanding **what** **interests you**, **what** **you care about**, and **what you’re good at**\.
    
    Knowing your strengths, values, and motivators can be a building block to **creating a lifestyle and career you enjoy**\. This toolkit is designed to help you reflect and discover what drives you\.
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### [https://sauder\-ubc\-csm\.symplicity\.com/students/app/resources/document\-library/content/a7f27b567144523c8f96aeb0da514f67](https://sauder-ubc-csm.symplicity.com/students/app/resources/document-library/content/a7f27b567144523c8f96aeb0da514f67)[Career Goals Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/career_goals_toolkit_3.png?itok=4Jb2UmEk)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **Career Goals Toolkit**
    
    Planning goals for your future and career can feel intimidating; however, breaking them down into **small achievable steps** can make your plans more tangible\.
    
    This toolkit will **empower you with the strategies** to tackle your big goals in your personal and professional life\. 
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    [https://sauder\-ubc\-csm\.symplicity\.com/students/app/resources/document\-library/content/d77f00697a52c000b7586dbfdd870d5a](https://sauder-ubc-csm.symplicity.com/students/app/resources/document-library/content/d77f00697a52c000b7586dbfdd870d5a)[Career Mindset & Emotional Intelligence Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/career_mindset_emotional_intelligence_toolkit_1.png?itok=SD1K1Z_Y)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **Career Mindset & Emotional Intelligence Toolkit**
    
    Emotional Intelligence \(EQ\) is one of the **strongest predictors of job performance**\.
    
    Having a healthy EQ means you find it easier to understand and **manage your emotions**, **get along with others**, **communicate**, and **thrive** in new situations\.
    
     Like a muscle, EQ is something you can improve and develop if you put in the work\. Learn more with this toolkit\.
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

###### Access additional Career Toolkits on other career\-related topics like resumes, cover letters, and interviews on [**UBC Sauder Career Hub**](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/)\.

*CWL login is required to access all Toolkits\.*

> -   [Graduate Studies](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-options/graduate-studies)
> 
> ### How can you get more support?
> 
> Book a career **[coaching & advising appointment](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching)** on UBC Sauder Career Hub for personalized 1:1 support for all aspects of your career journey\.
> 
> [Book an appointment](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments)
> 
> \(*CWL login required\)*

### Develop your EQ with the Emotional Capital Report

According to **[research](https://www.forbes.com/sites/travisbradberry/2014/01/09/emotional-intelligence/#797917801ac0)**, **EQ is the strongest predictor of workplace and leadership success**\. Findings show that **90% of top performers have high EQ**, and those with a high EQ have the potential to earn an average of **$29,000 more per year**\.

**[COMM 202 Career Fundamentals](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/comm202)** will introduce you to the **[RocheMartin Emotional Capital Report \(ECR\)](https://www.rochemartin.com/emotional-capital-report)\.** This 15\-minute assessment will give you a score based on ten leadership competencies using a global scientific measure\. It **provides explanations of the leadership behaviours** associated with the score and **coaching strategies** for developing your EQ and leadership abilities\.

The ECR has been vigorously and scientifically tested\. It gives a valid and reliable measurement of leadership competencies based on the Bar\-On and Goleman measures of EQ\.

[Emotional Capital Report book](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/emotional-capital-report-book.png?itok=G1bs9jww)

### Additional Resources

-   **[VIA Survey of Character Strengths](https://www.viacharacter.org/)** for a free, personalized analysis of your character strengths

-   Fill out the **[My Unique Career Journey worksheet](https://www.dropbox.com/s/1covz5wttkxaob1/My-Unique-Career-Journey-Worksheet.pdf?dl=0)** to help you set goals and understand opportunities for growth

### Navigate Your Career Journey

Trying to figure out what type of work interests you? Or maybe you’re wondering what resources can help you achieve your goals? No matter where you are in your unique career journey, you can use our career development model to help navigate your personal and professional goals at UBC Sauder and beyond\.

title: Work & Volunteer Experience
content_markdown:
### Gain experience & build your professional skills

[Students working at a whiteboard](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/level_2_-_work_and_volunteer_experience.jpg?itok=LzMGbyu9)

When talking about gaining experience for your resume, we’re **not just referring to *paid* work experience**, especially early on in your career journey\. To build your experience and skills, you can take part in a wide variety of activities, including:

-   Internships
-   Co\-op work terms
-   Paid work \(part\-time, full\-time, and contracts\)
-   Mentorship programs
-   Case competitions
-   Starting your own business
-   Volunteering
-   Team & club participation
-   Group projects in the classroom

These experiences will help you gain transferrable skills, make connections, build your story for future job applications, and clarify your career goals\.

### Ways to get started

#### Self\-guided toolkits designed for UBC Sauder students

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    [Work & Volunteer Experience](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/work_volunteer_experience_toolkit_0.png?itok=x3shJkHU)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **Work & Volunteer Experience Toolkit**
    
    Your previous work and volunteer experiences are essential indicators to employers of your capabilities\.
    
    This Toolkit explains how to gain experience strategically to align with the career path you want to take\. It also highlights the 70% rule: You don’t need to meet 100% of the job requirements to apply\!
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    [Job Search Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/job_search_toolkit_0.png?itok=rItqbaIk)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **Job Search Toolkit**
    
    Searching for work, whether you’re looking for an internship, Co\-op work term, part\-time position or full\-time role, takes time and planning\.
    
    Read this toolkit to learn about effective job search strategies and how to use your time best\.
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    [Career Goals Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/career_goals_toolkit_3.png?itok=4Jb2UmEk)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **Career Goals Toolkit**
    
    Setting specific goals about gaining work experience will help you take your next steps forward\.
    
    This toolkit will give you strategies to tackle your big goals by breaking them down into small steps\.
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

###### Access additional Career Toolkits on other career\-related topics like resumes, cover letters, and interviews on **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/)**\.

*CWL login is required to access all Toolkits\.*

### Where to find opportunities

**UBC Sauder Career Hub**: UBC Sauder’s exclusive all\-in\-one career platform where you can find **internships**, **Co\-op work terms**, and **full\-time job postings** from companies actively recruiting UBC Sauder students\.

[Access Job Postings on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/jobPostings#/jobPostings/home)

\(*CWL login required\)*

### Gain experience without an internship

Not landing an internship doesn't mean hitting pause on your professional growth\. A traditional internship isn't the only way to gain experience\. There are lots of alternative ways to explore new opportunities, build your network, and gain experience beyond traditional internships\.

Here are 11 alternatives to internships that can help you build relevant and transferable skills to help you move towards your career goals\. 

[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/file/6519/download?token\=MoyxaqlN](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/6519/download?token=MoyxaqlN)[Alternatives to summer internships](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/screenshot_summer_alternatives.png?itok=KBc1ZbRu)

[Click the image to download](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/6519/download?token=MoyxaqlN)

  
  
  
  

[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/file/6519/download](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/6519/download)

**CareersOnline**: Browse this job and volunteer board for all UBC students\. Find **[Work Learn](https://students.ubc.ca/career/ubc-experiences/work-learn-program)** positions along with other on and off\-campus opportunities\.

[Access CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/index.php/pid389509)

\(*CWL login required\)*

### Other things you can do

#### **Connect with**:

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   Employers actively recruit UBC Sauder students at **Company Recruitment Sessions** held throughout the year \(register on **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/events)** to attend\)

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   Peers and business professionals at student club events and conferences\. **[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/student-initiatives-and-government)** about student initiatives

#### **Apply for**:

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   The **[UBC Sauder Co\-op Program](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/co-op-program)**: gain three 4\-month work term experiences relevant to your BCom degree while getting paid

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[Mentorship & Specialty Programs](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/mentorship-specialty-programs)**: learn directly from business professionals

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[Work Learn Program](https://students.ubc.ca/career/ubc-experiences/work-learn-program)**: gain part\-time work experiences at UBC, where you can learn from a mentor and expand your professional network while a full\-time student\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[On\-campus jobs](https://students.ubc.ca/career/ubc-experiences/campus-jobs)**: Gain work experiences at specific UBC units, departments, and facilities such as the **[Alma Mater Society \(AMS\)](https://can231.dayforcehcm.com/CandidatePortal/en-US/almamater)**, **[UBC Recreation](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/)**, [**Student Housing**,](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/jobs/) **[Food Services](https://food.ubc.ca/jobs/)**, **[UBC Annual Giving](https://give.ubc.ca/about-us/join-our-team/call-centre/jobs-with-the-call-centre/)**, and **[UBC Libraries](https://about.library.ubc.ca/work-with-us/)**\.

#### **Go international with**:

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[Go Global Research Abroad](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/international-experiences/research-abroad)**: Build your academic network and get hands\-on research experience at a university outside of Canada

#### **Get involved with your community through**:

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   [**Student Initiatives and Government**:](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/student-initiatives-and-government) As a UBC BCom student, you’re a member of the UBC Alma Mater Society \(AMS\) and the Commerce Undergraduate Society \(CUS\)\. Funded by your student fees, both societies facilitate services and opportunities to enhance student experiences\. Explore leadership and community\-building involvement opportunities, case competitions, and networking events\.

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[UBC Spark Orientation](https://www.ubcsauderspark.com/)**: Spark welcomes first\-year and transfer students to the UBC Sauder community and is vital to the UBC Sauder experience\. Get involved as an Orientation Leader, leading cheers as a Spirit Leader, or supporting with logistics as a volunteer\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[Imagine UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc)**: A UBC\-wide orientation event where students can gain leadership skills and the opportunity to connect with first years\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[UBtheChange](https://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences/ubthechange)**: Develop leadership and career skills as a Student or Community Activator while working towards broader social and environmental initiatives\.

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[Student grants for community projects](https://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences/grants-community-projects)**: The Centre for Community Engaged Learning funds student\-led projects that partner with BC\-based community organizations\. Build on your experience working with the community and get creative with what you can do to address community needs\.

### Have questions?

**[Peer Career Advisors](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/career-peer-advisors)** will be back in September 2026\.

Book a career **[coaching & advising](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching)** appointment on UBC Sauder Career Hub for personalized 1:1 support\.

[Book your appointment](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments) 

\(*CWL login required\)*

Trying to figure out what type of work interests you? Or maybe you’re wondering what resources can help you achieve your goals? No matter where you are in your unique career journey, you can use our career development model to help navigate your personal and professional goals at UBC Sauder and beyond\.

title: Interview Prep Resources
content_markdown:
### Preparation is key\! Get interview\-ready 

[Students preparing for interviews](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/level_2_-_interview_prep_resources.jpg?itok=VodlrY3O)

Job interviews can be both exciting and nerve\-wracking\. **Practicing and preparing is the best way to boost your confidence** and land the job you want\.

Interviews are your chance to shine and to tell your unique story in more detail\. Do this by clearly showcasing your

-   Skills
-   Interests
-   What you can bring to the role and organization

Doing your homework before every interview to understand the role, organization, and industry will help you feel more confident, stand out, and land the position you want\.

### Ways to get started

#### Self\-guided toolkits designed for UBC Sauder students

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    [Interview Skill Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/interview_skills_toolkit.png?itok=YNN-trE7)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **Interview Skills Toolkit**
    
    Interviews are as much an opportunity for you to assess the company recruiting you as they are for the company to evaluate you\.
    
    This Toolkit will teach you about what interviewers are looking for, how to prep for different types of interviews, what questions to ask, and more\!
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    [Networking & Informational Interviews Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/networking_toolkit_icon_0.png?itok=uXfwWJFe)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **Networking & Informational Interviews Toolkit**
    
    Before the interview, you can start building connections within the organization you want to work for via informational interviews \(also known as coffee chats\)\.
    
    Learn tips on how to do this with this Toolkit\.
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

##### Access additional Career Toolkits on other career\-related topics like how to set SMART goals, resumes, and cover letters on **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/)**\.

### Strategies for crafting compelling cover letters 

[Student working on cover letter on computer](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/level_2_-_cover_letter_resources_0.png?itok=6yOiSnH1)

Although some employers no longer require cover letters, **most still expect you to submit one alongside your resume**\. Getting your cover letter right can be crucial to stand out in the application stage\.

This one\-page document allows you to communicate to potential future employers your:

-   Story
-   Skills
-   Qualifications
-   Motivations

Sharing your relevant skills and experiences and tailoring them to the position, organization, and industry you're applying to **helps hiring managers better understand** who you are and **why you’re the right candidate** for the job\.

title: Negotiation Resources
content_markdown:
### Learn the do’s and don’ts of negotiating offers 

[Students looking at laptop](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/level_2_-_negotiation_resources_0.jpg?itok=8BCZB4k2)

Your hard work has paid off, and **you’ve received a job offer\!**

While this is undoubtedly exciting, it’s best to avoid accepting job offers immediately\. Give yourself time to **consider whether the offer is really what you want**\. And if it isn’t, there may be room to negotiate\.

But how do you go about negotiating? Review the Hari B\. Varshney Business Career Centre's \(BCC\) below resources for guidance\.

### Ways to get started

#### Self\-guided toolkits designed for UBC Sauder students

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    [Navigating the Offer Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/navigating_the_offer_toolkit_0.png?itok=lrIAt8L8)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### [Navigating the Offer Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/13368)
    
    Negotiating job offers doesn’t come without risks, but the payoff can be worth it\.
    
    Learn about the risks and benefits of negotiation and how to navigate different offers\. This Toolkit provides you with example scripts to use with employers and tips about things other than the salary you can negotiate\.
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

##### *CWL login is required to access all Toolkits\.*

##### Access additional Career Toolkits on other career\-related topics like how to set SMART goals, resumes, and interviews on **[Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/)**\.

### Additional Resources

Understanding what people with your experience level get paid relative to the industry, company, and role is helpful\. Researching multiple sources is a crucial first step\. We recommend starting with:

[Job IQ Explorer on Career Hub](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/job_iq_explorer_homepage_for_promo_0.jpg?itok=DVo6qfAX)

Job IQ Explorer in the UBC Sauder Career Hub gives you exclusive access to real, anonymous hiring data from UBC Sauder students and recent alumni\. Explore employers, salary ranges, hiring trends, offer timing, and more to make informed career decisions\.

**Why use Job IQ Explorer?**  

Use real UBC Sauder hiring data to help guide your career planning and job search\.   

-   **Explore employers**: See which organizations hire UBC Sauder students and graduates 
-   **Compare salaries**: View salary ranges by employer, role, industry, and location 
-   **Plan your job search**: See when students typically receive offers 
-   **Discover job search strategies**: Learn which activities and resources helped students secure opportunities 
-   **Explore career paths**: Discover employment trends across different industries, degrees, and graduation years 

[Access Job IQ Explorer](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/job-analytics/post-graduation)

*\(CWL login required\)*

title: Career Exploration Resources
content_markdown:
### Explore different career paths & start your career planning today\! 

[BCom Student with Career Strategist](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/level_2_-_career_exploration_resources.jpg?itok=bj3FE1yl)

Are you interested in learning about different industries? Or maybe you’re wondering what skills and experiences can equip you for your chosen career path\.

Check out the career exploration resources below to develop a more robust understanding of:

-   How and where to do **career research**
-   **Different career paths** and what they involve
-   Ways to **get support** with career exploration

### Ways to get started

#### Self\-guided toolkits designed for UBC Sauder students

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    [Career Research Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/career_research_toolkit-300w.png?itok=YH9v5SDD)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **C****areer Research** **Toolkit**
    
    Whether you have a solid career goal or are still figuring things out, **researching is essential** to building a fulfilling career\.
    
    Find recommended resources, questions to ask, and tools for doing your research\.
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    [Role Alignment Toolkit](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/role_alignment-300w.png?itok=zLdnIKnF)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    #### **Role Alignment Toolkit**
    
    As you search for jobs, it’s helpful to know if the jobs you're finding align with your career goals and if you align with the job’s requirements\.
    
    This toolkit highlights which industries require certain grades, what to think about for locations, and when professional designations are needed\. 
    
    [Access on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13712)

Access additional Career Toolkits on other career\-related topics like resumes, cover letters, and interviews on **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/)**\.

*CWL login is required to access all Toolkits\.*

### Working In Guides

[Image](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/working_in_guides_career_hub_banner.jpg?itok=jEDeOwT8&c=9752d95754c0c92c3c41327a66fa50fc)

Curious about what different career paths have to offer? Check out the **BCC's Working In guides on UBC Sauder Career Hub** for a deep dive into the following fields:

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[Accounting](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13713)**: learn about different accounting practices, what Chartered Professional Accountants \(CPAs\) are, how to become a CPA, salaries, recruitment cycles, etc\.

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   [**Business Analytics**](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13713): learn about what analytics professionals do, different business analytics opportunities, skills & qualities employers look for, etc\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   [**Business Technology Management \(BTM\)**](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13713): learn about solving business challenges using technology, typical roles in BTM, where a BTM degree can take you, key employers, etc\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   [**Climate & Environmental Impact**](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13713): learn about climate\-related career opportunities for business students, key concepts & frameworks, company environmental, social, and governance \(ESG\) ratings, etc\.

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   [**Consulting**](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13713): learn about different consulting opportunities, different types of consulting firms, ways to get experience, salaries, etc\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[Finance](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13713)**: learn about different types of finance practices, the difference between "sell\-side" and "buy\-side", key employers, etc\.

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[Marketing](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13713)**: learn about the wide variety of marketing opportunities available, how to advance your marketing career, recruitment trends, etc\.

- **Row 8**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   **[Operations & Logistics](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/13713) \(OPLOG\)**: learn what OPLOG professionals do, different types of opportunities in the field, career progression, salaries, etc\.

*CWL login is required to access all Working In guides\.*

> -   [Graduate Studies](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-options/graduate-studies)

### Vault Career Guides & Rankings

[Vault logo](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/vault_new-01.png?itok=qnSmXeDI&c=0e89631cf728c28dde4932f49cc40efa)

**Find in\-depth intelligence on what it's really like to work in different industries, companies, or professions**\. With Vault, you get unlimited access to:

-   **Career Guides & Advice**: Access guides on a wide range of industries and roles, along with interviewing and networking tips
-   **Company Rankings & Profiles**: Find insider information on where people love to work and what might make an employer the right fit for you
-   **Jobs & Internship**s: Find opportunities and get all the details on top internship programs
-   **Exclusive Events**: Discover career fairs where you can meet and interview with employers

#### **How to access Vault**

The BCC provides all BCom students **free access to Vault** to support their career exploration\. Follow the below steps:

1.  Log in to **UBC Sauder Career Hub** using your CWL
2.  Click on ***Resource Library*** in the left navigation
3.  Search **"Vault"** in the top search bar
4.  Click on the Vault resource you want to use
5.  Once on the Vault page, select ***Get Started*** > ***Register now***
6.  Complete the registration form using your preferred email address
7.  Create your profile to tailor the content you want to see and more

[Access Vault on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/)

\(*CWL login required\)*

### Career Masterclass Collection 

[Person on laptop](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/career_masterclass_image_0.jpg?itok=EEce2yIX)

Ready to **AI\-Proof your job search, stand out in the job market** and **land that job?**

Check out the **Complete Career Masterclass Collection,** a set of **online courses** designed by former LinkedIn employees to help you take control of your career and get hired faster\!

The BCC provides all UBC Sauder students **FREE lifetime access \(**valued at $300\+\.\) 

**Learn how to:**

1.  **Optimize:** Accelerate your job search with ChatGPT
2.  **Strategize:** Build applications that land interviews
3.  **Stand out:** Get recruiters to notice your LinkedIn
4.  **Network:** Break into the tech industry
5.  **Succeed**: Get hired with a winning job search strategy

 **Career Masterclass Courses include:**

•    Unbreakable: How to AI\-Proof Your Job Search, Career, and Future

•    Accelerate Your Job Search with ChatGPT

•    Build a Resume \+ Cover Letter That Win Interviews  
•    Land the Perfect Job with LinkedIn  
•    Land Your First Tech Job  
•    Find Your Fit   
  

Fill out the form and create a new account to enroll\. 100% discount coupon automatically applied at checkout\. If you already have an account, login [here](https://courses.breakinto.tech/bundles/complete?th__ug=fc8e820c&th__c=goubc)\.

[Enroll for Free Here](https://forms.gle/r9FM3JQgqTLmQkhD6)

### Networking Resources

Talking with people working in areas you’re interested in is a great way to increase your understanding of working in different careers\.

Learn best practices and tips for connecting with professionals and building your network [**here**](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/networking-events/networking-resources)\.[https://w/BCC/Marketing/05%20Webpages%20\-%20MyBCom,%20Canvas,%20Sauder\.ubc\.ca/myBCom/2023\-2024/Navigation%20updates/Mock\-ed%20Up%20Pages/Level%202%20\-%20Career%20Exploration%20Resources\-KR\.docx\#\_msocom\_1](https://w/BCC/Marketing/05%20Webpages%20-%20MyBCom,%20Canvas,%20Sauder.ubc.ca/myBCom/2023-2024/Navigation%20updates/Mock-ed%20Up%20Pages/Level%202%20-%20Career%20Exploration%20Resources-KR.docx#_msocom_1)

### Want more support?

 **[Peer Career Advisors](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/career-peer-advisors)** will be back in September 2026\. 

 Book a **[coaching & advising](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching)** appointment on UBC Sauder Career Hub for personalized 1:1 support\.

[Book on Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments)

\(*CWL login required\)*

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-personal-exploration/career-exploration-resources)

### Career resources for students from specific communities

Campus partners have teamed up to create career resources for students with disabilities and LGBTQ2SIA\+ students\. These guides cover answers to your FAQs and link you to campus and community resources to help you thrive\. Check them out\!

[Learn More](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/career-resources-for-students-from-specific-communities/)

No matter where you are in your unique career journey, you can use our career development model to help navigate your personal and professional goals at UBC Sauder and beyond\.

title: Taking Courses Outside of UBC
content_markdown:
UBC provides a wide range of courses for your academic pursuits\. As a UBC BCom student, you are expected to complete your degree requirements at UBC through on\-campus or [UBC Distance Learning](https://distancelearning.ubc.ca/courses-and-programs/distance-learning-courses/) courses, or on [Go Global exchange](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/exchange)\. The Office of Student Academic Services \(OSAS\) is here to provide you with the information you need to help you achieve your personal and academic goals\. 

In certain circumstances, students may be eligible for/granted a Letter of Permission to take courses outside of UBC\. Before requesting an LOP, please read the following information carefully\.

## Letter of Permission \(LOP\)

In certain circumstances you can be granted permission to study outside of UBC with a Letter of Permission \(LOP\)\. Without an approved LOP, your transfer credits may not be counted towards your UBC degree\.

### You do NOT need an LOP if you:

-   are taking courses at a partner university through [Go Global Exchange](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/exchange)
-   have cross\-campus registration at UBCO\. For this you will need to complete a [Cross\-Campus Registration form](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/cross-campus-registration/)
-   are leaving UBC to complete your degree elsewhere
-   do not intend to apply credit completed towards your Bachelor of Commerce degree

### You need an LOP for:    

-   [The Explore French language program](https://englishfrench.ca/explore/?lang=en)
-   [City Studio](https://citystudiovancouver.com/schools/ubc/)
-   [Semester in Dialogue](https://www.sfu.ca/dialogue/semester.html)
-   To participate in a for\-credit program endorsed by Arts Indigenous Student Advising \(AISA\): BCOM students interested in these programs should still connect with an academic advisor at the OSAS for more information and are expected to request the LOP through OSAS
-   To participate in a for\-credit unique experience not available through UBC
-   To participate in a for\-credit program or Field School recognized by a UBC Department
-   In certain exceptional circumstances to meet core BCom degree requirements 

### You are eligible for an LOP if:

#### **You are in good academic standing**

To be eligible for a Letter of Permission \(LOP\), you must be in good academic standing\. Students are not eligible for an LOP if they:

-   Are currently on academic probation
-   Have had a failed session
-   Have received one or more failing grades during the current or previous academic year \(September to August\)

If you believe your situation may warrant an exception, please speak with an Academic Advisor at OSAS to explore your options\.

#### **You are a returning student**

First\-year students will not be granted LOPs in their first Winter session at UBC\.

#### **You have enough transfer credits left**

The residency requirement states that a minimum of 50% of your degree requirements \(61 credits\) must be completed while registered as a student in the BCom program\. Go Global exchange credits are eligible towards these minimums\.  
  
Note that the maximum number of transfer credits that can be obtained through LOPs is 12 credits\.

#### **The course is a lower\-level elective**

All required COMM\_V courses \(and CPSC\_V courses for BUCS\_V students\), and upper\-level elective courses must be completed at UBC\.

If the course is offered at UBC an LOP request will not be approved\.

#### **The institution is accredited**

Because transfer credit is only granted for courses that can be considered equivalent to something that UBC would offer, credit will only be granted for academic study at recognized post\-secondary institutions\.

#### **The course is considered a unique opportunity to enhance your degree**

This rationale must be provided in writing\. Note that LOP requests based on proximity to your home, or for financial reasons such as a lower tuition cost, will not be supported\.

### Requesting an LOP:

A student will need to **meet with an advisor and explain their situation** in order to request a Letter of Permission\. Please note that approvals are very rare, and are granted only in exceptional circumstances\.

Requests are reviewed individually and you will be notified with a decision by email\. The process to evaluate an LOP request can take several weeks, so please factor this into your planning\.

[Contact and Academic Advisor to Request an LOP](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/osas#connect)

### Other things to note:

**Recommendations:** a course recommendation by a professor or division does not guarantee that an LOP will be approved\.

**Admission to the other institution:** an LOP issued by UBC does not guarantee admission as a visiting student to another institution\. It is your responsibility to ensure that you meet all entry requirements as a visiting student at the host institution\.

**Concurrent registration:** Concurrent registration at both UBC and other post\-secondary institutions is not recommended\. 

**Scheduling conflicts:** if you decide to pursue a course at another institution while taking courses at UBC we expect that you will prioritize fulfilling academic responsibilities at UBC\. Students are expected to make note of any scheduling conflicts between coursework and/or exams at UBC and the other institution\. UBC will not support academic concession petitions based on such conflicts\.

**Expiration of the LOP:** An LOP can be used only for the Term that it is granted\. For example, if you have an LOP approved for Winter Session Term 1 and decide to take the course in Winter Session Term 2, you will need to reapply for a new LOP\.

**Applying the transfer credits to your degree:** to be eligible for transfer credits, BCom students must have approval from an Academic Advisor in OSAS before registering at another institution\. Please review [https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/letter\-permission](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/letter-permission)

title: Campus Closures
content_markdown:
#### The University may cancel or reschedule academic activities and reduce non\-essential services in response to extreme weather conditions or other unforeseen circumstances\. Updates and alerts regarding campus closures will be posted on [ubc\.ca](https://ubc.ca/) 

#### The information below applies to ALL students registered in COMM, COHR, COMR, BUSI and COEC courses\. 

## How will I know if my classes or exams are cancelled?

Always check [ubc\.ca](https://ubc.ca/) for the most up\-to\-date information about campus closures\. 

### If COMM, COHR, COMR, COEC or BUSI *classes or midterm exams* are cancelled:

-   Please monitor your Canvas Announcements and your email for direction from your instructors\. 

### If any *final exams* are cancelled:

-   Offical campus closure notice will be posted [ubc\.ca](https://www.ubc.ca/)\. 
-   UBC Enrolment Services will inform affected students via email and provide directions on the next steps\. 
-   Instructors may also provide additional information via Canvas Announcements and/or email\. [Click here](https://students.canvas.ubc.ca/how-to-personalize-your-notifications-in-canvas/) to learn how to personalize your notifications in Canvas\. 

## A campus closure was announced at ubc\.ca on the day and time of my exam\. What should I do?

### If *classes or midterm exams* are cancelled: 

-   Confirm closure announcements on [ubc\.ca](https://www.ubc.ca/), Canvas announcements, and your email\.  
-   Note that your instructor may choose to replace your midterm exam with a live online class via Zoom on that day\. Check Canvas to confirm\.  
-   Continue preparing for all your exams until you receive updated information about new arrangements and assume that the midterm exams will be rescheduled rather than cancelled\. 
-   [Centre for Accessibility \(CFA\)](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility) clients should discuss their CFA\-approved accommodations for the rescheduled sitting\(s\) with their instructor\(s\)\. 

### If any *final exams* are cancelled: 

#### **Monitor closure announcements on [ubc\.ca](https://www.ubc.ca/)** 

-   You will receive an email notification if in\-person exams are cancelled that will include the general dates for any rescheduled exams\. Be sure to check Canvas notifications and your email regularly for the latest updates\. 
-   Continue preparing for all exams until you receive information about the new arrangements\. 

#### **Rescheduling Information:**

-   Cancelled exams will be rescheduled as follows: 

-   **Winter Term 1**: Examinations will be rescheduled on the Saturday \(and, if necessary, the Sunday\) following the first full week of classes in Winter Term 2\. 
-   **Winter Term 2 and Summer**: Examinations will be rescheduled on the day\(s\) following the last day of the formal final exam period for that term\. 
-   The location, time, and date for your rescheduled final exam will be posted at [students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/exams/exam\-schedule](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/exam-schedule) 
-   Students registered with [**CFA**](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) [https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)who require exam accommodations that cannot be provided for during the rescheduled exam should contact the [Office of Student Academic Services OSAS](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/osas) \([bcomquestions@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:bcomquestions@sauder.ubc.ca)\) to discuss their case\.  

## What do I do if there is a conflict with my rescheduled exam?  

There may be situations in which a rescheduled exam conflicts with another course or pre\-existing commitment\.  

**For in\-term evaluations/midterms**: Unless you have been given different instructions on who to contact, the expectation is that you will contact the course instructor directly to understand how this will be resolved\.  

**For rescheduled COMM, COHR, COEC, BUSI, COMR final** **exams**: [OSAS](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/osas) will send a survey to students who have indicated that they are not able to sit the rescheduled exam as planned and determine if they eligible to write the exam at an alternate time\. Your instructor may post an announcement on Canvas informing you about this survey\. 

**NOTE:** The survey link will only be available via Canvas Announcement or sent to you via email\. This survey will not be published elsewhere\. 

For rescheduled final exams, [CFA](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility) will provide support to eligible students with approved exam accommodations\. You must be a registered client of [CFA](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) to receive this support\. 

## Other Considerations 

-   Non\-Commerce courses: Note that faculties and their affiliated courses may approach how to address campus closures differently\. Please be sure to follow any instructions provided by your course instructor as courses may have their own specific set of instructions\. 

-   In the event of a campus closure, some NON\-COMMERCE in\-person exams may be moved to an online, remote format\. If this shift in format presents a challenge for you, contact your instructor and [OSAS](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/osas)\.  
    

-   If extenuating circumstances UNRELATED to the campus closure prevent you from writing an exam as scheduled, please review the information on academic concessions to determine whether your situation warrants submitting a petition for academic concessions\. 
    

-   For students who already have an approved academic concession for the originally scheduled exam: if you wish to attend the rescheduled exam rather than write during the official SD period, you must inform your instructor and [OSAS](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/osas) to ensure that an exam will be available for you\. 
    

-   Please note that during a campus closure, the University remains open in principle, but some services may be limited in response to the conditions\. We appreciate your patience and hope you stay safe and healthy\. 

***Please note that once you have started an exam, the grade you earn will stand\. You will not be given another opportunity to increase your mark\.*** 

> ### Emergency contacts
> 
> If you have an urgent concern or you're currently in distress, the following resources are available 24 hours/day, 7 days/week:
> 
> -   **Emergency Services**: 911
> -   **[Vancouver Coastal Health Emergency Care](https://www.vch.ca/en/health-topics/emergency-care)**
> -   **[UBC Campus Security](https://security.ubc.ca/):** 604\-822\-2222

> 
> ### Other supports
> 
> If you need additional assistance, these services are also available:
>

title: What does academic integrity meme to you?
content_markdown:
## Academic Integrity is a fundamentally important concept for all students in academia\. We would like to encourage students to add their voice to why academic integrity is important in a fun way\. And what better way to encourage academic integrity then through memes\!

We’re asking students to submit a meme related to academic integrity for a chance to win a prize\. The meme could show why academic integrity is important, why students should ensure they follow the UBC’s Academic Integrity Policy, or how academic integrity relates to their future careers\. But most of all your meme should be fun, creative, and inspiring\!

Some important things to remember when creating your meme:

-   No swearing, crude language, or mean\-spirited entries will be accepted
-   Be thoughtful about the entries you create – we would like to share these with the world, and we think that our students can create some fun and smart work

### Contest open\!

The contest will open for students on April 7th, 2024\. Students will be able to continue to submit **until midnight on April 16th**, through the following link:

 [Submit your meme here](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6Mtl2x0MQ2XRT2S) 

## Selection and awards

### Submission Shortlisting  

Six submissions will be short listed by popular vote by staff in the UBC Sauder Undergraduate Office on April 17th, 2024\. Shortlisted candidates will be notified\.  

### Student Voting   

On April 18th the shortlisted candidates will have their submissions posted to the [@CUSAcademics](https://www.instagram.com/cusacademics/) Instagram, where students will be able to vote on their favorite submissions through likes and shares\. The three memes with the most likes and shares by 6:00PM PST on April 21, 2024 will be the contest winners\!  

**The winners will all receive a $100 Visa Gift Card or Amazon Gift Card\. Remaining finalists will all receive a $50 Amazon Gift Card\.**  

## Eligibility 

To be eligible for this contest, students must:

-   Be currently enrolled in the Bachelor of Commerce program during the Winter T2 2024 academic semester\. 
-   Agree to publishing their submission to CUS social media pages \([@cusubc](https://www.instagram.com/cusubc/?hl=en)\) 
-   This contest is open to both individual and group projects
-   Students may choose to submit up to three \(3\) submissions

## Rules

-   Submissions of a unique meme related to the importance of academic integrity\. The combination of the meme image and words should be unique and created by the student who submitted the work\.
-   Image dimensions must be 600 x 600 pixels 

-   Video meme videos should be a maximum of 1 minutes and 30 seconds long 
-   The width of video memes must be at least 600 pixels in width  

-   Ensure that your meme is appropriate for distribution on official social media channels \(no swearing, explicit imagery, etc\.\) \- your meme can be inspirational, informative or funny\.
-   Your image can’t contain any watermarks \(your own or someone else’s\)\.
-   You agree that whatever images you submit are your own\. If you’ve sourced the image from another site, please ensure that the image is free of any copyright restrictions\.
-   You agree that the quotes you submit are your own\. If they are not, then we kindly ask that you do not plagiarize content\. If you are using someone else’s quote, please provide the source for the quote\.

## How to enter

1\. Submit your meme to [this link](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6Mtl2x0MQ2XRT2S) or via the button above\.
