title: COMM_V 486J - Disruption
content_markdown:
### CDL overview

CDL\-Vancouver is an expansion from the original Creative Destruction Lab at the University of Toronto’s Rotman School of Management, a program that has created more than $5\.0 Billion in equity value in eight years targeting companies that have the potential to transform our social, industrial, and economic landscape\. The CDL is one of the world’s premier seed stage programs for massively scalable science\-based ventures\. Notable graduates include: [Atomwise](http://www.atomwise.com/), [Notch Therapeutics](https://notchtx.com/press_release/notch-therapeutics-closes-85-million-series-a-financing-to-develop-pipeline-of-renewable-stem-cell-derived-cancer-immunotherapies/), [Plantible Foods](https://www.plantiblefoods.com/), [Ionomr Innovations](https://ionomr.com/), [Shift](https://tryshift.com/130/?gclid=CjwKCAjwg4-EBhBwEiwAzYAlsjhB6kVXRu2fcG_P2A4NCoTqR4zii8cKfoIXz6Wgu_dIYhyK5s8TdhoCBhwQAvD_BwE), [Spiderwort](https://betakit.com/spiderwort-closes-3-4-million-cad-in-seed-financing/) and others\.

### Course overview

In September 2024, a brand new CDL course called Disruption \(COMM 486J\) will be rolled out to provide students an opportunity to work on a CDL venture’s strategy\. Specifically, students will be provided with an awareness of how both start\-ups and larger corporations can disrupt incumbents in a market by analyzing the human behaviours and biases that tolerate inaction, global trends and zeitgeist that impact organizations, strategic theories that provide access to disruptive innovation, and the transformational strategic models supporting entrepreneurs and business leaders to execute upon disruptive strategy\. Students will apply their learning by contemplating new, disruptive opportunities for an existing venture participating in the Creative Destruction Lab Vancouver \(CDL\-V\) program at UBC Sauder\. Also, the work students do for ventures will be seen by the mentors/investors in the CDL program, and influence their investment decisions and the progress of the ventures\. Some of the students across the CDL network have joined venture\-backed CDL companies in key roles – this course is a unique opportunity for students who are interested in real world exposure to start\-ups and seed funding\. This course will be a prerequisite for COMM 489\.

title: COMM_V 386M - Green Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Startups
content_markdown:
Entrepreneurs are a powerful force for change\. Green entrepreneurs are driven to design new products and launch new ventures that prioritize environmental stewardship and social responsibility\. These emerging innovators are tapping into critical market shifts such as circular economies, renewal energy, regenerative food systems, and conscious consumerism\. In the face of climate change and climate\-related disasters such as droughts, floods, and hurricanes, it is imperative for companies, communities, cities, and nations to invent and adopt sustainable solutions that promote the efficient use of resources, reduce pollutions, and protect biodiversity\. This new course invites multidisciplinary students to discover and apply the foundational frameworks of green entrepreneurship and innovation to crafting sustainable startup ventures\. The topics focus on developing a sustainability\-oriented and entrepreneurial mindset and skillset necessary to identify, design and pitch ideas that benefit people and the planet, profitably\. In Startup teams, students with discover, co\-design and pitch regenerative, restorative and innovative ideas to impact investors, provided by Sauder’s Centre for Climate and Business Solutions\.

Eligibility: This course is open to BCom students in Years 3 and 4; non\-BCom students in Years 3 and 4 and UBC graduate students\. 

### Learning objectives:

By the end of this experiential course, students will be able to: 

1.  Identify their own potential as a purpose\-driven entrepreneur and intrapreneur\.
2.  Interpret key considerations, opportunities and challenges for green innovation\.
3.  Use emerging entrepreneurial methods, tools and resources on a new venture\.
4.  Associate and integrate the First Peoples Principles of Learning and Four Rs of Indigenous education into ideas, experiments, prototypes and value propositions\.
5.  Design and pitch a sustainable venture business model to impact\-focused investors\.

 Prerequisite: [COMM 280](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/comm280) recommended\.

Course credits:

3

    ## Welcome to the Bachelor of Commerce program\!
    
    ### Please refer to the link below if you are looking for more information on **[Transfer Credits](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/transfer-credits)\.**
    
    ### [Transfer Credits Page](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/transfer-credits)[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/transfer\-credits](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/transfer-credits)
    
    ### The courses below are all degree requirements, even though they are first\-year courses\. With the exception of COMM\_V 101, all students—regardless of what their Class Standing is when they start the BCom degree\-\- must complete them\.
    
    **[COMM\_V 101](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-101)[:](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-101)** is not required for students transferring to Second or Third Year of the program\. Transfer students must complete 3 credits of Commerce or Non\-Commerce courses at any level in lieu of COMM\_V 101\. You will find details on electives for transfer students [below\.](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/program-requirements/transfer-students#electiverequirements)[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/courses\-money\-enrolment/program\-requirements/transfer\-students\#elec](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/program-requirements/transfer-students#elec)
    
    **[COMM\_V 105](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/14730)[:](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/14730)** is required if you transfer into Year 2 or Year 3 of the program\. Be sure to include this course in your planning\.   
    
    **[COMM\_V 196](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/15516)[:](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/15516)** is required if you transfer into Year 2 or Year 3 of the program\. Be sure to include this course in your planning\. A minimum grade of 60% in COMM\_V 196 is required to receive credit for the course\. 
    
    **[COMM\_V 202](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/5216)[:](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/5216)** is required if you transfer into Year 2 or Year 3 of the program\. Be sure to include this course in your planning\.   
    
    **Not completing COMM\_V 105, COMM\_V 196 or COMM\_V 202 in the year you enter into the BCom program will delay your [degree progression](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/exams-and-grades/academic-standing)****\.** Keep these courses in mind when you plan your registration and when you are working on your **[program planning worksheets](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-worksheets)\.**  
    
    For students transferring into Second or Third Year of the program, credits completed prior to entering the program may be acceptable alternatives to required courses\. After entering the program, you must satisfy the requirement with the COMM\_V course\. See a list of alternatives on the **[Transfer Credits page](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/transfer-credits)\.**

## Elective Requirements

##### Elective requirements differ slightly depending on which option you choose to complete\. Effective 2023W for transfer students, non\-Commerce electives must include at least 3 credits in the humanities, and at least 3 credits in science or social science\. These elective credits may be completed during any year of your program\. Language courses are not eligible for the humanities requirement, but literature courses are\. BUCS students are exempt and do not have to fulfil this requirement\. See Elective Requirements for a list acceptable humanities, and science or social science courses\.  

#### **Accounting, Entrepreneurship, Finance, General Business Management, Organizational Behaviour and Human Resources, Business Technology Management, Marketing, Real Estate** 

-   **45 credits in total** 
    

-   27 credits non\-Commerce: must include minimum 12 credits at the 300 or 400\-level and 15 credits at 100, 200, 300 or 400\-level 
    

-   15 credits Commerce or non\-Commerce: must include minimum 3 credits at the 300 or 400\-level and 12 credits at 100, 200, 300 or 400\-level 
    

-   3 credits Commerce or non\-Commerce in lieu of COMM\_V 101 and can be 100, 200, 300 or 400\-level 
    

#### **Operations and Logistics** 

-   **48 credits in total** 
    

-   27 credits non\-Commerce: must include minimum 12 credits at the 300 or 400\-level and 15 credits at the 100, 200, 300 or 400\-level 
    

-   18 credits Commerce or non\-Commerce: must include minimum 6 credits at the 300 or 400\-level and 12 credits at the 100, 200, 300 or 400\-level 
    

-   3 credits Commerce or non\-Commerce in lieu of COMM\_V 101 and can be 100, 200, 300 or 400\-level  
    

#### **Global Supply Chain and Logistics Management** 

-   **42 credits in total** 
    

-   27 credits non\-Commerce: must include minimum 12 credits at the 300 or 400\-level and 15 credits at the 100, 200, 300 or 400\-level 
    

-   12 credits Commerce or non\-Commerce at any level 
    

-   3 credits Commerce or non\-Commerce in lieu of COMM\_V 101 and can be 100, 200, 300 or 400\-level 
    

## Residency Requirement

Per the [UBC Calendar](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=3,40,0,0) at least 50% of the credits required for the program must be completed while registered in the program\. As the BCom program consists of 121 credits \(including one 1\-credit core course: COMM\_V 202\), 61 credits must be completed while in the BCom program and up to 60 credits completed prior to admission to the BCom program may apply\. In the case of BUCS, 64 credits must be completed while in the BCom program\.    

## Added Credit Summer Session

If you completed coursework in another UBC faculty prior to transferring from a post\-secondary institution into year 2 or 3 of the BCom program, you must notify the Office of Student Academic Services \(OSAS\) if you completed additional coursework at a post\-secondary institution in the summer prior to beginning your studies in the BCom program\. Consider the following example scenario\. A student completed one year in UBC Faculty of Arts \(Sept\-Apr\), one year at a post\-secondary institution \(Sept\-Apr\), and completed additional coursework at a post\-secondary institution in the summer \(May\-Aug\)\. The student must notify OSAS they earned additional credit\. Failure to notify OSAS of additional credit earned may lead to the inability to graduate due to insufficient credits completed in the program\.

## Bachelor of Commerce 

### Degree requirements for year 1 entry in 2022W or later

We encourage you to make use of the [BCom course planning worksheets](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/15052) as much as possible for the duration of your degree\. We also encourage you to consult with academic advisors to develop a comprehensive academic plan that aligns with your academic goals and ensures timely progression towards degree completion, particularly if you are considering a reduced course load\. Academic advisors can offer valuable insights and assistance in selecting courses, managing course loads, and navigating potential challenges in course registration\. To book an appointment with an Advisor, please go here: [https://calendly\.com/bcom\-ugo\-advising](https://calendly.com/bcom-ugo-advising)

title: Failed Year
content_markdown:
## Failed Year Standing  

All students in the Bachelor of Commerce program are required to maintain a sessional average of 60%\. This average is calculated on your grades from September to April\. Grades from courses taken in the summer session are not used in calculating a sessional average\.  

If your sessional average for the Winter Session falls below 60%, you are assigned a ‘Failed Year’ standing\. While students with a Failed Year standing are required to leave the BCom program, they may submit an appeal requesting permission to continue\. The appeal is an opportunity for students to present any extenuating circumstances that significantly affected them during the session\. The appeal can include documentary proof, where appropriate, that you connected with professionals \(doctors, counselors, etc\.\) to help resolve the extenuating circumstances\.

**If you have questions about your situation or need support, consider reaching out to an Academic Advisor at OSAS or consulting other on\-campus resources related to health, wellness, and financial planning:**

**[Support Resources](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/support)** 

### If this is: 

-   The first time you have a Failed Year standing and your appeal is successful: this means that you have been given permission to continue in the program\. OSAS will provide you with a letter that includes details on expectations that you must meet in order to be permitted to continue in the program\. This can include being placed on Academic Probation\.  
    

-   The first time you have a Failed Year standing and your appeal is NOT successful: you are required to withdraw from UBC for a period of at least one year\. OSAS will provide you with a letter that details the requirements you must meet in order to be eligible to apply for re\-admission\.  
    

-   The second time you have a Failed Year standing: you are required to [withdraw](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/advancement-regulations) from UBC for a period of one year\. Re\-admission to the BCom program after a second failed year is not granted\. \([UBC Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/advancement-regulations)\)\.
    

### If you intend to submit an appeal: 

The appeal form is open\. Appeals should be submitted by **May 27, 2026** in order to ensure you receive a response before registration for 2026W opens\. We cannot guarantee that appeals received after this date will receive a response before registration opens\.

**Requirements for submitting** **an appeal:**   

-   **Letter of appeal**   
    
-   **Supporting documentation** – If appropriate, provide doctors’ notes, official medical documentation, or other evidence that supports the grounds of your appeal\. If you are uncomfortable providing documentation, please connect with an Academic Advisor to discuss your situation\. Documentation and information provided will only be seen by the Academic Advisor preparing the appeal package and the Academic Review Committee for the purpose of reviewing your appeal\.
    

-   **Reference campus services** – If you have accessed campus services such as academic advising, peer programs, Counselling Services, the Centre for Accessibility, etc\., please include this in your appeal\. If you did not make use of campus resources, but intend to do so moving forward, please make specific reference to the resources you plan to use\. There are fields in the appeal form to include this information\.   
    

*If you have questions about the process or need support to structure your appeal, consider reaching out for additional support to an [Academic Advisor at OSAS](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/ugo) , the UBC Ombudsperson Office \(see [Appeal Guidelines](https://ombudsoffice-2016.sites.olt.ubc.ca/files/2024/06/Ombuds-Failed-Resources-Appeal-Guidelines-for-Students_Permission-to-Continue_UBCV-and-UBCO.pdf)\), or reach out to [AMS Advocacy](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/student-services/advocacy/)\.* [Appeal Form](https://sauder.jotform.com/260484797928073)

### FAQs:

Are sessional averages rounded up?

  
Averages are not rounded, so if your Winter Session average is below 60% \(e\.g\., 59\.9%\), you are considered to have failed the year\.  

I'm an international student\. What does being asked to discontinue mean for me?

  
As an international student, being required to discontinue the BCom program or withdrawing from UBC may affect your study permit and legal status in Canada\. It is imperative for you to review the International Student Advising website and seek advising from an International Student Advisor, as they are Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIA\)\. Academic Advisors at the UGO cannot advise on study permits or immigration\-related matters\.  

What will show on my Workday record?

  
Your Workday standing will reflect the status "Failed, Required to Withdraw" if you are not permitted to continue, regardless of whether it is your first or second failed year\.  

I am a fourth\-year student intending to graduate\. How does having a sessional average below 60% affect me?

  
If you are a graduating student and your final winter session average is below 60%, you will still be permitted to graduate\. However, your academic transcript will include the status "Failed, Permitted to Continue" for that Winter session\.

Note, however, that if you are a non\-graduating Year 4 student with a winter session average below 60%, your status will be "Failed, Required to Withdraw\." If this scenario applies to you, then we encourage you to connect with an Academic Advisor if you have not already done so\.  

I am registered in courses this summer\. Can I stay registered in them?

  
Because Term 1 classes start in May and appeal decisions are reached in June, you can stay registered in summer classes while your appeal is being reviewed\.

If your appeal is approved and the conditions of your appeal allow for you to remain registered in Term 2 courses, then you may keep those courses\.

title: Option Declaration
content_markdown:
Most students will be able to self\-declare their option \(specialization\) on Workday Student when they attain a Year 3 class standing \(year level\)\.

We encourage you to declare your option as soon as you’re eligible\. This will assist you in planning your saved schedules and ensure your access to required courses for your chosen option when your registration opens\.

You can register in one option only\.

Students who are unable to self\-declare their option can submit an option declaration request\.

### How to self\-declare your option

To declare your option, review the video tutorial on this page and the Workday tutorial *[Declaring or changing your primary major, honours, or specialization](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/declaring-or-changing-your-primary-major-honours-or-specialization/)*\. When following the steps in these tutorials, note that your current program of study is Bachelor of Commerce \(Vancouver\)\. Click on the white Request button in the right\-most column of that row to proceed\. Do **not** select the orange Add Program of Study button\.

Once you’ve declared your option, you won’t be able to change it yourself in Workday\.

If you're registering for the 2026 Winter Session, please self\-declare your option in Workday or submit the option declaration request form **by 11:00pm on June 21, 2026 at the latest**\. This will allow our office to determine remaining space in competitive options and process requests prior to registration for students who did not achieve minimum grades in required courses\.

**If you have not self\-declared in Workday or submitted the request form by the June 21 deadline you will be placed in the General Business Management option\.** Requests to switch from the option will be evaluated in mid\-July after all Year 3 students have registered, and approved only if eligibility requirements for the requested option are met AND there are seats remaining\. There are no guarantees that you will be switched to your preferred option even if you have met all minimum grade requirements so do not miss the deadline\.

If you have been granted deferred standing \(SD\) for any courses required for Accounting or Finance, you will be considered for your preferred option once you have completed your exams and your final grades have been posted\. You should still declare and register for an alternate option as backup\.

If you’ve been selected for the Global Supply Chain and Logistics Management option, our office will add you to your option\.

### Self\-declaration requirements for Accounting and Finance

Space in these options is limited, so students pursuing either one of these options must achieve minimum grades in prerequisite courses to self\-declare:

-   For Accounting, a minimum grade of 60% in each of COMM\_V 293 and COMM\_V 294
-   For Finance, a minimum grade of 67% in each of COMM\_V 190, COMM\_V 191, COMM\_V 293, COMM\_V 294, COMM\_V 295, and COMM\_V 298

### Option declaration after Term 1

If you meet the requirements for Year 3 after completing your Term 1 winter session courses, your class standing will be automatically updated and you'll be eligible to declare your specialization\. Given that many Term 2 option courses will already be fully enrolled, it's unlikely that you'll be able to start taking required courses for your option until the following winter session, in September\.

### Option declaration request form

You can request assistance if you’re unable to self\-declare your option in Workday if any of the following scenarios apply to you:

-   **You transferred to third year from another institution** – Year 3 transfer students who are new to UBC do not have access in Workday to self\-declare options until September\. Assuming you are eligible for the option that you are requesting, OSAS will add you to that option so that you are able to register in your required option courses when your registration opens\.
-   **You have transfer credit for one or more courses for which minimum grades are required \(Accounting or Finance\)** – Workday is unable to check transfer credit grades for the option selection process\. OSAS will review grades achieved in applicable transfer courses to determine your eligibility if you are requesting Accounting or Finance
-   **You did not achieve minimum grades in one or more courses required for Accounting or Finance** – Your request will be prioritized based on your previous academic performance if space remains once eligible students have declared\. We cannot guarantee a decision prior to your registration appointment\.

[Option Declaration request form](https://sauder.jotform.com/team/ugo/option-declaration-request)  

### Option switches

If you’ve just self\-declared your option in Workday, but have decided to pursue a different option instead, please submit the option declaration request form to initiate the change\.

While it may be possible to switch options once you’ve reached Year 4, space is often limited\. Typically, we won’t consider a switch request if you’ve completed more than two courses required for your current option\. We will not consider any requests as a means to complete a [double option](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/options/double-options)\.

title: COMM_V 486O - Innovation Consulting (Biomedical)
content_markdown:
Vancouver is a world\-leading hub for biomedical and life sciences innovation, and COMM 4860 will support graduates pursuing career opportunities in this field\. This class will provide an exponential learning environment where students will work as business and innovation consultants alongside the Faculty of Biomedical Engineering \(BMEG\), the Capstone teams and real med tech start\-ups\.  

This course will provide students with real\-world start\-up consulting experience, a basic technical literacy in some of the broader technologies and exposure to practicing professionals from various career paths in the industry\. In addition, students will interact with a range of Biomedical Engineering students who could become future co\-founders\. 

The course is scheduled in one 3\-hour block per week, of which one hour overlaps with BMEG student class time\. A flipped classroom approach will be deployed with pre\-readings and videos designed and structured to enable students to engage in classroom activities rapidly\. In addition, guest speakers will highlight different career tracks for business people in the industry and try to build some basic technical literacy with essential concepts from biomedical engineering\. 

### Learning objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the knowledge and skills to:

-   Analyze, evaluate and prioritize customer and stakeholder needs\.
-   Research, analyze and interpret the competitive landscape to identify gaps in the market\.
-   Develop a functional health industry literacy and translational capability and apply to business solutions\.
-   Interpret regulatory policy and IP commercialization principles to commercialization recommendations\.
-   Contribute to a diverse team with technical colleagues, industry, clinical and academic sponsors to collaborate on improved solutions\.
-   Undertake financial analysis and modelling to recommend cost and revenue structures\.
-   Analyze the buying process and recommend a go\-to\-market approach \(e\.g\. licensing versus company creation\)\.
-   Identify and map the logistical workflow involved in getting an innovation adopted, including channel partners\.
-   Assess and evaluate the resourcing of project implementation, enabling recommendations on implementation\.
-   Reflect on the contributions of all team members, including oneself, individually and in combination\. Identify strengths and areas for improvement\.

Note: COMM 486O will not be offered in 2026W\.

Prerequisite: [COMM/COMR 280](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/comm280) recommended\.

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 486A - Climate Finance
content_markdown:
This course covers a range of topics in the important and rapidly growing area of Climate Finance, centered on the confluence of finance and the mitigation of, and adaptation to, climate effects\. Implications will be drawn for all major segments of the global financial market\. Topics covered include:

-   Climate considerations in investment portfolios, including “green tilts\.”
-   Climate risk and global equity \(stock\) returns, including carbon\-premiums/discounts\.
-   Green bonds, investment yields, and the “greenium” premium\.
-   Real asset prices, climate effects and household finance\.
-   Climate risk, insurance, and financial risk management of climate effects\.
-   Carbon trading, pricing, and derivative financial securities\.
-   Climate risk and financial institutions including banks, capital requirements and regulation\.
-   Financing climate innovation, venture capital, and investor preferences\.

### Learning objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the knowledge and skills to:

-   Explain important issues, concepts and methods in climate finance, including those related to corporate finance, investments, risk management and financial institutions\.
-   Identify sources and analyze data on climate\-related financial assets\.
-   Transform research\-driven insights on climate finance published in leading finance journals into a practical toolkit for analyzing problems on both the buy\-side and sell\-side of financial market institutions\.
-   Apply core finance principles to the valuation, returns analysis, and risks analysis of climate\-affected and climate\-related real and financial assets\.

Prerequisites: All of [COMM 370](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/5240), [COMM 371](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-371)\.

Course credits:

3

## We are Recruiting\! International Case Competition Cohort

The UBC Sauder School of Business invites you to apply to represent the school at a prestigious International Case Competition taking place in Term 2 \(January\-March 2027\)\.

These competitions are held in person in the host country, and we will select up to 20 students to participate in this opportunity\.

This year, we are introducing a new cohort\-based recruitment model\. Students will first apply to join a **Term 1 Training Cohort**, designed to refine case competition skills in a collaborative and supportive environment\.

-   The cohort will meet **5–7 times in Term 1 \(September\-December\)** via Zoom\.
    
-   Sessions will focus on case analysis, structured problem\-solving, strategy, storytelling, and presentation skills\.
    
-   At the end of the term, students will participate in a **mock case competition**\.
    
-   Final team selection will be based on both Term 1 progress and mock competition performance\.
    

Successful students will then be assigned:

-   A specific team
    
-   A specific international competition
    
-   Focused team training leading up to the competition
    

[Apply here by August 9](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_8v9Cn1RG5G5sHr0)

**Information Session**

Interested in learning more about the cohort model, team selection process, or international competitions?

Please join our Information Session:

-   **Date \+ Time:** Tuesday, August 4
    
-   **RSVP \(Deadline Sunday, August 2\):  
    **[https://ubc\.ca1\.qualtrics\.com/jfe/form/SV\_a3sbx6o7BIPsCmG](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_a3sbx6o7BIPsCmG)
    

**About the Competitions**

Each year, UBC Sauder competes in several of the world’s leading undergraduate international case competitions\. All three events in Term 1 are consistently ranked among the **global top 10**, based on annual rankings by international competition coaches\.

This year’s locations will be confirmed in Term 1\. In the past, these have included competitions in **Copenhagen, California, or New Zealand\.** 

**Student Qualifications**

Applicants must:

-   Be a current **BCom student in 2nd, 3rd, or 4th year standing** as of September 2026
    
-   Be in any specialization or option
    
-   Be available for Term 1 virtual training
    
-   Commit approximately 30–40 hours of team training if selected from September to competition
    
-   Prior case competition experience is highly valued
    

Students with transferable skills \(e\.g\., consulting, public speaking, research, or relevant work experience\) are strongly encouraged to apply\.

**Costs**

The Term 1 Training Cohort is free\. Once students are selected to represent UBC Sauder, they will pay a standardized fee of **$850**, regardless of competition location\.

This fee covers:

-   Competition registration
    
-   Flights
    
-   Accommodation
    

Students are responsible for:

-   Meals not included in competition programming
    
-   Ground transportation
    
-   Cellular data/eSIM
    
-   Other personal expenses
    

If financial costs present a barrier, students may confidentially notify the International Case Competition Committee upon selection\.

**Application Process**

To apply, please:

-   Complete the online form:   
    [https://ubc\.ca1\.qualtrics\.com/jfe/form/SV\_8v9Cn1RG5G5sHr0](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_8v9Cn1RG5G5sHr0)
    

Upload a **single PDF** within the application that includes:

-   Resume
    
-   Transcript \(unofficial is acceptable; must include course numbers, course names, grades, and GPA by term or year\)
    

**Application Deadline:** **Sunday, August 9 at 11:59 PM \(Vancouver time\)**

**Selection Process**

Shortlisted applicants will be invited to interview via Zoom\.

Selection criteria include:

-   Academic record
    
-   Case analysis ability
    
-   Communication and presentation skills
    
-   Teamwork and collaboration
    
-   Complementary skill sets across the selected cohort
    

This is an exceptional opportunity to represent UBC Sauder on a global stage, develop advanced problem\-solving skills, and join a high\-performing community of peers\.

We encourage you to apply and look forward to connecting with you\.

If you have any questions, please contact [iccteams@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:iccteams@sauder.ubc.ca)\.

### What is a case competition?

Teams in a case competition are given a problem in the form of a case, and are given an allocated time frame to develop the best solution to with the information provided\. Teams deliver their solutions in a presentation format to judges and compete against other teams\. Formats for case competitions may vary, but teams will be assessed on their analytical, organizational, and presentation skills in relation to the case at hand\.

## Different Types of Case Competitions

### Internal

Internal case competitions are competitions hosted by a UBC or UBC Sauder\-affiliated group\. They are open to all students to register and compete in\.

NSCC

The National Strategy Consulting Competition and Conference is the largest undergraduate case competition at the University of British Columbia\. Our organization gathers students across the world to compete and connect while learning about the field of consulting\.

|  |

| [Learn more about NSCC](https://www.thenscc.com/competition) |

Imprint Case Competition

The Imprint Case Competition is held annually in February alongside the Imprint Conference\. As Western Canada's largest marketing and branding case competition, Imprint provides 100\+ undergraduate teams the opportunity to tackle real\-life, marketing\-related business problems from leading companies\.

|  |
| --- |
| [Learn more about Imprint](https://www.instagram.com/ubcimprint/) |

YWiB Simplifying Sustainability

Simplifying Sustainability is a case competition focused on creating a space in which participating students can learn more about the emerging sustainable business industry in Vancouver\. The case is about a real sustainable business in Vancouver; outlining the issues they face in their current business operations\.

Sauder Summit \(Internal\)

Sauder Summit is a week\-long case competition that will challenge students across the world to solve real and complex business situations\. Internal Sauder teams will compete for the chance to win a $1,000 cash prize and the opportunity to represent Team UBC in the Sauder Summit Global Case Competition\.

|  |
| --- |
| [Learn more about Sauder Summit \(Internal\)](https://www.saudersummit.ca/internal)[https://www\.saudersummit\.ca/internal](https://www.saudersummit.ca/internal) |

JDC West Junior Development

Sauder JDC West Junior Development works to bridge the gap between the school curriculum and other case development programs through interactive sessions, personalized feedback, and a final Mock Case Competition\. This is an opportunity for students who may be interested in the Sauder JDC West program\.

|  |
| --- |
| [Learn more about JDC West Junior Development](https://ca.linkedin.com/company/sauderjdcwestjuniordevelopment)[https://www\.instagram\.com/sauderjdcjuniordev/?hl\=en](https://www.instagram.com/sauderjdcjuniordev/?hl=en) |

### External

External case competitions are held by private, non\-UBC affiliated groups\. Any student team can sign up to compete in these, and they may not be the only UBC Sauder team represented\.

CPABC Annual Business Case Competition

The CPABC Annual Business Case Competition is a business strategy case competition that allows participants to demonstrate and develop their business acumen by challenging themselves and their teammates to create strategic, innovative solutions to real issues facing real businesses\.

|  |
| --- |
| [Learn more about CPABC Annual Business Case Competition](https://www.bccpa.ca/become-a-cpa/events/cpabc-annual-business-case-competition-2026/se-competition-2024/) |

CFA Institute Research Challenge

The CFA Institute Research Challenge is an annual global competition that provides university students with hands\-on mentoring and intensive training in financial analysis and professional ethics\. Each student will be tested on their analytical, valuation, report writing, and presentation skills\. They gain real\-world experience as they assume the role of a research analyst\. 

|  |
| --- |
| [Learn more about CFA Institute Research Challenge](https://www.cfainstitute.org/en/societies/challenge) |

Accounting for Sustainability

The A4S International Case Competition \(A4SICC\) is a unique opportunity for students across the globe to help shape a future where sustainable business is business as usual\. This is the chance for your ideas to be seen and heard by leaders from some of the world’s largest and most influential companies\.

|  |

| [Learn more about Accounting for Sustainability](https://www.accountingforsustainability.org/en/activities/awards/international-case-competition.html#:~:text=The%20competition&text=We%20invite%20students%20with%20creative,Support%20Human%20Rights%20for%20All) |

  

### Sauder presented teams \+ Invitational Case Competitions

There are case competitions where a specific team of students are selected to represent UBC Sauder against other universities\. Only one student team is selected, and a selection process is coordinated by the head organizer for UBC Sauder\. These include the JDC West team and Invitation Case Competitions \(ICC\) teams\.

JDC West

JDC West is the most prestigious undergraduate business competition in Western Canada, hosting 1,300 attendees and uniting over 650 delegates from twelve premier post\-secondary institutions each year\. Over the course of three days, students from British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba showcase their skills in the academic, athletic, and debate competitions\.

Our week\-long event, which consists of two 5\-hour cases, one 24\-hour case, several industry presentations from executive leaders, and a lifelong network of international connections\. 16 of the world's most prestigious business schools will be invited to send one team of four students to represent them\. The reach of this global competition spans across five continents and multiple nations, including China, U\.S\.A\., Australia, Denmark, Spain, Singapore, Thailand and more\.

| [Learn more about Sauder Summit](https://www.saudersummit.ca/global) |

The McGill Desautels Business Ethics Case Competition aims to increase student awareness of ethical decisions in business, to expose students to real\-world scenarios that they may encounter in their future careers, and provide students with the opportunity to enhance their critical thinking and presentation skills\.

CaseIT

CaseIT brings together top undergraduate students, distinguished faculty members, experienced industry professionals, and a dedicated student body\. This competition aims to challenge conventional thinking, offer professional connections to benefit your business career, and bridge the gap between business and technology\.

|  |

title: Office of Student Academic Services (OSAS)
content_markdown:
### Office of Student Academic Services \(OSAS\) Virtual Office

-   Please use your CWL to login to the Office of Student Academic Services \(OSAS\) Virtual Office\.
-   Please let one of our staff know if you have a time\-sensitive or urgent inquiry and do not have an appointment\.
-   If you are joining the Virtual Office for a scheduled advising appointment, please wait for the Academic Advisor  to move you to their private breakout room \(“office”\) for your meeting\.

Ensure that the name on your Zoom ID matches your name as it appears on Workday Student\. Do NOT put your student number on your Zoom ID\.

***AI tools which record, transcribe or take notes during meetings are not compliant with privacy laws at this time and are therefore NOT permitted during advising sessions\.***

[Access virtual office](https://site.sauder.ubc.ca/osas-virtual-office/)  

If you do not have a CWL and need to connect with the Office of Student Academic Services \(OSAS\), please contact us in person at HA 165, by phone at 604\.822\.8333 or by email at [bcomquestions@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:bcomquestions@sauder.ubc.ca)\.

#### Prospective Students

If you are a prospective student—whether you are currently in high school, studying at a different post\-secondary institution, or in a different faculty at UBC—you are welcome to connect with our Recruitment & Admissions team:

-   **Email us** at [bcom@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:bcom@sauder.ubc.ca)\.
-   **Book an appointment** or **register for an event** [here](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/programs/bachelors-degrees/bachelor-commerce/need-more-info)\.
-   To learn more about BCom program admissions, visit the [UBC Sauder Program Admissions webpage](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/programs/bachelors-degrees/bachelor-commerce/program-admission)\.

If you are on campus \(either as a student or visiting for the day\), you are welcome to drop by the Henry Angus Building \(Room HA 137\) for drop\-in admissions advising every **Thursday from 12 \- 2 pm\.**  
*Please note that drop\-in advising check\-in occurs with the Robert H\. Lee Graduate School and not the Office of Student Academic Services\.*

title: Transfer Credits
content_markdown:
## Transfer Credits

Transfer credit is awarded at the time of admission by the university\. However, faculties determine how the credits will apply to their programs\. 

 If you have been admitted to UBC and have accepted your offer of admission, you may be able to use transfer credits that you have been awarded by UBC to fulfill some of the requirements in the [Bachelor of Commerce \(BCom\) degree](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/program-requirements)\. Transfer Credits apply only to transfer students who completed the equivalent course prior to entering the BCom program\. Upon entering the program, BCom students are expected to satisfy the BCOM course requirements \(not the equivalent credits\) at UBC\. 

All students\-\-including transfer students\-\-must complete the following courses: [COMM 105, COMM 196 and COMM 202\.](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment-program-requirements/general-program-requirements/transfer-students) If you did not receive transfer credit for these courses, you should plan on registering in them as soon as possible\. Not completing these courses will delay your [degree progression\.](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/exams-and-grades/academic-standing)Transfer credits awarded at another institution or at UBC\-O will be reassessed for the UBC\-V BCom program\.

Per the [UBC Calendar](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=3,40,0,0) at least 50% of the credits required for the program must be completed while registered in the program\. As the BCom program consists of 121 credits \(including one 1\-credit core course: COMM\_V 202\), 61 credits must be completed while in the BCom program and up to 60 credits completed prior to admission to the BCom program may apply\. In the case of BUCS, 64 credits must be completed while in the BCom program\.  

If you completed coursework in another UBC faculty prior to transferring from a post\-secondary institution into year 2 or 3 of the BCom program, you must notify the Office of Student Academic Services \(OSAS\) if you completed additional coursework at a post\-secondary institution in the summer prior to beginning your studies in the BCom program\. Consider the following example scenario\. A student completed one year in UBC Faculty of Arts \(Sept\-Apr\), one year at a post\-secondary institution \(Sept\-Apr\), and completed additional coursework at a post\-secondary institution in the summer \(May\-Aug\)\. The student must notify OSAS they earned additional credit\. Failure to notify OSAS of additional credit earned may lead to the inability to graduate due to insufficient credits completed in the program\.

NOTE: *all* upper\-level \(300\- and 400\-level\) commerce courses, including core, option core and commerce electives must be completed while registered in the BCom program\. It is not possible to apply transfer credit toward these upper\-level requirements\. [See Requirements to Receive a Degree or Diploma\.](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/requirements-receive-degree-or-diploma) 

### Where to View Transfer Credits

You can view your credits on your Workday Student account by following the pathway Workday Student account > Academics > View Academic Record\. The exception to this is transfer students admitted with a prior degree\. Students holding a prior degree from another institution will receive a separate assessment from UBC Sauder\.

### First and Second Year Equivalent Credits

| COMM\_V 191 | STAT\_V 200 |  STAT 124 | Prior to 2025/26, STAT 200 must be completed at UBCV before admission to BCom to receive credit\. Effective for admission in 2025/26 and later, STAT\_V 200 completed at UBC or elsewhere will fulfill the requirement if completed prior to entering the BCom program |
| COMM\_V 192 | COMR\_V 329 | MGMT\_O 230 or MGMT\_O 330 |  |

| MATH\_V 100 | MATH\_V 104, 110, 180, 184, or 120 | MATH 100 or MATH 116 | 3 credits from MATH 110 \(6\) will apply towards the MATH 100 requirement and 3 credits towards a lower\-level non\-COMM elective\. |

NOTE: Organizational Behaviour and Human Resources courses with a prefix of COHR\_V and MGMT\_O courses from UBCO *cannot* be counted as non\-Commerce electives\. 

AP, IB or A\-Level Credits from High School

Refer to [UBC’s first year credit](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-credit/)\.

CEGEP

[Transfer credits](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/university-college-transfer/) may have been awarded at the time of admission to UBC\.

Post\-Secondary Studies

If you have received general transfer credits \(i\.e\., COMM 1\[st\], COMM 2\[nd\]\) and you feel the credits cover a specific COMM requirement \(i\.e\., COMM 293\) you can request an assessment \(see below\) \.Otherwise, the transfer credits remain general and may be used towards COMM electives\.

  

### Requesting Transfer Credit Assessments

Transfer students who received an unassigned COMM credit \(e\.g\., COMM 1st, COMM 2nd\) may request a re\-evaluation to determine if the credit fulfills a requirement in the program \(e\.g\., COMM 293\)\. Only requests for first\- or second\-year courses will be considered, as all upper\-level Commerce requirements must be completed while registered in the BCom program\.

Before submitting a request

-   Review the credits in the [BC Transfer Guide](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/) and/or [UBC’s Transfer Credit Search](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/search-tool) \(and [UBC’s first\-year credit](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-credit/) for AP, IB or A\-Level courses\)\. Some courses may already include a notation “not for credit in the BCOM program”\.
-   Check the [program requirements](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/program-requirements/bcom-requirements) and the course description to see if there is a substantial overlap in the content with the course you have completed\.

Requesting an assessment

-   Ensure you include a comprehensive outline of the course\(s\) you seek an assessment from the academic year when you had taken the course\. The outline should include:
    -   institution’s name
    -   course name and code
    -   credit value
    -   course completion year
    -   course duration
    -   name of the instructor
    -   textbook and materials used
    -   breakdown of the classes per week or day
    -   grade assessment
    -   course description/learning outcomes
    -   Complete the [Transfer Credit Evaluation Request Form](https://sauder.jotform.com/team/ugo/transfer-credit-evaluation)
    -   An assessment can take upwards to 4 weeks to complete from the time the request is submitted\.
    -   An assessment may results in one of the following:  
        -   Credit changing to a specific course
        -   No change and the unassigned credit may be considered toward a COMM toward elective requirements
        -   No credit in the program
            
            **NOTE**: *all* upper\-level \(300\- and 400\-level\) core requirements must be completed while enrolled in the BCom program\. It is not possible to apply transfer credit toward these upper\-level core requirements\. [See Requirements to Receive a Degree or Diploma\.](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/requirements-receive-degree-or-diploma)
            

After an assessment

-   You are not permitted to forfeit post\-secondary transfer credits that have been granted\.
-   Courses that are assessed to a direct equivalent COMM course will be updated on your UBC Workday Student\. No grade information is listed\. The grades you received for the course will not be reflected or used in the calculation of your UBC grades\. However, the Undergraduate Office will refer to the grade received from the original institution to determine if you have fulfill the [course minima required for declaring an option in Accounting or Finance](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/options)\.
-   You may decide to reduce your course load\. Note that reducing your course load may affect your eligibility to receive and retain scholarships, to reside in UBC residence, or to apply to a post\-graduation work permit\. Carefully review any conditions relevant to your personal circumstances to ensure your continued eligibility\.

title: Meet the Team
content_markdown:
### Visha Thamboo \(she/her\)

Director, Student Engagement & Development

**About Visha:** My role as Director, Student Engagement and Development is to focus on orientation planning and transitioning BCom students to UBC Sauder\. I also strive to build programming that fosters student leadership and involvement, both in and outside of the classroom\. I graduated from UBC with a BA in International Relations in 2016, where I loved creating meaningful experiences and interactions for my peers through Orientations, Residence Life, the Student Leadership Conference and student clubs\. I loved it so much that I decided to make a career out of it\! With my experience of hosting small intimate events, to large\-scale Orientations, I hope to help you re\-imagine your degree and push you to make the most of your time here at UBC Sauder\. **Fun Fact:** Giraffes are my favourite animal\!

### Lana To \(she/her\)

Manager, Student Engagement and Onboarding

**About Lana:** My role is to support BCom, DAP, and RHL graduate students to ensure a seamless transition to UBC Sauder, helping them kickstart and flourish within their own academic journey\! Before taking on this role, I was an Academic Advisor at OSAS and worked as Student Information Support and Academic Advisor at the UBC School of Kinesiology\. I hold a BKIN and MEd in Higher Education from UBC\. 

**Fun Fact:** I pick dessert over any other food any day\. I am a huge dessert lover\. 

### Hammond Yau \(they/them\)

Student Engagement and Development Advisor

**About Hammond:** I’m one of the Student Engagement & Development Advisors on the team\. I look after the Spark and community building events in Sauder\! I graduated from UBC with a BA in Psychology and also completed my Diploma in Adult Learning and Higher Education\. 

-   Learn more about [The Spark](https://www.ubcsauderspark.com/)\!  
-   Follow us on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/thesparkubc) \(@thesparkubc\) 

**Fun Fact:** Average daily screen time is 8\.5 hours\.

### Elsa Doxtdator\-Jansson \(she/her\)

Indigenous Student Engagement Advisor

**About Elsa:** My role as Indigenous Student Engagement Advisor is to support Indigenous Sauder students through creating programming that builds community and uplifts Indigenous students' personal and professional development\. Before joining OSAS team, I was the Program Manager for the Indigenous Business Leadership Executive MBA at Simon Fraser University\. I graduated from UBC Sauder with a BCom Specializing in Marketing and a Concentration in Sustainability and Social Impact\. 

  
**Fun Fact:** I volunteer as a ski instructor with Indigenous youth in Whistler\!

### Madeleine Kennedy \(she/her\)

Student Engagement and Development Advisor

**About Madeleine:** My role as a Student Engagement and Development Advisor is to support BCom students in building meaningful connections at Sauder\. I lead Imagine Day programming to welcome new students and support their transition, and I oversee case competitions, helping students develop their skills through experiential learning\. As a UBC Sauder alumna, I’m passionate about helping students make the most of their time here\.

**Fun Fact:** I don’t know how to whistle\.

### Stanley Turner Fowler \(they/them\)

Student Engagement and Development Advisor

**About Stanley:** I focus on awards, Student Experience Grants, and supporting students in our Bachelor \+ Master of Management and Diploma in Accounting programs\. I am passionate about building a sense of community while improving accessibility and inclusion\. I hold a BA in International Relations from King's College London and a Master of Management from UBC Sauder\. After working in management consulting, I returned to UBC Sauder, where in my previous role I helped to coordinate events and courses for graduate students\. I love being a part of such a kind, curious, and ambitious community\!

Fun Fact: I once helped to open Tower Bridge in London, UK \(where I grew up\)\! 

### Mason Margotta \(he/him\)

Student Engagement & Development Advisor

**About Mason:** My role as a Student Engagement & Development Advisor is to create an exciting and informative Opening Week for our graduate students in the Robert H\. Lee Graduate School, and to advise the Graduate Student Societies\. I was involved all over campus here at UBC when I was a student, working in the AMS, the Residence Hall Association, and Residence Life\. Since graduating UBC in 2017 with a BA in Asian Studies, I have worked in Residence Life, the Faculty of Arts, and Sauder, as well as brief journey to the island to work at UVic\.

**Fun Fact:** I own nearly 200 board games\! 

### Nafiza Ali \(she/her\)

Embedded Counsellor

**About Nafiza:** My role as the Embedded Counsellor is to support Sauder students in navigating the challenges of university while fostering resilience, wellbeing, and academic success through individual counselling, workshops and outreaches\. Before this role, I was a Wellness Advisor with Counselling Services and helped students with short term counselling and getting connected to resources both on and off campus\. I hold a BSc in Psychology and a MA in Counselling Psychology\.   
  
**Fun Fact:** I once competed in a beauty pageant\.

title: Academic Progress Report (APR)
content_markdown:
## Glossary

-   APR: Academic Progress Report
-   OAP: Overall Academic Progress
-   In excess: Extra Courses
-   Override: Manual update completed by OSAS
-   Didn’t Match: Course falls outside of academic requirements for your program
-   Didn’t Satisfy: Failed or repeated courses, or course falls outside of academic requirements for your program
-   In Progress: Course in progress \(grade not yet available\)
-   Credits Defined: Total number of credits needed for your degree
-   Requirements effective date: The date you were admitted to the program or declared your option
-   Class Standing: Year level

## What is Academic Progress Report \(APR\)?

Your personalized APR in Workday Student is a tool to keep track of your degree requirements and credits\. UBC’s degree audit tool displays your academic requirements as listed on the corresponding UBC Academic Calendar entries for your program and your progression in the program\.

### Attention: APR Limitations

The APR has limitations and should be used in combination with our [Course Planning Worksheets](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-tool) and [Elective Checklist](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/elective-requirements) for degree planning\. Refer to the important considerations listed below for additional information related to the APR, and for issues you may find with your APR\.

Be sure to check the [Elective Checklist](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/elective-requirements) for electives not for credit in the BCom program\.

## Reading Your Academic Progress Report

### Academic Progress Wheel

The Academic Progress Wheel shows you an estimate of the percentage of academic requirements you have completed for your program\. An academic requirement may be a single course or a group of courses\. There is one wheel for each program of study\. A program of study can be an option, co\-op, or, in some cases, a minor\. You will only see one wheel for your primary option and a wheel for co\-op if you are completing co\-op\.

The Academic Progress Wheel only provides a partial estimate of your progress toward degree completion\. **Because of this,** OSAS will not use this wheel to assess your graduation requirements, as it is not a reliable indicator of your full progression toward degree completion\.

**Academic Progress Wheel and CO\-OP**

The wheel for co\-op will only show "Satisfied" after all co\-op requirements have been completed\. Until then, the wheel will show "0 Satisfied\." BUCS CPSC co\-op courses are currently not applying correctly on the APR\. These courses will be found in Unused Registrations\.

### Key Components of Your APR

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Unused Registration** | Unused registrations are courses you have completed or registered in that are not currently counting toward satisfying your academic requirements\. Unused registrations include courses not for credit in the BCom program, repeated or failed courses, or extra courses taken that are not needed to fulfill BCom requirements\. |
| **Overall Academic Progress \(OAP\)** | The OAP section shows the total number of credits you need to complete for your degree\. This section of the report counts the total number of credits in progress and completed, regardless of whether or not they satisfy particular degree requirements\. Credits in Progress are included in Credits Satisfying\. A status of "Satisfied" for the OAP is not necessarily indicative of degree completion\. Do not rely on the OAP for an accurate number of remaining credits or degree completion\. |
| **Program Requirements** | Each program of study will have a table that shows the academic requirements for that program\. For each of these requirements, you will find the status of your progress, the remaining number of credits or courses required, the registrations used, the academic period when you took the course, and your letter grade earned\. The requirement will not show Satisfied until the entire requirement is complete\. In Progress indicates the requirement is in the process of being completed\. The Remaining column indicates any remaining requirement\. Please refer to your program requirements on [myBCom](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/program-requirements) and the [Course Planning\.](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-worksheets) |
| **Electives** | Prior to declaring your option, the total number of elective credits displayed in the APR is 42 credits\. After declaring Operations and Logistics, which requires 45 elective credits, an additional 3\-credit Commerce or non\-Commerce at 300 level or higher elective requirement will appear in your APR\. As the elective requirement for Global Supply Chain and Logistics Management is 39 credits, after declaring your option, the 3\-credit Commerce or non\-Commerce at 300 level or higher elective requirement will be waived for you\. All other options require 42 elective credits\. For electives planning, refer to our [Elective Checklist](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/elective-requirements) and use it in combination with the [Course Planning Worksheets\.](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-worksheets) |
| **Option Requirements** | Option requirements will not appear in the APR until your option has been declared\. For option requirements refer to [myBCom](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/options) and use in combination with the [Course Planning Worksheets\.](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-worksheets) |

### Important Considerations 

**Transfer Credit**

  
If you received transfer credits, the credits awarded can be viewed in Workday Student under Academics > Transfer Credits\.  
Transfer credits that have been given a specific UBC course subject and code \(e\.g\., MATH\_V 100\) which matches an APR requirement will automatically apply in the APR\.

COMM\_V unassigned transfer credits \(e\.g\., COMM 2nd\) must be reviewed by the UGO to determine if they can be used in the program\. An override may be needed to exclude or apply the credit correctly in the APR\.

Transfer credit assigned NC \(e\.g\., MATH 1NC, STAT 2NC, COMM 1NC\) is typically not for credit in the BCom program\. An exception is year 2 and 3 transfer students with COMM 1NC credit for IB Business Management HL or A\-Level Business Studies may use the credit toward electives\. UBCO transfer students may use only one of MGMT 100 and COMM 1NC\.

**Transfer Students**

  
Transfer students often require multiple overrides in the APR\. Overrides should be completed by the Term 1 deadline to add or drop a course without a W\. More information on transfer credits and how to submit a transfer credit assessment can be found [here\.](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment-program-requirements/general-program-requirements/transfer-students)  

**Viewing an Override**

  
Students will know an override has occurred if "Override Assigned" appears next to the requirement in your APR\. By clicking on "Override Assigned," you can view the comments associated with the override\. If an override has occurred in your OAP, you will see an Override Assigned column and can view the override by clicking on the magnifying glass symbol\.  

**COMM\_V 101 Override for Transfer Students**

  
COMM\_V 101 is not required for transfer students\. In lieu, transfer students will complete 3 additional credits of Commerce or Non\-Commerce courses at any level\. In your APR, you will see the additional elective has been applied to COMM\_V 101 as an override\.  

**APR Refresh after Registration Change**

  
It may take up to 24 hours after adding or dropping a course for your APR to refresh and for the change to display in your APR\.  

  

**Issues with “One of” Requirement**

  
If your option includes a requirement of completing one or two courses from a list of possible courses, they may be incorrectly applied to the option requirement and to the elective requirement\. In other words, the same course\(s\) will appear in two areas on your APR\. You cannot double count the same 3\-credit course toward your option and your elective requirements\.  

**Electives**

  
Your electives will not show Satisfied until the entire requirement is complete\. A status of In Progress indicates the requirement is in progress but isn’t necessarily fulfilled\. If the Status is In Progress and the Remaining column indicates Minimum Combination Required, the requirement is not being fulfilled\.  

**Courses Not Displayed in APR**

If a requirement has been met, excess courses fulfilling the requirement may not be displayed in the APR or in unused registration\.

**In\-Progress Excess Issue**

  
There may be some "In Progress" courses that appear in the "Unused Registrations" of your APR, even though they are intended to count towards a specific requirement\. Once the course is completed, the system should apply the course to the requirement\.  

**Residency Rule Edits**

  
Per the [UBC Calendar](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=3,40,0,0) at least 50% of the credits required for the program must be completed while registered in the program\. As the BCom program consists of 121 credits \(including one 1\-credit core course: COMM\_V 202\), 61 credits must be completed while in the BCom program and up to 60 credits completed prior to admission to the BCom program may apply\. In the case of BUCS, 64 credits must be completed while in the BCom program\. Go Global exchange credits completed after admission to the BCom program are eligible toward the minimum\. To ensure the appropriate number of credits are completed in the program, the APR for transfer students following the residency rule will be edited to exclude excess transfer credit\.  

**Exchange Transfer Credit**

  
Overrides for transfer credit earned on exchange may be necessary to split credit between elective requirements or apply transfer credit to specific requirements\.  

The APR is programmed to allow a maximum of 60 transfer credits\. If you are a transfer student and the transfer credit earned prior to admission to the program combined with your exchange transfer credit exceeds 60 credits, overrides may be necessary to allow the excess exchange transfer credit to apply\.

  

**Special Topics Courses**

  
Special topics courses that fulfill specific requirements, such as option courses \(e\.g\., COMM\_V 486T can be used toward the Finance option\), will need to be manually updated on the APR\. These courses will appear in electives until the override is made\.  

**Six Credit Courses Fulfilling Two 3\-Credit requirements**

  
A limitation of the APR is that it is unable to automatically split 6\-credit courses to fulfill two separate 3\-credit requirements\. An override can be made to 6\-credit courses taken at UBC to apply 3 credits to two requirements \(e\.g\., COMM\_V 466\)\.  
For students following the old BCom program requirements \(including those who entered the program directly to Year 1 in September 2021 or earlier, transferred as a Year 2 student in September 2022 or earlier, or transferred as a Year 3 student in September 2023 or earlier\), and if you have 6 credits of ENGL\_V 1st being used to fulfill the ENGL\_V 112 requirement, it is not possible to split transfer credit to use towards two separate requirements\. As a workaround, your APR will be updated so that all 6 credits of ENGL\_V 1st will apply to ENGL\_V 112, and your electives will be reduced by 3 credits\.  

**Requirements Effective Date**

  
Depending on what year you are enrolled in the program, your academic requirements will vary\. Your program requirements are based on the program effective date on the APR\. Your requirements effective date is usually the date you were admitted to the program or declared your option\. If your effective date appears to be incorrect, please submit an APR feedback form so that it can be corrected\.  

## APR Feedback

If you notice any inaccuracies, errors, or other issues within your APR on Workday, please email [bcomquestions@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:bcomquestions@sauder.ubc.ca "mailto:bcomquestions@sauder.ubc.ca") with a detailed description of the issue so that it can be corrected\.

## APR & Your Year Level

Please select your year level below for further information

### Year 1 Students

Overrides for students with high school transfer credit should be completed by the Term 1 deadline to add or drop a course without a W\. After that time the year 1 requirements outlined in your APR should be accurate\. The APR has limitations and should be used in combination with our [Course Planning Worksheets](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-tool) and [Elective Checklist](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/elective-requirements) for degree planning\.

### Year 2 Students

Overrides for transfer students and continuing students should be completed by the Term 1 deadline to add or drop a course without a W\. After that time the year 1 and 2 requirements outlined in your APR should be accurate\.The APR has limitations and should be used in combination with our [Course Planning Worksheets](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-tool) and [Elective Checklist](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/elective-requirements) for degree planning\.

### Year 3 Students

Overrides for transfer students and continuing students should be completed by the Term 1 deadline to add or drop a course without a W\. If registration changes occur further overrides may be necessary and should be completed by the Term 2 deadline to add or drop a course without a W\. The APR has limitations and should be used in combination with our [Course Planning Worksheets](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-tool) and [Elective Checklist](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/elective-requirements) for degree planning\.

### Year 4 Students

Any remaining overrides should be completed by the Term 1 deadline to add or drop a course without a W\. After that time your APR should correctly reflect your academic progression, and we recommend that you take a moment to review it\. Be sure to check whether your elective status is showing Satisfied or In Progress\. If the Remaining column indicates Minimum Combination Required your electives are not being satisfied\. If registration changes occur further overrides may be necessary and should be completed by the Term 2 deadline to add or drop a course without a W\. Please read the information on our website prior to viewing your APR\. The APR has limitations and **must** be used in combination with our Course Planning Worksheets and Elective Checklist\.

## Academic Progress Report \(APR\) FAQs 

**Why can’t I register in a course even though the APR says I have the pre\-requisite?**

Workday looks for the exact course code on your record to match with the pre\- or co\-requisite\. So, if your transfer credits are not an exact match to a UBC course—but an override was assigned so that your transfer credit is applying towards a UBC course—then you can register for the course, but you will need to contact the department who owns the course \(e\.g\., Math Department, OSAS\) to request a registration waiver to enable you to register yourself in the course\.

**Why is my co\-op APR wheel not moving although I have completed some of the requirements?**

The wheel will only show Satisfied after all requirements have been completed\. Until then, the wheel will show 0 Satisfied\.

title: Investment Banking Access Pathway
content_markdown:
The **Investment Banking Access Pathway \(IB\-AP\)** is a program designed to help 2nd\-year students in the Early Start to the Finance Option stand out in the competitive investment banking internship recruitment process\. It addresses the growing trend of finance employers—especially banks and investment firms—recruiting interns as early as midway through students’ second year\.

Participants will demonstrate their potential across a set of key criteria vetted by employers\. Those who meet the grade requirement and at least seven of the eight criteria will be included in a **UBC** **Sauder BCom resume book**, which will be distributed to **top financial employers such as CIBC, RBC, TD, BMO, and Scotiabank by January 2027**\.

Students selected for the resume book will also receive structured interview preparation, including technical training, mock interviews with finance professionals, and peer mentorship from upper\-year students with IB internship experience\.

### Eligibility

Students must meet the following requirements to participate in IB\-AP:

-   Be entering **Year 2** for the first time in **Fall 2026**\.
-   Be registered in the **Early Start to the Finance \(ESTF\) Option**\*\.  
    
    \*Click here to learn more about ESTF Option: [https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/early\-start\-to\-the\-finance\-option](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/early-start-to-the-finance-option)
    

### How to Participate

1.  Register in the Early Start to the Finance \(ESTF\) Option
2.  Enroll in the IB\-AP Canvas course, where detailed instructions on program application and evidence submission will be provided\.
3.  Submit evidence as instructed\. Guidance and support will be available during the evidence submission process; however, you will need to demonstrate strong self\-learning and self\-initiative to meet the criteria in the process\.
    

### Important Dates

Canvas site open date: **September 8, 2026**

Registration Timeline: **September 8 \- September 30, 2026**

Last day of evidence submission: **November 2, 2026**

**Enroll here: [CWL Login Required](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/ELGMW4)** 

### Selection Criteria

Participants are invited to demonstrate their potential by submitting evidence across eight key selection criteria we previously validated with employers\. 

Students who meet **at least seven criteria and with a minimum average grade of 80%** are included in this **Resume Book**\. 

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Relevant Work Experience:** Demonstrate experience in a professional work environment\.
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Provide a current resume aligning with the IB\-AP resume template\.
    -   Relevant work experience: e\.g\., internship/part\-time work in finance, accounting, sales, client\-facing roles in a corporate setting, or entrepreneurship experience\.
    -   **Note:** IB\-AP resume template will be provided on the IB\-AP canvas page\.

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Strong grades in Relevant Courses:**
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Provide evidence of strong academic performance, particularly a minimum average grade of 80% in the following courses:
    
    -   COMM 190 – Introduction to Quantitative Decision Making
    -   COMM 293 – Financial Accounting
    -   COMM 295 – Managerial Economics
    -   COMM 298 – Introduction to Finance
    
    **Note:** A minimum average grade of 80% is a must\-have for inclusion in the resume book, while a minimum average grade of 80% in all above courses is a criterion met\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Finance\-learning initiative:** Demonstrate interest in and aptitude for finance through preparatory courses or self\-directed learning\.
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Provide certificates or proof of completion of a minimum of two courses, including financial modeling, Excel, valuation modeling, data analysis, M&A, private equity, leveraged finance, and venture capital\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Professionalism, Communication, and Work Ethic:** Demonstrate readiness for the professional world\.
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Professionalism, communication, and work ethic will be continuously evaluated through student participation and interactions in the program\.
    -   Attend **at least** **one** career coaching session with one of the Business Career Centre’s \(BCC\) Career Strategists to discuss their career goals\.
    -   Attend an Investment Banking Industry Panel event organized by the BCC and the Finance department\.

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Involvement with Finance Clubs:** Show active participation and leadership roles in finance\-related student clubs\.
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Provide evidence of club participation, such as a copy of job offers, information about specific club projects they worked on, or a statement from a club leader outlining their contributions\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Finance Competitions:** Participate in case competitions or challenges showcasing analytical thinking\.
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Provide proof of competition participation outside regular classroom activity \(registration, results, etc\.\)\.

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Networking Skills:** Demonstrate the ability to build relationships and connect with finance professionals\.
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Provide the names of **four finance industry professionals** you had coffee chats with\. Write a brief reflection \(max 50 words\) on one key learning from each conversation
    -   Attend **at least** **two** Company Recruitment Sessions organized by the BCC\.

- **Row 8**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Non\-Finance Extracurricular Activities:** Demonstrate they are well\-rounded individuals with discipline, time management skills, and the ability to balance academic responsibilities with other pursuits such as arts, sports, or volunteering\.
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Provide details about participation in extracurricular activities, including duration and roles/responsibilities\.

- **Row 9**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    (empty)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    (empty)

### Interview Preparation Support from IB\-AP

Students who qualify for the IB\-AP Resume Book receive targeted interview preparation to help them succeed in the competitive investment banking recruitment process:

-   **Instructor\-led Technical Training**  
    In January, students participate in mandatory online sessions delivered by Training the Street\.
-   **1\-on\-1 Mock Interviews**  
    Between January and March, students complete a mandatory mock interview with a finance professional through Wall Street Oasis\. These sessions simulate real IB interviews and offer actionable feedback\.
-   **Peer Networking & Knowledge Sharing**  
    In November, IBAP students are matched with upper\-year peers who have secured and/or completed IB summer internships\. These conversations offer insights from peers and help build confidence ahead of interviews\.

### Contact us

If you’re considering a career in investment banking or have questions about the IB\-AP program, we encourage you to reach out\. Whether you're unsure if the program is the right fit or need guidance on how to strengthen your profile, we’re here to help\.

Please reach out directly to Misa Zhang at [misa\.zhang@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:misa.zhang@sauder.ubc.ca)

title: COMM_V 386N - Climate Leadership, Innovation and Strategy
content_markdown:
Climate change is altering the context in which businesses operate\. This course examines the implications of climate risk, evolving policy frameworks, and emerging market opportunities for firms across sectors\. Students will assess how organizations respond through strategic choices and approaches to innovation\. The course also considers how to sustain meaningful climate action amid geopolitical uncertainty and competing global priorities\. Over the course of two weeks, students will engage in discussions, case studies, lectures, and connect with industry experts to better understand how climate change is shaping business today and in the future\.

### Learning Objectives

• Analyze the business implications of climate\-related risks, regulations, and policy shifts across different sectors and regions\.  
• Evaluate strategic and innovative responses businesses can adopt to address climate change while maintaining competitiveness\.  
• Develop leadership approaches that embed climate action into core business practices and decision\-making processes\.  
• Assess the relevance and resilience of climate strategies in the context of ongoing geopolitical and economic uncertainty\.

Note: COMM 386N will not be offered in 2026W\.

**Eligibility:** This course is open to all UBC students in any specialization in Years 3, 4 and 5

content_markdown:
