title: Academic Honours
content_markdown:
### Dean's List 

For 23W and prior, the words 'Dean's Honour Roll' will be placed on your transcript\. Starting 24W, the words 'Dean's Honour Roll' will be replaced with Dean's List\. The criteria of the Dean's List and the Dean's Honour Roll are the same as follows:

-   pass all courses
-   achieve an average of 80% or greater on all percentage\-graded courses taken during the winter session \(September to April\)\.
-   be registered in a minimum of 24 percentage\-graded credits\[1\] within the session\.\[2\] 

###### \[1\] Prior to May 2019, a minimum of 27 percentage\-graded credits was required\.

###### \[2\] If you're a Co\-op student and you're registered at UBC for only one term in the winter session because of a Co\-op placement, you must be in 12 percentage\-graded credits \(15 percentage\-graded credits prior to May 2019\) in your non\-Co\-op term to be eligible\. If you participate in an exchange program in the 2025 winter session or prior, your grades earned while on exchange will be included in the calculation\.

2019 Winter Session: Special consideration due to the COVID\-19 pandemic

To be eligible for the Dean’s Honour Roll in the 2019 Winter Session, you must:

-   pass all courses \(including courses taken for Cr/D/F; excluding late course withdrawals\)
-   be registered in a minimum of 24 credits \(percentage\-graded and Cr/D/F\) within the winter session \(Terms 1 and 2\)\[1\]
-   achieve an average of 80% or greater on **ONE OF**:
    -   all percentage\-graded courses taken during the winter session \(Terms 1 and 2\), **OR**

-   all Term 1 percentage\-graded courses if a minimum of 12 percentage\-graded credits were completed that term

###### \[1\] If you're a Co\-op student and you're registered at UBC for only one term in the winter session because of a Co\-op placement, you must be in 12 percentage\-graded credits in your non\-Co\-op term to be eligible\. If you participate in an exchange program, your grades earned while on exchange will be included in the calculation\.  

### Degree with Honours

The words 'with Honours' will be placed on your transcript and your degree certificate if you meet the following conditions:

-   achieve an average of 80% or greater on all senior\-level \(300 and 400\-level\) Commerce courses \(COMM\_V and COHR\_V\)\.\[1\] Senior\-level \(300 and 400\-level\) CPSC\_V courses are also included for students in the Combined Major in Business & Computer Science \(BUCS\)\. The average is calculated to 2 decimal points and is not rounded\. **EXCEPTION**:

-   If you **HAVE** Cr/D/F grades for any senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC for BUCS\) in 2019W Term 2, then **ALL** senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC\_V for BUCS\_V\) courses taken in 2019W Term 2 are **EXCLUDED** from your graduating average calculation\.\[2\]
-   If you **DO NOT HAVE** Cr/D/F grades for any senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC\_V for BUCS\_V\) in 2019W Term 2, then **ALL** senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC\_V for BUCS\_V\) courses taken in 2019W Term 2 are **INCLUDED** in your graduating average calculation\.

-   meet **ONE OF** the following credit requirements\[3,4\]:

-   24 percentage\-graded credits in the Winter Session of Year 3 or Year 4, **OR**
-   At least 24 credits in Year 3 or Year 4 in the 2019 Winter Session including 12 percentage\-graded credits in 2019W Term 1

###### \[1\] If you were registered in Year 2 or above during the 2014 Winter Session, COMM\_V 203 \(COMM\_V 392 equivalent\), COMM\_V 204 \(COMM\_V 399 equivalent\), and COMM\_V 205 \(COMM\_V 391 equivalent\) will be included in the calculation of your average\. If you were in Year 1 during the 2014 Winter Session and took any of COMM\_V 391, COMM\_V 392, COMM\_V 399 during the 2015 Summer Session or prior, your grades for those courses will not be used to determine eligibility to achieve a Degree with Honours\.

###### \[2\] If you have CR/D/F grades for any senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC\_V for BUCS\_V\) in 2019W Term 2 and you have taken a six\-credit percentage\-graded COMM\_V course during 2019W that spanned Terms 1 and 2 \(COMM\_V 466, COMM\_V 486W\), your percentage grade for the six\-credit course will be included in your graduating average calculation, however, it will be weighted for only 3 credits rather than 6 credits\.

###### \[3\] Students who graduated in May 2019 or prior were required to be registered in at least 27 percentage\-graded credits during the winter session in at least one of Year 3 or Year 4 of the program\. For those students in the Co\-op program and registered at UBC for only one term in the winter session because of a Co\-op placement, they had to have been in 15 percentage\-graded credits in their non\-Co\-op term to be eligible\.

###### \[4\] If you're a Co\-op student and you're registered at UBC for only one term in the winter session because of a Co\-op placement, you must be in 12 percentage\-graded credits in your non\-Co\-op term to be eligible\. If you participate in an exchange program in the 2025 winter session or prior, your grades earned while on exchange will be included in the calculation\.

**If you're unable to calculate your eligibility to achieve a Degree with Honours yourself, you can confirm your Honours status at the Office of Student Academic Services after May 19 for the spring ceremony and November 20 for the fall ceremony\.**

title: Specialized Academic Opportunities
content_markdown:
### Experience business in other cultures, make research strides, even come up with a new UBC course – there are many ways to enrich your degree experience and explore different career directions\.

### [Co\-op program](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/build-my-career/co-op-program)

Be ready to hit the ground running in your future career by combining your academic studies with practical, paid work experience in your chosen field\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/build-my-career/co-op-program)

### [International exchange](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/reach-globally/international-exchange)

Imagine studying business and immersing yourself in a different language and culture\. You can do it all as part of your UBC BCom\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/reach-globally/international-exchange)

### [Ch'nook Scholars program](http://www.sauder.ubc.ca/Programs/Chnook/Students/Chnook_Scholars)

If you're an Indigenous business student, join this program to access a range of benefits including tools and connections to help you succeed in your studies and career\.

[Learn more](http://www.sauder.ubc.ca/Programs/Chnook/Students/Chnook_Scholars)

### [UBC Portfolio Management Foundation](http://www.sauder.ubc.ca/Faculty/Divisions/Finance_Division/Programs/PMF_Program)

Be part of a select team and add value to a $9 million portfolio of stocks and bonds\. Guided by mentors, qualified Finance students aiming for a career in capital markets can learn to manage the PMF Endowment Fund\.

[Learn more](http://www.sauder.ubc.ca/Faculty/Divisions/Finance_Division/Programs/PMF_Program)

### [UBCO cross campus mobility](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/specialized-academic-opportunities/ubco-cross-campus-mobility)

Expand your BCom experience by taking a term of Management courses in the Faculty of Management at UBC’s Okanagan campus in Kelowna, BC\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/specialized-academic-opportunities/ubco-cross-campus-mobility)

### [UBC SWIFT: UBC Sauder Women\+ in Finance Training](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/swift)

Through connections between academics and practitioners in finance, students reconcile practical portfolio management with rigorous academic theory\.

[Learn more](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/swift)

### [Sauder LIFT](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/LIFT)

Students travel to developing countries and deliver a series of workshops to empower local participants to start their own businesses for economic betterment\.

[Learn more](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/LIFT)

### [UBC Sauder Philanthropy Program](http://www.sauder.ubc.ca/About/Sauder_Philanthropy_Program)

Learn the practice and impact of philanthropy through exposure to local philanthropists and community leaders, and opportunities for hands\-on experience\.

[Learn more](http://www.sauder.ubc.ca/About/Sauder_Philanthropy_Program)

### [Directed studies](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/directedstudiesformpdf)

Complete an independent project under the supervision of a faculty member and receive course credit\. Once you have found an instructor agreeable to supervising your project, complete the Directed Studies application form and submit it to the Office of Student Academic Services for approval and registration\.

[Download an application](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/directedstudiesformpdf)

### [Student directed seminars](http://students.ubc.ca/success/student-directed-seminars)

Is there a subject you’re passionate about, but that isn’t offered at UBC? Why not propose your own course? Under the guidance of a faculty sponsor, you can take charge of your own learning experience in a small, self\-directed group\.

[Learn more](http://students.ubc.ca/success/student-directed-seminars)

title: Minors and Concentrations
content_markdown:
### Allowed Combinations

UBC Sauder BCom students have the flexibility to customize their degree by combining options, concentrations, and non\-Commerce minors\. You may pursue any of the following combinations:

-   Two options and one non\-Commerce minor
    
-   Two options and one concentration
    
-   One option and two concentrations
    
-   One option, one concentration, and one non\-Commerce minor
    

These combinations allow you to tailor your BCom experience to suit your academic interests and career goals\.

### Credit/D/Fail Restrictions

You **cannot** take courses required for **minors or concentrations** on a Credit/D/Fail basis\. You may take elective courses for Credit/D/Fail **as long as they do not fulfill** a requirement for an option, minor, or concentration\. Read more about Credit/D/Fail at [mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/creditdfail](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/1812#creditdfail)\.

## Minors

A minor is an optional component of your BCom program that requires completion of at least 18 credits of upper level courses in a single subject area outside of Commerce\. The courses taken for a minor are counted toward elective requirements in the BCom degree\.

**Please note**: The minor you wish to pursue must be available to BCom students\.

[More about minors](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/minors-and-concentrations/minor-arts-or-science)  

## Concentrations

A concentration is an optional set of related courses beyond your core degree requirements, separate from your option\. The 12 credits taken for a concentration are counted toward elective requirements in the BCom degree\.

[Business Analytics concentration](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/business-analytics-concentration)  

[Business Law concentration](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/business-law-concentration)  

[International Business concentration](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/international-business-concentration)  

[Sustainability and Social Impact concentration](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sustainability-and-social-impact-concentration)  

## Minor in Commerce

Enrolled in another degree program at UBC? Learn the fundamentals of business by taking 9 to 18 credits of upper level Commerce courses \(requirements vary by Faculty\)\. Flexible course delivery options and summer sections allow minor requirements to fit within the schedule of your primary field of study\.

[More about the Minor on Commerce](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/minors-and-concentrations/minor-commerce)

title: Minor in Arts or Science
content_markdown:
### A minor is a good way to broaden your studies, complement your option, have another subject area recognized on your official transcript, and expand your employment opportunities\.

### Minor in Arts

If you plan to complete a Minor in Arts, you must meet with an Arts Departmental Advisor who can assist you in completing a minor study plan\.

[Minor study plan](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/media/minor_study_plan_-_form.pdf)  

Once you have your minor study plan approved by the Arts Departmental Advisor, submit the approved study plan to the UBC Sauder Office of Student Academic Services\.

The minor designation will be added to your academic record at the time of graduation if you have successfully completed all requirements\.

Visit the UBC Calendar to check the academic requirements of a minor in a particular subject area\.

[Minor requirements at UBC](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=12,197,282,56)  

### Minor in Law and Society

If you're planning to complete a Minor in Law and Society \(LASO\), you must complete and submit your minor study plan or the Minor Program in Law and Society advising form, available from the LASO program advisor, to the UBC Sauder Office of Student Academic Services before you start the required introductory course, [LASO 204](https://courses.students.ubc.ca/cs/main?pname=subjarea&tname=subjareas&req=1&dept=LASO)\.

[LASO Minor advising form](https://laso.arts.ubc.ca/files/2019/05/Advising_FillableLASO-20190529.pdf)  

Once the Law and Society minor designation has been added to your record, you will be able to register in the course and receive all communications and updates about the program\.

[LASO minor requirements](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=12,197,282,1448)  

### Minor in Science

If you plan to complete a Minor in Science, you must meet with a Science Departmental Advisor who can assist you in completing a minor study plan\.

[Minor study plan](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/media/minor_study_plan_-_form.pdf)  

Once you have your minor study plan approved by the Science Departmental Advisor, submit the approved study plan to Office of Student Academic Services\.

The minor designation will be added to your academic record at the time of graduation if you have successfully completed all requirements\.

Please be aware that space in science courses is limited\. Admission to a Science minor does not guarantee access to courses agreed upon for that minor\.

Visit the UBC Calendar to check the academic requirements of a minor in a particular subject area\.

[Minor requirements at UBC](https://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=12,215,410,410)  

### Minor in Data Science

If you plan to complete a Minor in Data Science, you’ll need to apply through the [Data Science Minor \(DSM\) website](https://datascience.ubc.ca/minor) when applications open in April\. The site outlines all key details, including admission criteria and required courses—make sure to review these carefully\.

BCom students can use the Minor Study Plan form for planning and meet with a Data Science Minor Advisor for guidance\. However, DSM advisors will not sign the form, as a signed plan is not required for the application\. Students only need to submit the online application, as outlined on the [DSM website](https://datascience.ubc.ca/minor)\. Before contacting the DSM team, check the FAQ section for helpful information\.

[Minor study plan](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/media/minor_study_plan_-_form.pdf)  

If you're admitted, the DSM admissions team will notify OSAS, and the minor will be added to your Program of Study record in Workday Student \(Please note that process is different from the other Arts and Science minors\)\.

The minor designation will be added to your academic record at the time of graduation if you have successfully completed all requirements\.

[DSM Requirements at UBC website](https://datascience.ubc.ca/minor)  

### Frequently asked questions about minors

Can I double count International Business and minor credits?

A maximum of six credits may be double\-counted between a minor and International Business option course requirements\.

Will a minor appear on my transcript or degree?

If you have completed the required courses for a minor by graduation, “Minor in \[subject\]” will be denoted on your transcript, however the minor designation will not appear on your degree certificate\. Make sure that you have submitted your approved study plan for your minor to the UBC Sauder Office of Student Academic Services \([bcomquestions@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:bcomquestions@sauder.ubc.ca) / HA 165\) by February prior to May graduation or by August prior to November graduation\.

title: Minor in Commerce
content_markdown:
### Welcome to the Minor in Commerce Program at UBC Sauder School of Business\!  

As you embark on this exciting journey, you are joining a community that values integrity, collaboration, and innovation\. At UBC Sauder, we believe in fostering not only academic excellence but also a strong sense of responsibility to the world around us\. Your experience here will challenge you to think critically, act ethically, and develop leadership skills that can shape the future of business\.  

We look forward to seeing you thrive as you take on new challenges, explore opportunities, and leave a positive impact both on campus and beyond\. Welcome to UBC Sauder, where your potential meets endless possibilities\!  

#### **Why a Minor in Commerce?**  

A Minor in Commerce equips you with foundational business knowledge that complements your major\. Whether you are studying Arts, Science, or Engineering, business skills such as accounting, marketing, finance, and management are universally applicable and enhance your employability across various fields\.  

Through case studies, projects, and real\-world applications, you will gain hands\-on experience that prepares you for the workforce\. UBC Sauder emphasizes practical learning that helps you develop problem\-solving skills and an entrepreneurial mindset\.  

The program also connects you with a diverse group of peers, faculty, and industry professionals\. UBC Sauder’s strong connections to the business community mean you can develop meaningful relationships and expand your professional network\.  

Courses in the Minor in Commerce program

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [COMR\_V 329](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-329) | Principles of Organizational Behaviour |
| [COMR\_V 398](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-398) | Introduction to Business Processes and Operations |
| [COMR\_V 457](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-457) | Fundamentals of Financial Accounting |
| [COMR\_V 458](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-458) | Fundamentals of Managerial Accounting |
| [COMR\_V 465](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-465) | Marketing Management |
| [COMR\_V 473](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-473) | Business Finance |
| [COMR\_V 493](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-493) | Strategic Management in Business |

###### Note: The eligibility to apply transfer credits, including [course equivalencies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/equivalency-search) taken at UBC, towards Minor in Commerce requirements vary by faculty\. Consult your [home faculty](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising#undergraduate-academic-advising) for additional information\. Students in the Faculty of Arts can refer to details [here](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/commerce-minor/)\.

### Achieve academic success  

Many of the Minor in Commerce courses are offered in a [Flexible Learning](https://flexible.learning.ubc.ca/) format to allow you to take them along with your own program requirements\.  

Students are encouraged to actively participate, seek out diverse perspectives, and build relationships that support both personal and professional growth\. Active participation enhances learning by deepening understanding, sharpening critical thinking, and fostering engagement with course material\. It also promotes interaction with peers and instructors, helping to clarify doubts, apply concepts in real\-time, and improve retention\. Additionally, participation strengthens communication skills, boosts confidence, and contributes to a collaborative learning environment\. By embracing values such as respect, accountability, and inclusivity, you help cultivate the vibrant and dynamic culture at UBC Sauder\. 

##### **What is required of you?**  

Know your rights and responsibilities: It is up to you to take responsibility for your goals, values, and academic decision making\. Knowing about the policies and regulations that apply to you as a UBC student will help you to better plan your studies and make smart decisions toward achieving academic success\.  

### [Academic integrity](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/academic-integrity)

Academic integrity is honest and responsible scholarship\. As a university student, you are expected to submit original work and give credit to other peoples' ideas\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/academic-integrity)

### [Attendance](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/attendance)

As a UBC student, you are expected to regularly attend all of your classes, including associated lectures, labs, tutorials, seminars, and any other course\-related activities\. Both excused and unexcused absences may be taken into account when evaluating your overall attendance\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/attendance)

### [Professionalism and Code of Conduct](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/statement-of-professionalism-and-code-conduct)

At UBC Sauder, professional behaviour aligns with the school’s guiding values – rigour, respect, and responsibility\. These values help shape our behaviour both inside the classroom and in our communities to inspire and guide students, staff, and faculty\. Please acquaint yourself with the expectations for professional behaviour and the consequences of unprofessional conduct to help ensure a positive and respectful environment for everyone\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/statement-of-professionalism-and-code-conduct)

> ### Thinking of applying? 
> 
> If you are completing a program other than the Bachelor of Commerce, you may be eligible to complete a Minor in Commerce\. Contact your [home faculty](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising#undergraduate-academic-advising) and consult the [UBC Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools) for further information regarding eligibility, course requirements, and application procedures\.  
> 
> Students in the Faculty of Arts can refer to information [here](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/commerce-minor/)\.
> 
> ### Flexible Learning
> 
> **What is it?**
> 
> In some courses, you will spend 20\-70% of your time studying with online learning materials in preparation for fewer scheduled in\-person classes\. Flexible sections are labeled with the Delivery Mode ‘Hybrid Learning’ on the course schedule\.
> 
> **What are the benefits?**
> 
> With Flexible Learning, most of your learning happens outside the classroom\. That allows for more time in class to help you put ideas into action and develop the critical thinking and analytical skills today’s employers demand\. This delivery method gives you far more flexibility for combining a Minor in Commerce with your other studies\.
> 
> **Who is it best suited for?**
> 
> This format is ideal for independent students who are self\-motivated, self\-regulated and comfortable with less face\-to\-face interaction\.
> 
> [Learn more about Flex](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/about-ubc-sauder/learning-services/learning-design/flexible-learning-initiative)  
> 
> ### Looking for commerce courses to take in summer?
> 
> Explore Commerce courses available to all undergraduate students this summer\! Check out the list of courses and their details in the document below\.
> 
> [View Course Details](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/6452/download)

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/minors-and-concentrations/minor-commerce)

### Learning and Studying Resources

In the following section, you'll find a variety of learning and studying resources to support your academic needs\. Click through the links to access toolkits, resource guides, and blog posts that can help you further your learning as a Minor in Commerce student\.

### Learning and studying

Everyone has their own way of learning effectively, so what's yours? Take the [learning quiz](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/tutoring-and-advice/approach-to-learning-self-assessment/) to gain some insight into your typical approach to learning and which methods may work for you\!

Tutoring services

The Alma Mater Society \(AMS\) provides tutoring for first and second year students\. Become more confident in tackling academic challenges by attending AMS group tutoring, a free drop\-in service available for all UBC students\. Paid private tutoring is also available\.

[Search tutoring sessions](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/student-services/tutoring/)  

Studying and reviewing

You may have noticed that the way you used to study might not be as effective as it was before\. The Commerce Mentorship Program \(CMP\) holds review sessions for various courses which includes review packages and solutions to common questions\. These review sessions are open to all BCom students and information regarding upcoming sessions can be found on the CMP Facebook page\.

[Attend review sessions](https://www.facebook.com/ubccmp)   

Additional resources:

Note\-taking methods

Taking good notes during class will help you better understand the course material\. Everybody has a different approach to studying, so what's the best method for you? 

[Access the Taking Notes Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/taking-notes/)  

Additional reading:

-   [UBC Life blog: How to take rock\-solid notes for online lectures](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/take-rock-solid-notes-online-lectures)

Critical thinking

A skill for learning, but also for life\. Critical thinking is one of the skills you will revisit most throughout your academic and professional career, as it helps us analyze, assess, and improve the ways we tackle a situation\.

[Access the Critical Thinking Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/thinking-critically/)

As student, you will need to know how to navigate the digital resources at UBC to improve your learning experience\. Watch and learn how to utilize online learning platforms like Canvas and Zoom, reformat digital documents, and more\!

[Watch videos on fundamental skills](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/tech-support/foundational-skills/)

Office hours

Going to your professor or TA during office hours is a great way to get to know your instructors and get some extra help\. It can be scary to ask your professor questions but know that they want to help you learn and succeed in their course\. Discover a few tips to help you feel prepared and get the most out of your professor’s office hours\.

Assignment calculator

Assignment Calculators are time management tools that will break down research or lab assignments into a series of manageable steps, *and* give you expert tips for success\. 

[Calculate how much time you need for assignments](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/tutoring-and-advice/assignment-calculators/)  

Group projects

-   [UBC Life blog: How to tackle multiple choice based exam](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/tackle-multiple-choice-tests)

Although, these two types of exams or a mix of the two are popular with instructors, you could also encounter exams with questions that require answers in the following responses: true/false, fill in the blanks, quantitive or problem solving, or short answers\. Exams can also be online, oral, open book, or take home\. Instructors may also develop an exam in a format not listed above\. In any case, try to give yourself enough time to study the materials and get a good night's sleep the day before so that you are prepared for any questions that may come your way\.

> ### Being a university student
> 
> Overcoming challenges
> 
> It's completely normal for a student to face learning challenges in university and what's important is learning how you can overcome them\. In this article, learn about the five most common challenges you may face as a student, from failing a course to keeping up with class, and what steps you can take to combat them\.
> 
> [Learn more about overcoming challenges](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/tutoring-and-advice/learning-challenges/)  
> 
> ### Reading and writing
> 
> Reading textbooks
> 
> How much reading do you do as a university student? A lot\! So make sure you're reading your textbooks in the most effective way\.
> 
> [Access the Reading Textbooks Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/reading-textbooks/)  
> 
> Writing
> 
> You can't escape writing in university\. Effective writing skills will take you a long way and help you nail your assignments, papers, and exams\.
> 
> [Access the Writing Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/writing/)  
> 
> Additional resources:
> 
> -   [CLC: Writing coaching](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/get-better-grades/communication)
> -   [https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/get\-better\-grades/communication](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/get-better-grades/communication)[UBC Library: Centre for Writing and Scholarly Comunication](https://writing.library.ubc.ca/undergraduates/)

> -   [https://www\.library\.ubc\.ca/](https://www.library.ubc.ca/)[WriteAway](https://writeaway.ca/connect)
> 
> Additional reading:
> 
> -   [UBC Life blog: 5 things student tend to miss when proofreading](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/5-things-miss-when-proofreading)
> -   [UBC Library: Library skills tutorials Canvas course](http://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/F3GKXM)
> -   [UBC Library: Citation tutorial Canvas course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/B7AYEN)
> 
> Research support
> 
> Strengthen your work\! Take advantage of the highly resourceful information and professional research support from the David Lam Management Research Library, located in the Canaccord Learning Commons\. 
> 
> [Find research supports](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/get-better-grades/research-support)  
> 
> Academic integrity
> 
> Academic integrity means that you are honest and accountable in your work as a scholar\. Understand plagiarism and how you can avoid it by learning about student integrity and ethics\.
> 
> [Learn more about academic integrity](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/resource-guides/understand-academic-integrity/)  
> 
> Additional resources:
> 
> -   [UBC Academic Integrity website](https://academicintegrity.ubc.ca/student-start/)
> 
> Additional reading:
> 
> -   [UBC Life blog: Academic integrity](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/academic-integrity)
> 
> ### Time and self\-management
> 
> Time management
> 
> Wasting a lot of time online? Pulling too many all\-nighters? Time management is key to achieving all your goals whilst finding time for yourself, which is especially important as a university student\. Learn how you can manage your time effectively and learn about the different methods you can adopt to make the most out of your time\.
> 
> [Access the Managing Your Time Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/managing-your-time/)   
> 
> Additional reading:
> 
> -   [UBC Life blog: Pinpointing and perfecting your productivity zone](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/pinpointing-perfecting-productivity-zone)
> -   [UBC Science Distillation blog: 80/20 \- How to Increase Your Productivity by Doing Less](https://science.ubc.ca/students/blog/how-to-increase-your-productivity-by-doing-less)
> 
> Concentration and focus
> 
> Believe it or not, finding focus is a skill that one can improve on\. It's easy to get distracted, especially with everything that goes on in a student's life\. Learn how you can avoid these distractions and settle yourself into a rhythm of focus, so that you can study, absorb material, and perform better in school\.
> 
> [Learn about strategies to help you focus better](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/cultivating-the-ability-to-focus/)  
> 
> Motivation
> 
> Wondering how to build motivation and discipline throughout the school year? Check out this resource guide for tips and helpful resources to stay on track\!
> 
> [Read the Motivation Guide](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/resource-guides/motivation-resource-guide/)   
> 
> Additional reading
> 
> -   [UBC Science Distillation blog: Struggling to Find the Motivation?](https://science.ubc.ca/students/blog/struggling-find-motivation)
> 
> Procrastination
> 
> It's easy to fall off track and get stuck in a pattern of procrastination\. To avoid the stress and anxiety that follows, here are some strategies to help get you started and trick yourself into taking action\! Below are some of the best practices you can try out:
> 
> -   Pomodoro technique: do uninterrupted work for 25 minutes, take a 5 minute break, then repeat 3 times and take a longer 20 minute break
> -   5 minutes: You can do almost anything for 5 minutes\. Start an assignment, start reading a chapter, review your lecture notes, etc\. You’ll find that after 5 minutes, you either want to keep plugging away at it, you’re almost done whatever you set out to do, or you’re really not into it\. But at least you took action for those 5 minutes\.
> -   Sounds silly, but put your phone somewhere you can’t get to it: give it to your neighbour in residence, charge it across the room, or turn it off so it’s more challenging to check it\. At least keep it out of arm’s reach\.
> 
> [View strategies to help with procrastination](https://academicservices.engineering.ubc.ca/2021/03/11/procrastination-why-do-we-do-it-and-what-can-we-do-to-stop/)  
> 
> Additional reading:
> 
> -   [UBC Life blog: A chronic procrastinator's guide to independent projects](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/chronic-procrastinators-guide-independent-projects)
> -   [UBC Life blog: Procrastination: It's not what you think it is](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/procrastination-its-not-what-you-think-it)
> 
> Sleep
> 
> In order to perform at your best in university, it's important you take care of yourself and how you sleep\. Despite how easy it is to stay up late to study or do homework, you should set aside time for your brain to process the information you're learning\. Access the Sleep and Academic Success Toolkit by the Chapman Learning Commons, a 3\-video series on how you can apply techniques to improve your sleep and studies\.
> 
> [Access the Sleep and Academic Success Toolkit](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/student-toolkits/sleep-and-academic-success/)  
> 
> Additional reading:
> 
> -   [UBC Life blog: How to get your sleep schedule back on track—now](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/sleep-schedule-back-tracknow)
> 
> Stress
> 
> Stress is a normal part of the human experience\. However, everyone experiences stress differently and stressors are unique to each person\. Find information on recognizing signs of stress, managing the stress response, and understanding different types of stressors\.
> 
> [Learn about strategies on how to manage stress](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/understanding-stress)  
> 
> Additional reading:
>

No one knows students better than other students\. Stay connected with students from other faculties and learn about the stories happening around you at UBC\. Visit the UBC Student Life blog for study tips, student experiences, and general lifehacks, written for students, by students\.

Accessibility Advisors can help if you have a disability or ongoing medical condition that you think will impact your academics or any other aspect of university life\. ## Examine the environmental, economic, and social sustainability challenges and opportunities faced by today’s business leaders\.

### Looking for the Sustainability concentration?

The Sustainability concentration has been renamed the Sustainability and Social Impact concentration\. Requirements to complete the concentration have not changed\.

### Course requirements

Completion of the Sustainability and Social Impact concentration does not require pre\-approval or special admission\. If you would like to pursue this concentration, complete a total of 12 credits of sustainability\-related courses as listed below\.

The 12 credits also count toward fulfillment of your electives requirement, but note that COMM courses cannot be counted as non\-Commerce electives\. If the courses you take for a concentration overlap with the courses you take for an option or minor, you can double count a maximum of 3 credits of coursework in your degree toward both the concentration and one of either one option or one minor\.   

After you've applied to graduate, we'll provide instructions for how to declare the concentration so that it will appear on your academic transcript\.

title: Scholarships and Funding
content_markdown:
### Funding your studies

Student loans, scholarships, bursaries, and employment are all ways for you to finance your studies\. Take time to understand the full range of financial support options available to you so that you can spend less time worrying about money and more time focusing on your coursework\.

[Financial support for students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/funding-studies)  

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/scholarships-and-funding)

### Maintain your eligibility for student loans

Government loans, grants, and interest\-free status all require students to be enrolled in at least 60% \(80% for Newfoundland and Labrador loans\) of a full\-time course load in each term\. Given the credit structure of the BCom program, the minimum number of credits you must be enrolled in varies at different year levels\. Consult the course load guide at students\.ubc\.ca to ensure that you meet the requirements to maintain your funding\. Note that eligibility to receive scholarships and to live in UBC residence is determined by separate registration criteria\.

[Consult the course load guide](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-load-guide)

## Scholarships and awards

In addition to entrance scholarships, there are many other scholarships and awards available to you as a student in the BCom program\. At the start of the academic year, typically over 50 academic merit awards are assigned to continuing students based on academic achievement in the previous academic year\.

### By application awards

-   In addition to merit awards, many more awards are available by application to recognize achievement in your previous year of studies\. Academic achievement may be a factor, but non\-academic factors such as leadership, community involvement, or financial need may also be included in individual award criteria\.
-   The application deadline for 2026W awards is **September 20, 2026 \(11:59 PM PT\)**\. Applications are evaluated sequentially by award\. Recipients will be notified as decisions are made, from early October until late November\.

The list of available awards by application for 2026W will be posted at the end of August\. 

[List of available awards by application \(2026W\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/6891/download?token=ixOPH6rD)

[Budget planner](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/6752/download?token=XQb0-QEV)

Eligibility requirements

There are limited awards available to new BCom students\. Awards for Indigenous students are available to both new and continuing students\. All other awards are only available to continuing students who were registered in the BCom program the previous academic year\.

#### Academic Merit awards

Award eligibility is based on the academic year \(September\-April\) and does not include summer registration\. Candidates must be registered in the BCom program in a minimum of 24 percentage\-graded credits in the previous academic year with no failures or missing grades and a minimum of 24 credits in the current academic year\. A minimum 75% in the previous academic year is required\.

##### Exceptions to minimum credit rules can be found [here](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/special-circumstances-receiving-awards/)\.

#### Non\-Academic Merit awards

Candidates must be registered in the BCom program in the previous academic year and in the current academic year\. Applicants are expected to be in good academic standing \(obtained minimum 60% in the previous academic year\)\.

Refer to the list of available awards by application to determine if an award is an academic merit award or a non\-academic merit award\.

Application instructions

In your online application, be sure to:

-   provide all biographic details as applicable
-   upload your one\-page resume
-   provide an accompanying statement \(350\-word maximum\) for each award to which you wish to apply
-   provide details of your estimated budget for the 2026/27 Winter Session if you are applying to any awards that list financial need as one of their criteria \(refer to the downloadable budget planner for guidance\)

Once you start your online application you CANNOT save a draft to return to at a later time\. Please be prepared to complete the entirety of your application in one sitting\. We recommend that you prepare your responses in advance and then paste them into your application when you are ready to submit it\. Submit only one complete application\. If duplicates are submitted, only the most recent submission will be reviewed\. Incomplete or late applications will not be reviewed\.

[Apply now](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4NP6B7qjc4t1PRY)

title: Graduation
content_markdown:
### If you've completed all of your degree requirements, it's time to graduate\. Congratulations\!

### Preparing for graduation

You’ve worked hard to get here so let’s make it an awesome occasion for you, your proud family and friends\.

Graduation ceremonies are held annually in May and November\. You must complete your degree requirements by the end of April to graduate in the May ceremony or by the end of August to be eligible to graduate in the November ceremony\.

In order to graduate, you must submit a formal application for graduation\. In Workday, this is called the **“Program Completion Application”**\. You can find the application deadlines for the May ceremony and November ceremony on **[the Applying to Graduate website](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate)\.**

Your application to graduate will be reviewed in April for the May ceremony or in October for the November ceremony\. Note that if you achieve a winter session average below 60% in your final year, you will be permitted to graduate, however, a notation of ‘Failed Year, Permitted to Continue’ will appear on your academic transcript for that session\.

You must complete your BCom degree requirements within six years of your original admission to the UBC Sauder School of Business\. It’s up to you to make sure that you've fulfilled all program requirements when applying to graduate\. Check your [program requirements](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/program-requirements) and contact the [Office of Student Academic Services](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/ugo)  if you have any questions\.

### Expected Completion Date \(ECD\) for Graduation Application

You **must** enter your Expected Completion Date \(ECD\) according to the conferral period you are applying for:

-   **May Graduation:** Enter **April 30**\.
-   **November Graduation:** Enter **August 31**\.

For detailed instructions on how to apply for graduation, please refer to the [Workday tutorial here](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/applying-for-graduation-or-program-completion/)\.

### Academic Progress Report

Your personalized APR in Workday Student is a tool to keep track of your degree requirements and credits\. The APR replaces Degree Navigator \(Degree Credit Check\) as UBC’s degree audit tool and displays your academic requirements as listed on the corresponding UBC Academic Calendar entries for your program and your progression in the program\.

The APR **has** **limitations** and **must** be used in combination with our **[Course Planning Worksheets](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-tool)** and **[Elective Checklist](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/elective-requirements)** for accurate degree planning\.

Please visit the [l](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/apr)ink below for more information on how to read your APR\.

[Academic Progress Report \(APR\) Webpage](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/apr)[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/bcom\-program\-planning\-worksheets](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/bcom-program-planning-worksheets)

### Your big day

Learn more about your graduation day including ceremony instructions, schedules, tickets, gown rentals, and photos\.   
  
[Graduation at UBC](http://graduation.ubc.ca/)

>

>

### Declaring a second option, minor, or concentration

When the graduation application period opens, the Office of Student Academic Services \(OSAS\) will email all applicants with instructions on how to affirm their expected completion of a second option, minor, or concentration, if applicable\. Please ensure you submit your most up\-to\-date minor or concentration forms by the graduation application deadline\. At the time of graduation, completion of a second option and/or concentration will be noted on your transcript\. Students must complete all course requirements for a second option, minor, or concentration by the graduation application deadline, as requirements cannot be completed after the BCom degree has been conferred\.

### Degree with Honours

The words 'with Honours' will be placed on your transcript and your degree certificate if you meet the following conditions:

-   achieve an average of 80% or greater on all senior\-level \(300 and 400\-level\) Commerce courses \(COMM\_V and COHR\_V\)\.\[1\] Senior\-level \(300 and 400\-level\) CPSC\_V courses are also included for students in the Combined Major in Business & Computer Science \(BUCS\)\. The average is calculated to 2 decimal points and is not rounded\. **EXCEPTION**:

-   If you **HAVE** Cr/D/F grades for any senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC for BUCS\) in 2019W Term 2, then **ALL** senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC\_V for BUCS\_V\) courses taken in 2019W Term 2 are **EXCLUDED** from your graduating average calculation\.\[2\]
-   If you **DO NOT HAVE** Cr/D/F grades for any senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC\_V for BUCS\_V\) in 2019W Term 2, then **ALL** senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC\_V for BUCS\_V\) courses taken in 2019W Term 2 are **INCLUDED** in your graduating average calculation\.

-   meet **ONE OF** the following credit requirements\[3,4\]:

-   24 percentage\-graded credits in the Winter Session of Year 3 or Year 4, **OR**
-   At least 24 credits in Year 3 or Year 4 in the 2019 Winter Session including 12 percentage\-graded credits in 2019W Term 1

###### \[1\] If you were registered in Year 2 or above during the 2014 Winter Session, COMM\_V 203 \(COMM\_V 392 equivalent\), COMM\_V 204 \(COMM\_V 399 equivalent\), and COMM\_V 205 \(COMM\_V 391 equivalent\) will be included in the calculation of your average\. If you were in Year 1 during the 2014 Winter Session and took any of COMM\_V 391, COMM\_V 392, COMM\_V 399 during the 2015 Summer Session or prior, your grades for those courses will not be used to determine eligibility to achieve a Degree with Honours\.

###### \[2\] If you have CR/D/F grades for any senior\-level COMM/COHR\_V \(and CPSC\_V for BUCS\_V\) in 2019W Term 2 and you have taken a six\-credit percentage\-graded COMM\_V course during 2019W that spanned Terms 1 and 2 \(COMM\_V 466, COMM\_V 486W\), your percentage grade for the six\-credit course will be included in your graduating average calculation, however, it will be weighted for only 3 credits rather than 6 credits\.

###### \[3\] Students who graduated in May 2019 or prior were required to be registered in at least 27 percentage\-graded credits during the winter session in at least one of Year 3 or Year 4 of the program\. For those students in the Co\-op program and registered at UBC for only one term in the winter session because of a Co\-op placement, they had to have been in 15 percentage\-graded credits in their non\-Co\-op term to be eligible\.

###### \[4\] If you're a Co\-op student and you're registered at UBC for only one term in the winter session because of a Co\-op placement, you must be in 12 percentage\-graded credits in your non\-Co\-op term to be eligible\. If you participate in an exchange program in the 2025 winter session or prior, your grades earned while on exchange will be included in the calculation\.

**If you're unable to calculate your eligibility to achieve a Degree with Honours yourself, you can confirm your Honours status at the Office of Student Academic Services after May 19 for the spring ceremony and November 20 for the fall ceremony\.**

title: Study spaces
content_markdown:
### Group work rooms

[The Canaccord Learning Commons](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/clc) has a variety of groupwork rooms available to all UBC Sauder students\. Our large rooms \(six to eight person capacity\) come equipped with a whiteboard and a digital screen\. Our small rooms \(two to three person capacity\) located on the main level have a white board only\. Whiteboard markers and erasers, as well as laptops and mac adapters for the screens, are [available for loan at the Service Desk](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/know-sauder/learning-commons-and-library/book-and-equipment-borrowing)\. These rooms are meant for academic purposes and should not be used for individual study, TA office hours, or club administration\.

The Birmingham Undergraduate Centre, located on the first floor of the Henry Angus Building provides additional rooms for groupwork\. There are also several more groupwork rooms located on the fourth floor of the Henry Angus building\.  

### Communal and silent study

The Learning Commons offers a variety of options for individual and group study\. Communal tables where quiet conversation is permitted are available on the main floor for individuals and small groups\. Both the main and upper floors feature Silent Study areas\. Study carrels are available on the upper floor, and all come equipped with a plug for electronics\.

### Computer workstations

Computer terminals and printers are available in the main area of the main and upper level\. Additionally, there is a small computer lab on the main level \(adjacent to Silent Study\) with more computers, access to datastream and Capital IQ, and a Bloomberg terminal\.

> ### Reminders
> 
> As common courtesy to your fellow students and UBC Sauder staff, please ensure you pick up after yourself, and leave the room clean and tidy\. No hot food is allowed anywhere in the Learning Commons\. Furniture should not be removed from any room\.

### Need a quiet space for a group work meeting or study session?

Visit the UBC Sauder Room Bookings site to reserve a room\. Bookings are limited to two hours in length\. To ensure wide access, individuals and groups may only make one booking per day\. Rooms may only be used for academic purposes, organizations and student clubs should find alternate meeting space\.

[Book a room](http://booking.sauder.ubc.ca/)

title: Industry Events & Workshops
content_markdown:
### Make real connections\. Launch your future\.

[Students at Spring Networking Social](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/slideshow-images/springnetwork-83.jpg?itok=NzVgJq7e)

The Hari B\. Varshney Business Career Centre \(BCC\) organizes events all year to help you:

-   Explore career paths
-   Build job\-ready skills
-   Connect with employers & alumni
-   Meet companies hiring now

Find events on **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/events)** and watch your inbox for the BCC's **BCom Careers Newsletter** \(and Co\-op Newsletter, if you're registered in the program\)\.

## Connect with employers

### Company Recruiting Sessions \(CRS\)

Exploring career paths, internships, or full\-time roles for after graduation? CRS events connect you with employers who are hiring now\. 

The BCC brings in companies from a wide variety of industries, including:

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   Marketing
    -   Finance
    -   Accounting
    -   Technology
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Consumer Packaged Goods \(CPG\)
    -   Consulting
    -   Real Estate
    -   Supply Chain

**Why attend?**

-   Employers come to meet students like you
-   Make a strong first impression
-   Get insider insights from recruiters, hiring managers, and UBC Sauder alumni

**Pro tip**: Sessions fill fast—check **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/events)** often so you don't miss out\. 

> ## Networking & Events
> 
> -   [Networking Resources](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/networking-events/networking-resources)
> -   [LinkedIn Resources](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-resources/linkedin-resources)
> -   [Industry Events & Workshop](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/industry-events-%26-workshops)
> 
> ### Have questions about networking?
> 
> **[Peer Career Advisors](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/career-peer-advisors)** will be back in September 2026\.
> 
> Looking for personalized 1:1 support? Book a **Networking & Connecting coaching appointment** on **UBC Sauder Career Hub**\.
> 
> [Book your appointment](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments)

### UBC Sauder Recruit Night

Meet employers who are actively recruiting and connect with business professionals and alumni at this annual UBC Sauder\-exclusive event\.

This event is designed for **4th\-year and above BComs and BCom Co\-ops seeking full\-time roles**\.

Before the event, we encourage students to:

-   Do your homework: research attending companies in advance
-   Come prepared with questions to make a strong impression

-   **Date:** February 24th, 2026
-   **Registration**: Sign up on [Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/events)

The Business Career Centre thanks the **[Commerce Undergraduate Society](https://www.cus.ca/)** for supporting UBC Sauder Recruit Night\.

### UBC\-wide career events & workshops

Along with events hosted by the BCC, you can also check out events hosted by the **[UBC Career Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-career-centre)**\. Make the most of their career events, typically held every year:

-   **[Career Days](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/ubc-career-days)**: Visit the 2\-day in\-person career fair that features over 90 employers from various industries, eager to engage with students and alumni to share career opportunities and insights\.
-   [**West Coast Virtual Fairs**](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/west-coast-virtual-fairs): Find work, volunteer, and academic opportunities available after your UBC degree at this 2\-day, multi\-school virtual fair\.
-   [**Spring Career Fair**](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/spring-career-fair): Take part in UBC's 2\-day event and meet around 90 employers and schools for potential career opportunities\.
-   [**Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference**](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference): Attend the MURC to present your research to other UBC students, friends, and family\.
-   [**Graduate and Professional Schools Fair**](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/graduate-professional-schools-fair): Meet recruiters from graduate and professional programs to learn about further educational opportunities at UBC and beyond\.

Find out more about UBC Career Centre events and workshops **[here](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops)**\.

### Get involved on campus

[Campus](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/images/teaser-widget/45768497911_8879f86fc7_o.jpg?itok=YwIUxKlu)

**Case competitions and conferences**

By participating in student\-led case competitions, conferences and club activities, you can apply your classroom learning and meet people from the business community, including potential employers\.

-   The **[UBC Sauder Summit Global Case Competition](https://www.saudersummit.ca/)** is organized and hosted by UBC Sauder students each March\.
-   The **Case Competition Club** organizes internal and external competitions, including the **[National Strategy Consulting Competition and Conference](http://www.thenscc.com/)** and the **[Strategy Consulting Initiative](https://www.linkedin.com/company/strategy-consulting-initiative/posts/?feedView=all)\.  
    **
-   You can also take part in the UBC Sauder student\-run conferences [**Me Inc**\.](https://www.linkedin.com/company/me-inc-conference/posts/?feedView=all) and **[Imprint](https://www.ubcimprint.com/)**\.

Look for opportunities to get involved throughout the year\!

title: Frequently Asked Questions
content_markdown:
[Image](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/6.png?itok=-db_cxH1)

[Image](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/website_faqs_2023_-_co-op_team1_0.png?itok=hqaI8rzm&c=ee2c71d04c449f4ad58a5372d7c116ff)

### **General Program Inquiries**

Can I apply to the UBC Sauder Co\-op Program anytime throughout the year?

You can only apply to the UBC Sauder Co\-op Program during the intake period, which occurs once a year in September\.  
  
As part of the accreditation standards under [CEWIL Canada](https://cewilcanada.ca/CEWIL/CEWIL/Councils%20and%20Committees/Accreditation.aspx), pre\-employment workshops are hosted by the Co\-op team from January to April\. This programming structure only allows for one intake period in the calendar year\. If you miss the intake period, you can apply again the following year if you still meet all eligibility requirements\. No exceptions will be made\.

Can I apply for a Co\-op position if I am not in the Co\-op program?

You cannot apply to Co\-op positions as a non\-Co\-op student; however, you are welcome to apply for internships in the summer\. If you would like to apply to Co\-op positions, you must be admitted into the Co\-op Program\. See how to apply [here](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/co-op-program/requirements-%26-how-to-apply)\.

I received an offer for a Co\-op job, but I'm not in the Co\-op program\. What should I do?

Students who are not enrolled in the Co\-op program cannot apply to jobs requiring Co\-op student standing\. If the job is posted for Co\-op students, it is likely that you will not be able to accept the offer\. Employers who specifically hire Co\-op students often receive funding that requires the student to be enrolled in an accredited Co\-op program\. Also, students working specifically in the January or September term must be enrolled in the Co\-op program to maintain full\-time student status\.

Please let the employer know immediately and discuss whether an accommodation can be made for your particular case\.

Do international students need a Co\-op work permit to work in Canada?

As of April 1, 2026, international students **enrolled in the Co\-op program** no longer need a separate work permit to participate in a Co\-op work term that is required as part of their academic program, provided they meet the [eligibility criteria](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#confirm-eligibility)\.

Students must still meet Co\-op\-specific requirements, such as full\-time student enrolment, a valid study permit with work authorization, and Co\-op program registration\.

Click [here](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/) for more information\.

Can I still work full\-time off\-campus during the school year as a non\-Co\-op student?

If you are a non\-Co\-op international student, you can only work off\-campus part\-time\* during the school year\*\*, provided you meet the [eligibility requirements to work off\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#make-sure-youre-eligible-to-work-off-campus) and maintain full\-time student status\. If you are a part\-time student, you are not eligible to work in Canada for the rest of that term\. Co\-op program registration is the only way to work full\-time off\-campus during this period\. See [here](https://students.ubc.ca/career/working-canada) to view the work you are eligible for with your study permit\.

If you are a domestic student, working full\-time during the school year as a non\-Co\-op student may lead to losing your full\-time student status\. There are complications to losing this status and it is recommended you contact an [OSAS Academic Advisor](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/ugo) to understand your individual case\.

\*Up to 24 hours per week\.

\*\*Outside of scheduled breaks\.

Why would you want to maintain full\-time student status at UBC Sauder?

There are commitments and considerations that require students to be registered as a full\-time student to maintain eligibility \(e\.g\., student loans, scholarships, housing, study permit, U\-Pass, etc\.\)\. If you are an international student, maintaining full\-time student status is required to meet [eligibility requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time) such as working in Canada, working full\-time during scheduled breaks, and Post\-Graduate Work Permit eligibility\. Co\-op program registration allows you to work while retaining full\-time student status\. 

Find out more [here](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide)\. If you have any questions about full\-time student status, please contact an [OSAS Academic Advisor](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/ugo)\.

Can I go on exchange while in the Co\-op Program?

Yes, we have many Co\-op students who go on exchange for an academic term, while in the Co\-op Program\! You can also still apply to the Co\-op program with an exchange term lined up\. Speak to your Co\-op Manager about your Co\-op work and study plan and connect with representatives from [Go Global](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global) to learn more\.

If I am in BUCS do I need to apply to both the Science Co\-op program and Sauder Co\-op program?

You are not required to apply to both Co\-op programs\. You may choose which Co\-op program is the best fit for you depending on the types of roles you interested in\. [Science Co\-op](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/prospective/apply/cs) offers more technical roles \(e\.g\., Software Engineering, Software Development, etc\.\) while Sauder Co\-op provides more business\-related roles \(e\.g\., Analyst, Technology Consulting, etc\.\)\. 

That being said, some students do choose to apply to both Co\-op programs\. If you are admitted into both, you can select the program that is the best fit for you depending on the roles you want to pursue\. Science Co\-op typically has [intake periods](https://sciencecoop.ubc.ca/prospective/applydeadlines) that are later than Sauder’s\. This means you may need to decide on Sauder’s offer of admission before knowing the results of your Science Co\-op offer of admission\.[https://w/BCC/Portfolios/Co\-op/08%20Projects/myBCom%20Website/2023\-2024/Updated%20Website%20Content/FAQ%20Page%20additions\.docx\#\_msocom\_3](https://w/BCC/Portfolios/Co-op/08%20Projects/myBCom%20Website/2023-2024/Updated%20Website%20Content/FAQ%20Page%20additions.docx#_msocom_3)

If you are in Science Co\-op already as a BUCS student and would like to join Sauder Co\-op, contact your Co\-op Manager for next steps\. You will be able to apply to the Sauder Co\-op program in a shortened and more expedited process once a year in the Fall\.

### **Co\-op Work Terms**

Will the Co\-op Program place me into a job?

No\. As a Co\-op student, you are responsible for your own job search in order to find employment during your time in the Co\-op program\.

The Co\-op team and the Hari B\. Varshney Business Career Centre work with local, national, and international employers to post valuable jobs with a variety of growth opportunities for Co\-op students\. You will be able to apply for these opportunities on the UBC Sauder Career Hub, our online job portal, or do your own self\-directed job search\. You will also be supported by the Co\-op team before, during, and after your search\.

What is the difference between a Co\-op term and an internship?

Please note that some companies use the word “Co\-op” and “internship” interchangeably; however, Co\-op terms can take place throughout the year while internships typically take place in summer\. See the [Why Co\-op? web page](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/co-op-program/why-co-op) for more details on the differences between Co\-op and Internships\.

Does Co\-op count for academic credit?

Students on a Co\-op work term are registered into a Co\-op course, which allows you to maintain full\-time student status that term\. However, Co\-op courses are non\-academic credits that do not count towards graduation\. A Co\-op work term does not replace or add academic course credits for that term\.

Am I graded on a work\-term?

Co\-op courses are Pass/Fail only\. You must complete all work term deliverables on time in order to pass the course\. This includes:

-   Submitting your work term learning objectives
-   Completing a site visit with your Co\-op Manager
-   Submitting a high quality end of term Work Term Report, Program Evaluation, Self Evaluation, and updated resume
-   Having your supervisor complete their Employer Evaluation

Can part\-time jobs count as Co\-op?

No\. Only full\-time positions that are a minimum of 420 hours can count for Co\-op \(e\.g\., 35 hours per week for 12 weeks or any other combination of the required hours in the 4\-month work term period\)\.

Can I count past internships retroactively as one of my three Co\-op work terms?

You would not be able to count past internships as a Co\-op work term\. All Co\-op work terms must be completed after your admission into the program\.

Can I do an international work term?

Our students are welcome to explore opportunities outside of Canada for their Co\-op work terms\. If you do so, be mindful that there might be regulations outside of our control that may preclude you from doing your Co\-op work term in a specific country\. Before you apply for a role in a foreign jurisdiction, it is important to do basic research of the required documents to submit and conditions for you to work there\. One example is France, where all internships and Co\-op work terms require “convention de stage”, which is currently not a document that UBC Sauder provides to our students\.

### **Co\-op Fees and Financial Information**

What are the fees of the UBC Sauder Co\-op program?

In addition to University of British Columbia fees, students are required to pay fees associated with the UBC Sauder Co\-op program:

-   Co\-op students pay a [one\-time workshop and administration fee](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/program-course-and-faculty-fees), payable upon acceptance into the UBC Sauder Co\-op Program
-   [Course tuition fees](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/program-course-and-faculty-fees) are paid during each Co\-op work term, payable to UBC  
      
    
    |  |  |  |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | UBC Sauder Co\-op Fees | Co\-op Fees \(Per Term\) | Total Amount |
    | Workshop and Administration Fee | $288\.25\*x 1 terms | $288\.25 |
    | Co\-op Course Fee | $889\.00\*x 3 terms | $2,667\.00[https://w/BCC/Portfolios/Co\-op/08%20Projects/myBCom%20Website/2022\-2023/FAQs/FAQ%20\-%20Co\-op%20Fees%20\-%20v2\.docx\#\_msocom\_2](https://w/BCC/Portfolios/Co-op/08%20Projects/myBCom%20Website/2022-2023/FAQs/FAQ%20-%20Co-op%20Fees%20-%20v2.docx#_msocom_2) |
    
    *\*These fees are for 2026\-27, and are subject to change, as per* [*UBC tuition guidelines*](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/program-course-and-faculty-fees)

What is the Co\-op course fee for?

Each time you participate in a Co\-op work term, you will be registered in a Co\-op work term course \(COMM 380/381/480 or 481\) and pay the course tuition fees\. Registration in the Co\-op work term course is mandatory and maintains your full\-time student status with UBC; you will receive non\-academic credits for each Co\-op work term course\. Please note that Co\-op work term courses do not count towards your academic degree requirements\.

Why am I paying Co\-op fees?

**This is not a job placement fee\.** These fees help us to offset the costs of running the Co\-op program and allow us to offer services that help students throughout their journey, including:

-   Advising and preparing you for your Co\-op work terms through mandatory pre\-employment workshops, networking events, mock interviews, and more
-   One\-on\-one office hours for assistance during your job searches with our Co\-op Career Strategists
-   Support provided before and during your work term, such as site visits, newsletters, job recommendation emails, directory of past Co\-ops and hiring timelines
-   Building relationships with reputable employers who post new and recurring positions with the program

What do Co\-op fees cost for an international student?

International students pay the same amount as domestic students, and Co\-op allows you to work full\-time off\-campus during academic terms while maintaining full\-time student status\. If you have any questions about fees, please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors)\.

Tuition is reviewed annually by the UBC Board of Governors; in recent years, tuition increases have been 2% annually\. Visit the [UBC Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/program-course-and-faculty-fees) for the latest fee information

Am I still eligible for student loans and scholarships while in Co\-op?

For details about student loans or your scholarship status while in the Co\-op program, see [special circumstances for students receiving awards](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/special-circumstances-receiving-awards)\.

title: What Can I Do With My Degree?
content_markdown:
### Discover your career options and get a head start on your career journey

[Student with a laptop in classroom](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/level_2_-_what_can_i_do_with_my_degree.jpg?itok=lbt4BokP)

 Wondering what **types of jobs** are available to you **with your degree** and the different BCom option areas? Or, trying to decide what option to choose

Explore the below links to get an overview of the **UBC BCom option areas** and the types of **careers usually associated** with them\. Here you'll find details on:

-   Employment outlook
-   Skills employers look for
-   Employers that hire BCom grads
-   Common job titles
-   Recommended resources for each field and more\!

### Explore your options

### [Accounting](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/accounting)

Accounting plays a crucial role in any organization's strategic planning and future development by analyzing financial records and accounting information\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/accounting)

### [Business Technology](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/business-technology-management)

BTM\-related careers are high in demand and leverage technology to contribute to a company's competitive advantage\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/business-technology-management)

### [Consulting](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/consulting)

Consulting is a dynamic, fast\-paced career path that involves analyzing information, problem\-solving, and creating strategic solutions for various clients\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/consulting)

### [Entrepreneurship](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/entrepreneurship)

Does the idea of creating new ventures or driving innovation excite you? Entrepreneurship might be the right option for you\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/entrepreneurship)

### [Finance](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/finance)

An option in Finance equips you with the essential skills and knowledge to help individuals and organizations reach their unique financial goals\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/finance)

### [General Business](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/general-business)

Interested in wearing different hats as new organizational needs arise? This option is designed to meet the needs of the ever\-evolving business community\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/general-business)

### [Human Resources](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/human-resources)

Human capital is often a company's most valuable asset\. Whether you're interested in labour relations, training, or development/change management, this career path can be very rewarding\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/human-resources)

### [Marketing](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/marketing)

Marketing helps businesses understand its target audience and develop strategies to attract and retain customers\. From market research to brand management, career opportunities in marketing are varied and adaptable\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/marketing)

### [Operations and Logistics](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/operations-and-logistics)

Logistics involves the flow of goods, information, and money in organizations\. This career path opens opportunities in manufacturing, distribution firms, and government departments at all levels\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/operations-and-logistics)

### [Real Estate](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/real-estate)

Real estate is a valuable option due to increasing international demand\. From real estate agents to mortgage analysts, this option prepares you with the skills to embark on a lucrative career\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/careers/real-estate)

### How to choose your option

Access info to help you find a BCom option that fits you best\.

[Access now](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/options/choosing-your-option)

### Additional resources

-   [**Role Alignment Toolkit**](https://authentication.ubc.ca/idp/profile/SAML2/Redirect/SSO?execution=e4s1): Learn what to expect regarding grades, location, and professional designations for your desired career paths
-   [https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/ubc\-sauder\-alumni\-job\-data](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/ubc-sauder-alumni-job-data)**[Job IQ Explorer](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/ubc-sauder-alumni-job-data):** on Career Hub: All BCom students and recent alumni are provided exclusive access to Job IQ Explorer, which offers invaluable information about jobs UBC Sauder students have landed up to 6 months after graduation\.

### Get decision\-making support

Whether you know which option is for you or are you still deciding, get personalized advice and guidance on your career path\.  
  
[**Peer Career Advisors**](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching-advising/career-peer-advisors) will be back in September 2026\.

Book a 1:1 "Selecting Academic Option/Track" [**coaching & advising**](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching) appointment on Career Hub\.

  
[Book an appointment](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments/%5D) 

### Navigate Your Career Journey

Trying to figure out what type of work interests you? Or maybe you’re wondering what resources can help you achieve your goals? No matter where you are in your unique career journey, you can use our career development model to help navigate your personal and professional goals at UBC Sauder and beyond\.

[Learn More](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/navigate-your-career-journey)

title: Careers in Accounting
content_markdown:
### What do accountants do?

**[Accountants](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/options/accounting)** play a valuable role in any organization: from making sure that money is coming in, to keeping the doors open and lights on\.

They use financial data to **help shape businesses and support future growth**\. Organizations rely on accountants’ expertise to make tough decisions related to:

-   Moving into new markets
-   Starting or ending business ventures
-   Launching new products
-   Avoiding unprofitable business moves
-   Finding creative ways to reduce waste and unnecessary spending

Accounting always needs new people and offers an **exciting, secure, and financially rewarding career path**\.

Even with advancements in artificial intelligence and automation, **businesses need accountants to interpret complex tax laws and ever\-changing regulations**\.

Plus, accountants help manage and decode financial information to help organizations make informed business decisions\.

### Types of accounting practices

According to the **[“Vault Career Guide to Accounting”](https://ubc-sauder.firsthand.co/vault-guides/guide/vault-career-guide-to-accounting-third-edition/view)**, which is available to UBC Sauder students on Firsthand, accountants typically work in one of five areas:

1.  Public practice
2.  Industry practice
3.  Government
4.  Nonprofit accounting
5.  Academia

### Skill set required

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    -   [Analytical skills](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/289/download)
    -   Leadership skills
    -   Communication skills \(written and verbal\)
    -   Mathematical skills
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Attention to detail
    -   Ability to work independently and within a team environment
    -   Excellent work ethic

> ### [Book a coaching appointment](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments)
>

The Public Practice Recruit \(PPR\) is a semi\-annual recruitment campaign where international, national, and mid\-sized \(local\) **CPA firms hire accounting students** for full\-time, summer internship, or Co\-op positions in the spring and fall each year\. These positions generally start in January, May, or September the following year\.

Varshney Business Career Centre, Diploma in Accounting Program, UBC DAP Student Club, and UBC Accounting Club work together with [**Chartered Professional Accountants of British Columbia \(CPABC**\)](https://www.bccpa.ca/students-candidates/) to coordinate and support students along the way\.
