## Online Request Forms

Academic concession

Sometimes unanticipated events or circumstances can affect your ability to complete your academic responsibilities\. You may be eligible to submit a petition for an academic concession if you meet the certain eligibility criteria, and in some circumstances, provide supporting documentation\.  

An academic concession is a form of support that allows for deferment of marked work so that you can complete a course's requirements\. Carefully review UBC's academic concession policy to understand the different types of concessions as well as how to submit a petition\.

[Request academic concession](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/academic-concession)  

Credit/D/Fail grading

If you would like to switch a course to [Credit/D/Fail grading](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/exams-and-grades/grades) you can submit the request form once you have registered for all of your courses; you won’t be able to perform this function yourself in Workday\. OSAS will only process requests as defined in the form’s instructions\. Academic advisors will direct all requests they receive to this form\. Please allow at least five business days for processing\. The deadline to switch between percentage and Credit/D/Fail grading is the same date to which you are still eligible to drop the course without a W standing\.

[Request Credit/D/Fail grading switch](https://sauder.jotform.com/team/ugo/switching-course-to-cdf)  

Proof of enrolment and confirmation of program completion letters

Your UBC transcript and diploma are official documents issued by the university to affirm your academic record and completion of degree program, respectively\.

On occasion, you may be asked by a third\-party to provide additional documentation regarding your studies at UBC, such as when applying to extend your study permit or proving your credentials to a potential employer\. This is typically provided in the form of a letter from the school which may, for example, confirm:

-   your status as a registered, full\-time student
-   your expected program completion date
-   your completion of degree requirements
-   conferral of your degree 

You can download some of these letters on demand from the Student Service Centre \(SSC\), but others must be requested from the UGO\.

[Request a letter](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/letters)  

Registration assistance

All registration requests will be reviewed to determine if they meet one of the valid reasons for registration assistance\. Requests made for invalid reasons will be dismissed\. Office of Student Academic Services \(OSAS\) will attempt to accommodate your registration request based on seat availability in sections \(not necessarily section preference\), and in some cases seat availability in alternate courses that will fulfill the same requirement\.

Please review the following webpage to determine if your reason for registration assistance is valid before submitting your request\. Do not submit requests until you have an open registration\.

[Registration Assistance Webpage](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses-and-registration/registration-assistance)

Credit limit increase

Balancing a full course load is challenging, so a credit increase is not usually recommended, particularly if you work or have other responsibilities\. If you are approved for a credit increase \(3\-6 credits max\), you will not be eligible for academic concession for any issues related to your increased workload\.

In Workday, the credits for two\-term, six credit courses are not evenly split across academic periods, but instead apply to the term in which the course begins\. In this instance, you can request an increase to your Term 1 limit to offset the imbalance – your Term 2 credit limit will be reduced accordingly\.

Credit increases to take an increased course load are only permitted after all students have had a chance to register\. Year 1 students are not eligible for credit limit increases\.

The credit limit increase request form below is available for students to request rebalancing of credit limits to allow for registration in two\-term, six credit courses\.

**Requests for credit limit increases to take additional courses in the Winter Session will be accepted starting August 1 once all students have had an opportunity to register\.**

#### [Request a credit limit increase](https://sauder.jotform.com/team/ugo/credit-limit-increase)

title: Business Career Centre
content_markdown:
### The Hari B\. Varshney Business Career Centre \(BCC\) is here to support every step of your career journey

[3 students in front of the BCC](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/files/styles/panopoly_image_original/public/media/about-bcc.jpg?itok=jwSAQX6S)

The Business Career Centre \(BCC\) plays a crucial role in your UBC Sauder experience\. We aim to equip you with the tools and knowledge to **gain work experience** and **find fulfilling careers after graduation**\.

Through one\-on\-one coaching with our experienced **[BCom Career Strategists](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/bcom-career-strategists)**, **[Co\-op Career Strategists](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/co-op-managers)**, and **[Peer Career Advisors](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/career-peer-advisors)**, along with tailored events and programs focused on your career development, you have opportunities to **explore, discover, and realize your career aspirations**\.

Plus, we leverage UBC Sauder's extensive network to connect you with the business community\. To help you make connections we facilitate:

-   **[Industry events & workshops](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/industry-events-%26-workshops)**: Company recruiting sessions, hiring events, networking events, and more
-   Information interviews and mock interviews: check out our **[interview prep resources](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/job-interviews/interview-prep-resources)**  
    [https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/file/1467/download](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/1467/download)
-   **[Mentorship & specialty programs](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/mentorship-specialty-programs)**: Brand Management, Finance Mentorship, and Capital Markets Training, to name a few[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/file/2663/download](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/file/2663/download)

Additionally, each year, we post thousands of internship and full\-time job opportunities on the **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-resources/cool-career-platform)** that span diverse industries and roles\.

While we provide these opportunities, it's up to you to take action\. The BCC's career team is here to support you every step of the way\.

### Career services designed for UBC Sauder students

We provide services and resources to help you clarify career goals, explore career options, develop job search skills, and find job opportunities through the following:

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **Career development resources**: self\-serve resources available 24/7 on **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/resource-library/)** to help you with resumes, cover letters, career research, interviews, and more

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    In\-person and virtual one\-on\-one **[career coaching & advising](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching)** appointments \(book on **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments)**\)

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Drop\-in **[Peer Career Advising](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/career-peer-advisors)**  
    
    -   **When**: 11:00 am to 2:00 pm \(Monday\-Friday\), during the academic term
    -   **Where**: CPA Hall near the BCC \(HA 155\)

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **[UBC Sauder Co\-op program](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/co-op-program)**: opportunities to apply your classroom learning with three 4\-month work terms in your chosen field

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **[COMM 202 \- Career Fundamentals](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/comm202)**: learn about professional cover letter and resume writing, professional employment, networking, and information interviews

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **[Industry events & workshops](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/industry-events-%26-workshops)**: Company recruiting sessions \(CRS\), Beyond Vancouver Panel Series, Spring Hiring Fair, and more\. Register on **[UBC Sauder Career Hub](https://sauder-ubc-csm.symplicity.com/students/app/events)**\.

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    **[Mentorship & Specialty programs](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/mentorship-specialty-programs)**: learn directly from people with business experience

Learn more about [**UBC Sauder Career Hub**](https://sauder-ubc.12twenty.com/appointments) and what it can do for you **[here](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-resources/cool-career-platform)**\.

### BCom Career Strategists & Co\-op Career Strategists

The BCC offers a variety of coaching and advising appointments you can book throughout the year \(even in the summer\!\) to get personalized, 1:1 support\. Your **[BCom Career Strategists](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/bcom-career-strategists)** and **[Co\-op Career Strategists](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching/co-op-managers)** \(for those enrolled in the Co\-op program\) will work alongside you throughout your degree to help you take action and thrive in your personal and professional life\.

Not sure what coaching & advising is? Learn more **[here](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/career-experience/career-coaching)**\.

### Connections with Business Communities

We also help students **connect with business communities**, **explore job markets**, and **find job opportunities** in Vancouver and worldwide\.

Our eight\-person **team of industry\-focused Business Development professionals** actively bridges the gap between our students and the business world\. We connect students with hundreds of potential employers, from global industry leaders to local growing startups\.

title: Student Initiatives and Government
content_markdown:
### Some of the best learning opportunities at UBC and at UBC Sauder are managed and delivered by students just like you\.

### Student government

As a UBC BCom student, you are member of both the UBC [Alma Mater Society \(AMS\)](http://www.ams.ubc.ca/) and the [Commerce Undergraduate Society \(CUS\)](http://www.cus.ca/)\. Funded by your student fees, elected representatives in both societies facilitate services and opportunities to enhance your student experience, including conferences, clubs, and social events\.

Key activities include:

-   annual conferences focusing on leadership, research, sustainability, strategic consulting, entrepreneurship, career exploration, corporate and personal branding
-   numerous opportunities to volunteer and gain leadership experience
-   career and academic services including social and professional events
-   over 370 student clubs in which to make friends and have fun

[AMS website](http://www.ams.ubc.ca/)  

[CUS website](http://www.cus.ca/)  

Student Conferences

-   [CUS Events](https://www.cus.ca/events/annual-events)
-   [MURC](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference)

-   The Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference \(MURC\) is UBC's premiere undergraduate research symposium\. Learn about the latest happenings in the world of research from inspiring keynote speakers and see some of the exceptional work being done by students in different disciplines\. Are you currently conducting some amazing research of your own? Apply to present\!

Student Clubs and Services

-   [AMS Clubs](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/student-life/clubs/) 
-   [CUS – Sponsored Clubs and Services](https://www.cus.ca/get-involved/get-to-know) 

-   [Get involved with the CUS](https://www.cus.ca/get-involved/join-the-cus) 

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/student-initiatives-and-government)

### Student conferences

Student conferences can help you build on your classroom learning, meet others with similar interests and goals, and develop communication, organizational, leadership, and networking skills\.

### CUS conferences

Each of the major conferences hosted annually by the CUS provides an excellent opportunity to increase your business acumen and meet potential employers\. Want to get involved to help organize and run one of these amazing events? Check the [CUS website](http://www.cus.ca/) and weekly CUSunday newsletter for hiring notifications\.

Here are some conferences that you can get involved with:

-   [Me Inc\.](https://www.instagram.com/ubcmeinc/)  
    An exploration of career options that focuses on the alignment of career choices with individual goals and personalities\.
-   [Imprint](https://www.ubcimprint.com/)  
    Focuses on branding, both corporate and personal, for success\. 
-   [National Strategy Consulting Conference \(NSCC\)](https://www.thenscc.com/)Provides students from Canada’s top universities with the opportunity to hone their abilities in analyzing problems, solving cases, and learn about strategic consulting\.

> #### [Activate](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/activate) 
> 
> Activate is a Student Leadership Conference held by OSAS and CUS\. Each year, Activate focuses on a different theme to support emerging leaders by providing them with keynotes, workshops, and student panels to build foundational leadership skills\.
> 
> #### [Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference](http://students.ubc.ca/career/murc)
> 
> The Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference \(MURC\) is UBC's premiere undergraduate research symposium\. Learn about the latest happenings in the world of research from inspiring keynote speakers and see some of the exceptional work being done by students in different disciplines\. Are you currently conducting some amazing research of your own? Apply to present\!

### Student clubs and services

At last count, there are over 370 AMS student clubs for you to choose from at UBC\. Dabble in the arts, join a cause, dance the night away, gaze at the stars, work up a sweat, catch the snitch \- the possibilities are endless\. 

[Explore AMS student clubs](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/student-life/clubs/)  

### CUS\-sponsored clubs

These CUS\-sponsored clubs focus on a different business discipline or topic\. Club membership is a great way to explore interests and learn about potential career paths\. See the list of CUS\-Sponsored Clubs [here](https://www.cus.ca/get-involved/get-to-know)\.

### CUS\-sponsored services

In addition to student clubs, the CUS also offers a multitude of services to students including mentorship programs, philanthropy programs, health and wellness programs, and more\. See the list of CUS\-Sponsored Services [here](https://www.cus.ca/get-involved/get-to-know)\.

title: UBC Sauder Learning Labs
content_markdown:
### What are the UBC Sauder Learning Labs?

The UBC Sauder Learning Labs are designed to foster strategic design, an emerging business discipline where multi\-disciplinary project teams use creative and critical thinking, and data analysis to create, test, and launch solutions to ‘big picture” problems\.

The learning labs are not typical classrooms\. The instructor does not stand behind a lectern at the front of the class, but instead circulates freely throughout the space\. Teams of students cluster at tables throughout the room for brainstorming and lively discussion\. Wall\-to\-wall back\-lit whiteboards serve as large canvases for ideas and mind maps\. At each table, a video camera and large LCD screen allow students to view media and communicate with other teams in the room or collaborators from anywhere in the world\.

The learning labs are home to one of the school’s most unique courses, [COMM 388 Design Methods for Business Innovation](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-388)\. In this project\-driven course, students from Commerce, Arts, Engineering and Environmental Design employ analytical and creative thinking techniques to both ask questions and find solutions to real world business challenges\. They also learn about sustainable business practices and effective teams\.

### Learn more

For more information about the UBC Sauder Learning Labs and [COMM 388](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/5247), check out the [d\.studio website](http://dstudio.ubc.ca/) or email your questions to [studio@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:studio@sauder.ubc.ca)\.

The Digital Media Lab is only able to be used by current UBC Sauder students, and access is granted through your CWL credentials\. If you have any questions, please reach out to Fei Song, Investment Labs Coordinator \([fei\.song@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:fei.song@sauder.ubc.ca)\)\.

##### Ethical/Appropriate Use of Data

-   All data should be accessed, used, and shared in accordance with UBC policies and legal  
    regulations\.
    
-   Users must adhere to strict ethical standards when using data and software\.
    
-   Unauthorized manipulation, distribution, or misuse of data and software is strictly prohibited and may result in disciplinary action\.
    

##### No Food/Drink

-   Absolutely no food is allowed in the lab\.
-   Only sealed water bottles for drinks are permitted\. Cups with straws or holes are not accepted\.

##### Responsible Use

-   Do not unplug any cords or alter the equipment setup in any way\.

-   Priority use is given to patrons who need access to the computer's specialized financial software\.

-   Do not remove or rearrange the furniture in the lab\.

##### Conduct

-   Conversations are allowed, keep a reasonable volume to maintain a conducive learning environment\.
    
-   Maintain a respectful demeanor towards all lab users and staff\.
    
-   Refrain from any disruptive behavior that could disturb others\.
    
-   Clean up your workspace before leaving\. Dispose/recycle of any trash properly\.
    
-   Respect others' privacy and work\. Do not look at or interfere with other users' screens or materials
    

##### Consequences

-   Failure to comply with these policies may result in being asked to leave the lab\.

4.  If you do not have an existing account, click on “Create New Login” under the username and password

-   Use your cell phone number as the work phone number
-   Use your *student\.ubc\.ca* email address as your work email address\. You cannot use any non\-UBC email address\. Using a generic ubc\.ca email address that does not belong to you constitutes non\-academic misconduct\.

-   Your personal Bloomberg account is associated with the Bloomberg terminal that you logged in last time, and thus will not work on other Bloomberg terminals\. 
    

If you are currently enrolled in a UBC Sauder course for which completing Bloomberg certification is an assignment, please refer to course instructions shared on your course Canvas\.

1.  Log in to the computers with the "Capital IQ" label using CWL\.stu

title: Research Support
content_markdown:
### Research for assignments

##### **Librarians Available for Research Help\!** 

David Lam Librarians are available to provide research help in\-person and via email\! Please visit [here](https://lam.library.ubc.ca/research-help-2/) for more information on how to get research help from a professional business librarian\!

##### **Research Guides:** 

Many of your class assignments will require you to find high quality information on an industry, company, consumer group, location or business topic\. Our business librarians are subject experts and they have curated many research guides for you to consult\.

-   Find books, articles, library databases and websites on topic\-based online research guides\.
-   Find guides to researching assignments for selected courses \(e\.g\., COMM\_V 296, etc\.\) on course guides\.

[David Lam Management Research Library](http://lam.library.ubc.ca/)  

### Evaluate and cite information sources

Reputable business information comes from a variety of sources\. You may need to find information from library databases and/or freely available internet sources\. It's important for you to evaluate your sources to ensure that you are using reputable and appropriate information\. Consider:

-   Author/organization credentials
-   Accuracy
-   Currency
-   Bias
-   Purpose

[Evaluating Information Sources guide](http://help.library.ubc.ca/evaluating-and-citing-sources/evaluating-information-sources/)   [UBC Library How to Cite guide](http://help.library.ubc.ca/evaluating-and-citing-sources/how-to-cite/)  

### Top research topics

Companies, industries or markets

Identify and research a company, the industry in which it operates or its target market using credible information sources\. 

[Company research](http://guides.library.ubc.ca/company)   [Industry & market research](http://guides.library.ubc.ca/industry)  

Case competitions prep

Learn how and where to research companies and industries for case competitions\.

[Case competitions guide](http://guides.library.ubc.ca/businesscases/competitions)  

Startups and entrepreneurship

Find out what it takes to start your own business using a variety of sources to understand your target industry and market, costs and funding opportunities\. 

[Entrepreneurship research guide](http://guides.library.ubc.ca/entrepreneurship)   [Small business accelerator](https://sba.ubc.ca/)  

International business

Find information sources on the business and economic climate and business culture for different countries\. 

[International business guide](http://guides.library.ubc.ca/international_business)  

Finance and investment

Data sources for popular finance and investment topics\.

[Finance and investment guide](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/finance)  

> ### Find business databases
> 
> Not sure which database will work best for your topic? Use one of the Library's **[business research guides](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/business)** such as the **[industry guide](https://guides.library.ubc.ca/industry)**, or browse the **[databases by subject](https://lam.library.ubc.ca/databases-by-subject/)** list\.
> 
> If you know the database you're looking for, use the Library's **[Database A\-Z](http://resources.library.ubc.ca/branchlist/lam/)** list to locate and access specific business databases \(e\.g\., Passport GMID, Business Source Ultimate, Bloomberg, S&P Capital IQ, and more\)\.
> 
> **Tip: Connect to databases from home using the Library's links \(you'll be prompted to login with your CWL\)\.**

# Gain an international perspective

## At the UBC Sauder School of Business there are many opportunities for you to internationalize your BCom experience and fully realize your potential on the global stage\.

### [International exchange](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/international-exchange)

Study business from an international perspective and immerse yourself in a different culture\. Check requirements and explore the possibilities\.

[Learn More](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/international-exchange)

### [Coming to UBC Sauder on exchange](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/visiting-exchange-students)

Benefit from our school's strong teaching and research reputation, diverse faculty and study body, and spectacular natural setting\.

[Learn More](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/visiting-exchange-students)

### [UBC Sauder LIFT: Africa](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/current-students/support-involvement-opportunities/ubc-sauder-lift/program)

Mentor and train aspiring entrepreneurs living in Kibera and Mathare, Kenya to develop business plans and start their own ventures\.

[Learn more](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/current-students/support-involvement-opportunities/ubc-sauder-lift/program)

### Global partnerships

You can apply to study abroad at over 200 of UBC's partner schools in 40 countries\. If you opt for a Commerce\-specific exchange, you’ll find that the UBC Sauder School of Business has partnerships with some of the best business schools around the globe—61 business schools in 30 countries\.

[Learn more about where you can go on exchange](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/international-exchange)

## UBC Sauder's Embedded Counselling Services

### Nafiza Ali \(she, her, hers\), MA

Registered Clinical Counsellor for the UBC Sauder School of Business

[Nafiza](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/custom_small_200x200_/public/2022-07/NafizaBioPicture_portrait.jpg?itok=4IBOFORJ)

Nafiza Ali \(she/her\), MA, is the registered Clinical Counsellor for the UBC Sauder School of Business\. Nafiza offers drop\-in and short\-term mental health and wellbeing counselling to undergraduate and graduate students at UBC Sauder\. She also facilitates workshops and provides outreach support tailored to the concerns and needs of students, staff, and faculty\.

Students can book an appointment with Nafiza to discuss any personal, professional, or academic concerns impacting their lives\.

To learn more and book an appointment with UBC Sauder's Embedded Counselling Services:

[UBC Sauder's Embedded Counselling Services](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/current-students/mental-health-and-wellbeing?sess=r6d3f5e0esi)

---

## Other Supports

### [Wellness Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-centre)

Talk with a trained student for tips and resources on managing stress, study tips, or navigating life as a student\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-centre)

### [Crisis Support](https://students.ubc.ca/health/crisis-support-services/)

Reach out for immediate help if you or someone else is in danger, or at risk of harming yourself or others\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/health/crisis-support-services/)

### [Sauder Wellbeing Exchange](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sauder-wellbeing-exchange)

Join fellow Sauder students for supportive conversations and practical tools to manage stress, expectations, balance, and self\-doubt\. Drop in for one session or all five\.

[Learn more](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/sauder-wellbeing-exchange)

### [EDI resources and support](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/edi-support)

Find out how to get support or discuss an issue related to discrimination, bullying, harassment or sexual misconduct

[Learn more](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/edi-support)

### [CUS Sauder Health and Wellness \(HEWE\)](https://www.sauderhewe.com/)

Sauder HEWE is a CUS Service that aims to provide events that support mental and physical wellness for all Sauder students\.

[Learn more](https://www.sauderhewe.com/)

### [Student Health Service](https://students.ubc.ca/health/student-health-service)

Visit a doctor, nurse, or other medical professional on campus for help with a variety of health concerns\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/health/student-health-service)

### Wellness Video Library 

### Take care of your mind, body, and spirit

Being mentally and physically healthy includes taking care of yourself every day, understanding that challenges are normal, and knowing what to do when you don't feel well\. 

Some of the top wellness concerns affecting students include: 

Food and nutrition

Learn how to eat well on a budget, get started on cooking, and meal prep\. Food access supports can also be found on our ['student support and resources'](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/support) page\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/food-nutrition)  

Physical activity

Being physically active can reduce stress and help you feel more energized and alert, making it a lot easier to focus on studying, writing, completing assignments or lab work, and preparing for exams\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/physical-activity/)  

Sleep

Getting enough quality sleep is crucial for performing your best\. Lack of sleep has a significant impact on brain function, health, safety, and longevity\. Sleep itself can actually improve mental function is vital for learning and memory\. 

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/sleep-success)   

Understanding stress

Stress is a normal part of the human experience\. However, everyone experiences stress differently and stressors are unique to each person\. Below you will find information on recognizing signs of stress, managing the stress response, and understanding different types of stressors\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/understanding-stress/)  

Sex & sexual health

Learning about sex and sexual health can help you have safe, respectful, and enjoyable experiences\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/sex-sexual-health/)  

Alcohol and other drugs

Understand UBC substance use policies and learn more about substance misuse\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/alcohol-cannabis-nicotine/)  

### Safety on campus

Everyone plays a role in making UBC’s Vancouver campus a safe and welcoming place\. The best way to keep our campus safe is to look out for each other and to reach out when we need help ourselves\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/)

title: CLC Book and Equipment Borrowing

### Borrowing books

The [Canaccord Learning Commons and David Lam Library](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/know-sauder/learning-commons-and-library/) have a variety of books, [ebooks](http://guides.library.ubc.ca/businessebooks) and course reserves available to all students\. All course reserves must be requested at the Service Desk\. For new releases on a variety of business topics, visit our Great Reads section on the main floor\.

### Borrowing equipment

UBC Sauder students are permitted to borrow items \(for academic use only\) from our equipment lending pool, located at the Service Desk\. All equipment is lent on a first\-come, first\-served basis and a student card is required to sign items out\. Any questions about proper care or operation can be directed to the Service Desk\. 

The CLC is not responsible for any damage to a user's computer, phone or other equipment that might be caused by items borrowed from our help desk\.

title: Printing and photocopying
content_markdown:
### Printing

[The Canaccord Learning Commons](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/clc) has two printers, one located on the main floor by the computer workstations and one by the upstairs computer workstations\. The following instructions are available to help you use the Pay for Print system\.

**How to print from a Library workstation**

1.  Log in to the desktop computer using your CWL username and password\.
2.  Navigate your web browser to [payforprint\.ubc\.ca](https://payforprint.ubc.ca:9192/user?) and log in using your EAD account\. Your EAD login is your CWL username followed by \.stu \(*e\.g\.,* jsmith\.stu\) and your CWL password\.
3.  Once logged in, your account information including available funds will display\. If you have funds in your account, you are ready to print\. If you need to add funds, click on “Add Funds – UBCcard\.”
4.  Open the file you want to print, go to “File”, select “Print” and choose a printer: “DLAM Mono on Lussier” for black and white OR “DLAM Colour on Lussier” for colour\.
5.  Log in with your EAD account when the pop\-up login box is displayed\.

At the print station swipe your UBC card in the card reader OR log in with your EAD \(CWL\.stu\) username and password\.

**How to print from Web Print \(from your laptop\)**

1.  Navigate your web browser to [payforprint\.ubc\.ca](https://payforprint.ubc.ca:9192/user?) and log in using your EAD account\. Your EAD login is your CWL username followed by \.stu \(*e\.g\.,* jsmith\.stu\) and your CWL password\.
2.  Once logged in, your account information including available funds will display\. If you have funds in your account, you are ready to print\. If you need to add funds, click on “Add Funds – UBCcard\.”
3.  Click on “Web Print” and then click on “Submit a Job\.”
4.  Select the appropriate printer:  
    -   library/Colour for colour, single\-sided
    -   library/Colour Duplex for colour, double\-sided
    -   library/Mono for black and white, single\-sided
    -   library/Mono Duplex for black and white, double\-sided
5.  Click on “Print Options and Account Selection” and then click on “Upload Documents\.”
6.  Click on “Upload from Computer” and select the file you want to print\.
7.  Click on “Upload & Complete\.”

Go to the print release station and swipe your UBC card OR log in with your EAD \(CWL\.stu\) username and password\.

### Photocopying

There is a photocopier in the copy room on the main floor available for colour or black and white copies\. The copier can be used by swiping your UBC card or entering your CWL username and password when prompted\. Staplers and papercutters are available in the copy room for your convenience\.

> ### [Printing and photocopying prices](http://services.library.ubc.ca/computers-technology/copy-print-scan/pay-for-print-students-faculty-staff/)
> 
> Printing and photocopying costs 7¢ a page for black and white, and 40¢ a page for colour\. Be sure you select the correct setting to print or copy in colour before sending your job\.
> 
> [More about Pay for Print](http://services.library.ubc.ca/computers-technology/copy-print-scan/pay-for-print-students-faculty-staff/)
> 
> ### [Reloading your card](https://payforprint.ubc.ca/)
> 
> Your UBC card is your print card\. To add funds to your card, visit payforprint\.ubc\.ca
> 
> [payforprint\.ubc\.ca](https://payforprint.ubc.ca/)

### Need help?

If you require assistance with printing or photocopying, our staff at the Service Desk will be happy to help\.

### Scanning

The colour photocopier in the copy room can be used to scan multiple pages to store directly onto a USB drive\. Please activate the copier with your UBC card or enter your CWL credentials when prompted\.

There is also a scanner in the Digital Media Lab\. It can only scan one page single\-sided at a time\. The use of this scanner is limited to five pages per user\. If you are scanning longer documents, or wish to scan double\-sided, please use the colour photocopier's feed tray\.

> ### [Scanning prices](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/know-sauder/specialized-learning-spaces/digital-media-lab)
> 
> Scanning from the feed tray of the colour photocopier costs 2¢ a page\. For small jobs there is a free flatbed scanner in the Digital Media Lab\.
>

### Thinking about studying at the UBC Sauder School of Business on exchange? We welcome exchange students from around the world\. 

### The UBC Sauder advantage

##### A rich student life

The UBC BCom program offers you a wealth of opportunities to make new friends, develop personally and professionally, and get involved\. See what [student life at UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life) is like\.

##### Our dedicated Business Career Centre

Exchange students have access to the full scope of services at UBC Sauder's [Business Career Centre \(BCC\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/know-sauder/business-career-centre) including career coaching, recruitment events, and job postings\.

##### Your Commerce Undergraduate Society

The [Commerce Undergraduate Society \(CUS\)](http://cus.ca/) is the largest student\-run business school organization in Canada, both in terms of its over $1 million annual operating budget and its thousands of active members\. Get involved in the UBC Sauder student community by participating in CUS activities\.

### Eligibility

Check our list of business partner schools to find out if your university has a business school exchange with us\. If not, you can still apply to come on exchange with the business school as long as your university has an exchange agreement with UBC\.

Explore this website and find out what our program has to offer\. Then review the UBC Go Global website for everything you need to know to make your exchange a reality\.

### Sauder International Student Association

The Sauder International Student Association is part of the CUS and a good option for students specifically interested in international student activities\. Getting involved is a great way to build relationships with other international students and to experience what the school has to offer\.

[Find out how you can get involved](https://www.instagram.com/ubcsisa/)

### Frequently asked questions about coming to the UBC Sauder on exchange

How do I apply for exchange at UBC?

Exchange at the UBC Sauder School of Business is administered through UBC Go Global\. The UBC Go Global [website](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc) includes all the information you need about coming to UBC\.

Do I have the appropriate academic background to apply to the business school?

To apply, you need to be at the academic level required for third and fourth year BCom courses\. See [studying commerce at UBC on exchange](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange/step-1-planning-eligibility/studying-commerce-ubc-exchange) for details\.

Where can I find the course schedule?

Check the Vancouver campus [course schedule](https://courses.students.ubc.ca/) for courses offered in the semester you plan to come on exchange\. Business courses are labeled COMM\_V, COHR\_V and COMR\_V\.

What courses can I take?

Exchange students can take business courses along with a wide variety of courses offered in other disciplines at UBC\. It is your responsibility to check for prerequisites to ensure you have the appropriate academic background to be successful in your courses\.

Are there any business courses I can’t take?

See [studying commerce at UBC on exchange](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange/step-1-planning-eligibility/studying-commerce-ubc-exchange) for a list of courses not available\.

Are course outlines online?

You can find brief course descriptions in the [UBC Calendar](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/courses.cfm) and more detailed descriptions on our [website](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/courses-and-registration/registration-assistancehttps:/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/courses-and-registration/registration-assistance)\. Course syllabi will be available at the start of the semester via the course website, Canvas\. If you need a syllabus in advance of the course start for transfer credit purposes you can request a recent copy by emailing [bcomquestions@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:bcomquestions@sauder.ubc.ca)\.

How many courses can I take?

A typical course load per semester is 12 to 15 credits, or 4 to 5 courses\. Consider combining business courses with courses in other disciplines as space in business courses may be limited\. Students on exchange with business will have priority in our courses\. Students on exchange through another program may request to take business courses\.

Can I take courses if I’m not on exchange with the business school?

Students on exchange through another program may request to take business courses\. While other courses may be available, COMR\_V 100, COMR\_V 329, COMR 398\_V, COMR 458\_V, COMR 465\_V, COMR\_V 473, and COMR\_V 493 are typically taken by students in non\-business majors\.

How can I make changes to my registered courses?

To request changes to your registration including course add, course switch and course section switch please submit a registration assistance form [here](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/courses-and-registration/registration-assistancehttps:/mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-and-enrolment/courses-and-registration/registration-assistance)\.  You can drop courses yourself via [Workday Student](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/dropping-a-course/)\.

title: Sean Gilbert - Crowe MacKay LLP Memorial Award (#1017)
content_markdown:
Awards have been made through an endowment established by family, friends and colleagues in memory of Sean Gilbert \(1965\-2012\), for outstanding Bachelor of Commerce students in the Accounting option\. Sean Gilbert \(B\.Com\. 1988\) was a Chartered Accountant at MacKay LLP for twenty\-five years\. This award was established as a tribute to Sean and recognizes his legacy of selflessness, mentorship, and commitment to excellence in professional practice and education\.

title: Peter Lee Scholarship in Finance (#1666)
content_markdown:
Scholarships are offered by Peter Lee to students entering the third or fourth year of the Finance option in the Bachelor of Commerce Program at the Sauder School of Business\. The awards are made on the recommendation of the school\.

Applications are now being accepted for one of four awards of $5,000 each under the Peter Lee Scholarships in Finance\. The recipients will be individuals with a strong interest in finance and a high degree of motivation for a career in the capital markets\.

Qualifications:             

-   3\[rd\] or 4\[th\]\-year Sauder School of Business undergraduate student in the Finance Option
-   Outstanding academic credentials
-   Evidence of leadership skills and the ability to work well in groups
-   Evidence of a desire for a career in the capital markets

Application Process: Applicants must submit one pdf file with three items in the order shown:

1.  A 1\-page cover letter stating why they deserve the scholarship
2.  A 1\-page resume
3.  A list of all university \(UBC or elsewhere\) grades \(this can be an o[fficial or an unofficial](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/), but accurate, transcript\)

**Application Deadline: Noon, Friday, 18 October 2024** 

Submit applications by email to: Professor Rob Heinkel \| [Rob\.heinkel@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:Rob.heinkel@sauder.ubc.ca)

Additional Qualifications: The Peter Lee Scholarship is a UBC\-recognized scholarship\. As such, it will appear on the scholarship recipients’ transcripts\.

title: Harold A. Jones Memorial Scholarship (#1512)
content_markdown:
The Harold A\. Jones Memorial Scholarship is donated by Seaspan ULC \(an organization integrating Vancouver Tug Boat Co\. Ltd\. and Island Tug & Barge Limited, both pioneer companies in marine transportation on the B\.C\. coast\) as a memorial to Harold A\. Jones, who was President of Vancouver Tug Boat Co\. Ltd\. from 1924 to 1956\. This scholarship serves not only to pay tribute to Mr\. Jones' contribution to the company, but also to give recognition to his interest and participation, both public and personal, in all matters pertaining to coast\-wise shipping\. The scholarship is to be awarded to an outstanding student entering the final year in the Bachelor of Commerce Program and majoring in the field of transportation in the Sauder School of Business\.

title: COMR_V 100 - Introduction to Business
content_markdown:
This course informs potential managers and knowledge workers in all business areas about issues and problems related to the planning, establishment, and management of a successful business\. The course and the text take an "integrative" approach\. That is, the course aims to introduce the student to the concept of "business," as a whole, by examining the types of activities any business engages in\. During this inquiry, the course will investigate a number of problems and opportunities that typically occur while a business conducts these activities\.  
  
Students will gain an understanding of the fundamentals of business structure, activities, and the forces — both internal and external — that impact businesses\. In particular, by studying how the "parts" interact together to form the "whole," you will learn how businesses work, and about how the interaction of the parts determines whether businesses fail or succeed\.

### Learning objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the knowledge and skills to:

-   understand the role of vision, organizational design, and structure in business\.
-   identify a variety of indicators of desirable performance\.
-   understand how the environment impacts business activities and performance\.
-   understand the factors involved in providing a product or service\.
-   evaluate the outcomes of business processes\.

Note:

-   Formely numbered COMM 100
-   Equivalent to COMM 120\.

3

title: COMM_V 101 - Business Fundamentals
content_markdown:
## Course Description

COMM 101 provides a broad introduction to the field of business\. It gives students a big\-picture understanding of the different business functions they may study at Sauder, including finance, accounting, marketing, operations and logistics, entrepreneurship, organizational behaviour and human resources, and strategy\.  
The course also provides an introduction to AI and how students can determine which tasks to delegate to AI, communicate with AI, evaluate AI outputs critically, and use AI responsibly as part of business decisions\.

COMM 101 is designed for students to bring their unique perspectives and backgrounds into lessons and discussions\. Your instructors bring diverse experience and expertise to the classroom to provide a multidimensional look at business\.

### Responsible Business Content

This course addresses responsible business and sustainable development through real\-world case studies and a consulting project that provide opportunities to apply discipline\-specific decision\-making techniques across a variety of industries and contexts\. Students assess whether proposed business models are feasible, realistic, and socially responsible, including whether they support fair compensation, inclusive hiring, employee well\-being, and long\-term organizational sustainability\. Students also reflect on their use of AI in academic contexts and how to use artificial intelligence thoughtfully and responsibly\.

### Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the knowledge and skills to:

-   Explore the building blocks of business, including various specializations, analytical tools, and real\-world cases\.
-   Apply knowledge from diverse business disciplines to address business opportunities\.
-   Develop practical oral and written communication skills through class participation and course assignments\.
-   Collaborate on a team of peers to consult for a business using course tools and creative thinking\.
-   Use AI effectively, critically, and responsibly across business contexts\.

### Students Will Gain Confidence In

-   Critically diagnosing business problems by evaluating evidence, applying frameworks, and identifying assumptions to distinguish material insights from unsupported, misleading, or strategically irrelevant claims\.
-   Integrating quantitative and qualitative insights across business functions to assess trade\-offs and make decisions under uncertainty\.
-   Developing practical, evidence\-based strategies that balance customer value, financial impact, operational feasibility, risk, and stakeholder interests\.
-   Collaborating effectively with diverse teammates and AI tools to create, communicate, and defend high\-quality work\.

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 202 - Career Fundamentals
content_markdown:
## Course Description

COMM 202 helps students explore, pursue, and prepare for meaningful work using the four pillars of the Hari B\. Varshney Business Career Centre's career development model: Know Yourself, Tell Your Story, Explore Career Opportunities, and Learn Through Experience\. Topics include career design and self\-assessment, the future of work, emotional intelligence, career exploration, job\-search strategies, networking and relationship\-building, resumes and cover letters, interviews, and navigating employment offers\. Content is delivered through lectures, interactive tutorials, workshops, reflective exercises, networking activities, and practice with peers and industry professionals\. Emphasis is placed on self\-awareness, career adaptability, professional communication, relationship\-building, and the ability to communicate one's value authentically and persuasively\. Assessment methods may include career\-design reflections, an emotional\-intelligence assessment and development plan, a tailored resume and cover letter, a relationships\-building assignment, participation, and an employment interview\.

### Responsible Business Content

The course addresses responsible business and sustainable development by examining how personal values, inclusion, emotional intelligence, and well\-being contribute to meaningful, equitable, and sustainable careers and workplaces\. Students practise truthful self\-representation, respectful and inclusive relationship\-building, responsible use of AI\-supported career tools, and ethical decision\-making throughout recruitment and employment processes\.

### Learning Objectives

-   Summarize and rank their priorities and values, craft career aspirations through personal reflection, and formulate meaningful goals for their professional development\.
-   Evaluate various career paths, companies, and industries, and identify the necessary steps to pursue their next job experience\.
-   Recognize the importance of establishing and cultivating professional relationships, and apply relationship\-building skills to expand their network and gain valuable insights and support their career journeys\.
-   Explore the importance of Emotional Intelligence in career advancement, which is critical for job acquisition, reflect on personal EQ strengths and areas for improvement and develop strategies and practices for cultivating and enhancing EQ skill sets for career success\.
-   Identify, locate, and effectively utilize various services and resources provided by the Hari B\. Varshney Business Career Centre \(BCC\), to support their career development, enhance job search strategies, and increase their chances of securing job opportunities\. Examples: Career Coaching & Advising, Career Options Online \(COOL\), Career Toolkits and Industry Guides\.

### Students Will Gain Confidence In

-   Create persuasive narratives emphasizing their relevant skills and job alignment, and effectively communicate their value to employers through resumes, cover letters, networking opportunities, and interviews\.
-   Employ effective job search strategies, such as networking and utilizing online platforms like COOL & SEAT, to increase their chances of securing relevant opportunities\.

Course credits:

1

title: COMM_V 280 - Entrepreneurship
content_markdown:
Entrepreneurship involves creativity, critical thinking and a commitment to research and develop new ideas and associated business models\. Entrepreneurs, in both startups and corporations \(also known as, intrapreneurs\), possess a mindset and skillset to identify, articulate and solve compelling problems\. This interactive course provides an introduction to the fundamental principles, concepts, and frameworks essential for aspiring venture founders\. Additionally, it explores the typical challenges encountered in identifying customer needs, validating product ideas, and refining business models\. Students will learn how to identify desirable and viable opportunities; experiment, prototype and test market\-driven ideas; form a founding team; and, design innovative business models\. In simulated ‘startup’ teams, comprised of students from all faculties, you will apply the concepts of ideation, customer discovery, experimentation, prototyping, and proposing a new venture\.

The course is a strongly recommended course for COMM 386M \(NEW: Green Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Startups\) and COMM466/APSC 486 \(New Venture Design\)\.

Eligibility: This course is open to BCom students in Years 2 and 3, and non\-BCom students in Years 2, 3, and 4\. 

### Learning objectives

By the end of this experiential course, students will be able to: 

-   Understand key considerations, opportunities and challenges for entrepreneurs and innovators\.
-   Gain experience with common entrepreneurial methods, tools and resources\.
-   Develop an initial plan for an innovative entrepreneurial venture\.
-   Explore your potential as an entrepreneur and intrapreneur\. 

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 271 - Introduction to Capital Markets
content_markdown:
COMM 271 is designed for curious, motivated students eager to explore the world of capital markets\. It blends rigorous academic content with first\-hand perspectives from leading professionals across the entire spectrum of the industry: private equity, private credit, investment banking, quantitative investing, hedge funds, and thematic investing\. Students will not only study the economic foundations that shape market behavior but also engage directly with practitioners who apply these concepts in high\-stakes, real\-world settings\. 

The course fosters integrated learning: academic frameworks will inform discussions with industry experts, while professional insights will enrich students’ theoretical understanding\. By the end, students will have developed a holistic, practice\-informed view of capital markets, preparing them to think critically and operate effectively in this dynamic environment\.

### Learning objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to: 

-   Analyze the roles of key institutions and functions within capital markets, and assess how various career paths align with their skills, interests, and long\-term goals\.  

-   Interpret and respond to written and verbal communications commonly used in capital markets, applying appropriate terminology and professional conventions\.  
    

-   Identify and evaluate firm\-specific and market\-level factors that influence fundamental value\. 
    

-   Apply core valuation frameworks and techniques to assess the attractiveness of stock investments\. 
    

-   Develop and present well\-supported written and verbal arguments regarding the fairness of a company’s valuation\.  
    

-   Integrate rigorous academic theory with practitioner insights to design and deliver a comprehensive stock valuation project, demonstrating the ability to synthesize multiple perspectives into an actionable investment view\.

### Admission

Admission to COMM 271 is by application only and is restricted to BCom students entering Year 2\. To apply, please self\-enroll in the course admission site using this [link](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/M48GCE)[https://canvas\.ubc\.ca/enroll/M48GCE](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/M48GCE) and complete all components of the application package provided\. For any questions about the course or the application process, please feel free to contact James Shou at [james\.shou@sauder\.ubc\.ca](mailto:james.shou@sauder.ubc.ca)\. 

For the 2026 Winter Session, the deadline to apply is **Friday,** **June 19, 2026**\. Successful applicants will be notified of acceptance and registered in the course in early July\. 

Students with a pre\-existing interest in capital markets may also consider applying to the [UBC Portfolio Management Foundation](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/thought-leadership/divisions/finance/pmf-program)[https://www\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/thought\-leadership/divisions/finance/pmf\-program](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/thought-leadership/divisions/finance/pmf-program) \(PMF\) program in their second year or to the [UBC Sauder Women\+ in Finance Training](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/swift)[https://www\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/swift](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/swift)\(SWIFT\) program\. However, please note that admission to COMM 271 is not a factor in the selection process for either PMF or SWIFT\. This course is intended to help students prepare for a career in capital markets, regardless of whether they plan to participate in the PMF or SWIFT program\. 

Students with a pre\-existing interest in capital markets or any area in finance more broadly are encouraged to pursue the [Early Start to Finance Option](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/early-start-to-the-finance-option)[https://mybcom\.sauder\.ubc\.ca/early\-start\-to\-the\-finance\-option](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/early-start-to-the-finance-option)\.

title: COMM_V 190 - Introduction to Quantitative Decision Making
content_markdown:
## Course Description

Introduction to decision models in business, including basic optimization, linear programming, probability, decision analysis, random variables, simulation, and solving decision problems using spreadsheet tools\.

### Responsible Business Content

This course incorporates responsible business perspectives through applications of quantitative decision\-making in areas such as sustainable resource allocation, healthcare operations, and public\-sector planning \(Environmental Sustainability, Health and Well\-Being, Responsible Business and Ethics\)\.

Strongly recommended as corequisite: One of MATH\_V 100, MATH\_V 102, MATH\_V 104, MATH\_V 110, MATH\_V 120, MATH\_V 180, MATH\_V 184\.

title: COMM_V 191 - Application of Statistics in Business
content_markdown:
## Course Description

Methods and applications of statistics in business; data analysis, descriptive regression; data generation; sampling distributions; hypothesis testing; confidence intervals; two sample problems; inference in regression\.

### Responsible Business Content

This course incorporates responsible business perspectives through the application of statistical methods to business and societal challenges, including infrastructure and innovation, equity and inclusion, and environmental sustainability \(Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure, Reduced Inequalities, and Climate Action\)\.

### Learning Objectives

-   Interpret and critically evaluate data using appropriate graphical, numerical, and statistical methods\.
-   Apply statistical inference techniques to draw evidence\-based conclusions and assess uncertainty in business and real\-world contexts\.
-   Develop and interpret regression models to explain relationships between variables and make informed predictions\.
-   Select appropriate statistical methods to analyze data and solve business and analytical problems\.
-   Communicate statistical findings effectively and critically assess the validity, limitations, and implications of data\-driven conclusions\.

title: COMM_V 192 - Management and Organizational Behaviour
content_markdown:
## Course Description

Organizations succeed through people\. This course introduces students to the principles of organizational behaviour and management by examining how individuals, teams, and organizations think, feel, and behave in the workplace\. Students explore topics including perception, personality, motivation, teamwork, leadership, power and influence, organizational culture, decision making, ethics, and organizational design\. Through interactive discussions, case analyses, team projects, and applied exercises, students develop evidence\-based management skills to understand workplace behaviour, lead themselves and others effectively, collaborate in diverse teams, and make informed managerial decisions that enhance both organizational performance and employee well\-being\.

### Responsible Business Content

This course addresses responsible business by examining how managers create ethical, inclusive, and high\-performing workplaces where individuals and teams can thrive\. Students learn how leadership, organizational culture, motivation, decision making, and power influence employee well\-being, collaboration, and organizational effectiveness\. The course emphasizes evidence\-based management and ethical decision making, encouraging students to consider the broader consequences of managerial actions for employees, organizations, and society \(Responsible Business and Ethics\)\.

In addition, through topics such as gender and leadership, teamwork, organizational culture, and respectful workplace interactions, students develop the knowledge and skills to foster inclusive organizations that value diverse perspectives and promote belonging \(Indigenous \+ Equity, Diversity and Inclusion\)\. The course also highlights the importance of creating psychologically healthy and supportive work environments that enable individuals to perform, develop, and flourish \(Health and Well\-being\)\.

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 293 - Financial Accounting
content_markdown:
## Course Description

This course introduces students to key concepts and practices in financial accounting\. Financial accounting is principally concerned with the construction and interpretation of financial reports prepared for external parties to the issuing firm or entity\. Topics include the accounting cycle, accrual accounting, adjusting entries, merchandising operations, inventory, revenue recognition, receivables, property, plant and equipment, intangible assets, shareholders’ equity, liabilities, cash flow statements, carbon accounting, and financial statement analysis\. Content is delivered through lectures, tutorials, quizzes, group assignments, and practice problems, with student engagement fostered through collaborative group work, class and tutorial discussions, and exercises\.

Consideration will be given to accounting techniques and the formulation of financial reports; however, the course focuses on understanding accounting policies, their rationale, and their implications for users of financial accounting information\. Emphasis is placed on developing an understanding of the concepts, principles, and conventions upon which financial accounting is based; appreciating the extent of professional judgment required in measuring and recording transactions and preparing financial statements; and building an analytical basis for interpreting financial statements\. The course uses a user\-oriented approach that includes interpretation and assessment of financial statements from a variety of North American corporations\. Students will have multiple opportunities to apply core accounting knowledge and use financial information to make better decisions in real\-world business and organizational contexts\. Assessment methods include group assignments, peer evaluations, quizzes, a midterm exam, and a final exam\.

### Responsible Business Content

This course addresses responsible business and sustainable development by examining how transparent, informative, and ethically prepared financial accounting information supports better decision\-making by external users and contributes to strong institutions and well\-functioning markets\. Topics include brief introduction to carbon accounting and climate\-related reporting \(Environmental Sustainability; Climate Action\), professional judgment and ethical financial reporting \(Responsible Business and Ethics; Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions\), and the measurement of infrastructure and intangible assets, including innovation\-related assets \(Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure\)\.

### Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

-   Discuss and apply the concepts, principles, and conventions of financial accounting to business transactions at a broad level\.
-   Identify and explain the role of judgment in accounting\.
-   Broadly interpret and apply professional ethical codes and norms\.
-   Analyze financial statements\.
-   Diagnose and solve common financial accounting issues impacting businesses\.
-   Evaluate common financial accounting problems, dilemmas, and methods\.

### Students Will Gain Confidence In

-   Interpret and assess financial statements to understand a firm’s financial position, performance, and underlying accounting choices\.
-   Apply financial accounting concepts, principles, and conventions to analyze common business transactions and reporting issues\.
-   Evaluate the role of professional judgment and ethical considerations in measuring, recording, and reporting financial information\.
-   Use financial accounting information to support informed decision\-making by external users, including investors, creditors, and other stakeholders\.

Prerequisite: One of MATH\_V 100, MATH\_V 102, MATH\_V 104, MATH\_V 110, MATH\_V 120, MATH\_V 180, MATH\_V 184, MATH\_O 100, MATH\_O 116\. 

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 294 - Managerial Accounting
content_markdown:
## Course Description

COMM 294 is an introductory course that provides the fundamental concepts of managerial accounting\. Unlike financial reporting, which focuses on presenting information to outside financial report users, managerial accounting is mainly focused on providing information to internal management to make better production/manufacturing decisions\. The course covers basic concepts and ideas on cost system design, cost behavior, cost\-volume profit relationships, budgeting, variance analysis, and decision making\. Students who like to learn more about cost accounting and managerial accounting can take COMM 354 and COMM 454 in the future\.

### Responsible Business Content

The course also has implications for how management accounting supports sustainable and responsible business through efficient resource use, informed decision\-making, and effective incentive systems\.

### Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the knowledge and skills to:

-   Understand different cost concepts\.
-   Know how costs are allocated to products or services depending on the underlying cost driver\.
-   Use information to analyze cost variation, and to make better business decisions\.
-   Develop their problem\-solving skills and apply their knowledge and understanding of managerial accounting to solve real\-world problems\.

Prerequisite: [COMM\_V 293](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-293)\.

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 295 - Managerial Economics
content_markdown:
## Course Description

This course covers the economic foundations of managerial decision–making\. Topics include supply and demand, empirical methods, organization and objectives of business enterprises, competition and monopoly, pricing with market power, oligopoly, game theory, uncertainty and information, agency relationships, and behavioral economics\. This course is primarily a lecture course although in\-class activities such as poll questions and class discussion are important parts of the course\. Emphasis is placed on analytical reasoning and applying economic models to business settings, preparing students to assess managerial choices in a systematic way\. Assessment methods include exams, group projects, take\-home assignments, and in\-class participation\.

### Responsible Business Content

This course addresses responsible business and sustainable development by considering and analyzing how private sector firms can efficiently provide access to goods and services, including to those at the lowest end of the income spectrum \(No Poverty\)\. A large part of the course also discusses various forms of industrial organization and their implications for consumer well\-being \(Responsible Consumption and Production\)\.

### Learning Objectives

By the end of the course students will:

-   Apply economic models and economic analysis to a wide range of business problems, including pricing decisions and competitive strategy decisions\.
-   Describe, interpret, and analyze economic issues reported in the business media\.
-   Use diagrams, statistical and mathematical techniques, spreadsheets, and verbal logic while carrying out economic analysis\.

### Students Will Gain Confidence In

-   Critically evaluate financial statements to identify underlying assumptions, risks, and strategic implications\.
-   Navigate ambiguity in cross\-functional team environments by applying evidence\-based frameworks for collaboration and conflict resolution\.
-   Construct and defend ethical business strategies that balance competing stakeholder interests and organizational values\.
-   Translate complex technical and quantitative findings into clear, credible, and actionable insights for non\-specialist audiences\.
-   Assess the organizational and societal implications of business decisions across diverse economic and cultural contexts\.
-   Integrate competing theoretical perspectives to develop original, well\-reasoned positions on complex business problems\.

*Prerequisite: Either \(a\) ECON\_V 100 or \(b\) all of ECON\_V 101 or ECON\_O 101, ECON\_V 102 or ECON\_O 102\.* 

*Note: Credit may be obtained for only one of ECON\_V 201, ECON\_V 206, ECON\_V 301, ECON\_V 304, FRE\_V 295, COMM\_V 295\.*

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 296 - Introduction to Marketing
content_markdown:
## Course Description

This course is designed to provide a broad introduction to the field of marketing\. Marketing is far more than just selling or advertising within a business setting; it is a major part of everyday life\. This course will illustrate the importance of marketing and will help students develop fundamental marketing knowledge and skills applicable to all specializations within business\. Topics include context analysis; consumer behaviour; marketing research; segmentation, targeting, and positioning; product, price, distribution, and promotion strategies; and ethics and sustainable marketing\. Content is delivered through lectures, in\-class activities, and multimedia resources\. Emphasis is placed on critical thinking and practice, preparing students to maximize the value of marketing across wide\-ranging industries and organizations\. Assessment methods may include quizzes, in\-class exercises, group projects, exams, and discussions\.

### Responsible Business Content

This course addresses responsible business and sustainable development by examining how marketing decisions, from analyzing the external environment to designing the marketing mix, shape outcomes for consumers, organizations, and society\. Topics include the macroenvironmental factors shaping sustainable production and consumption, sustainable and circular supply chains, and sustainability marketing strategy \(Environmental Sustainability\); equity, diversity, inclusion, and Indigenous reconciliation, examined through segmentation, targeting, and positioning and marketing's broader social impact \(Indigenous \+ Equity, Diversity and Inclusion\); and marketing codes of conduct and the study of consumer behaviour to understand how to encourage and support responsible decision making \(Responsible Business and Ethics\)\.

### Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the knowledge and skills to:

-   Understand marketing's role in creating value for consumers, society, and organizations, including its ethical responsibilities\.
-   Analyze the micro\- and macro\-environmental factors and consumer behaviour influences that shape marketing strategy\.
-   Conduct marketing research and apply the segmentation, targeting, and positioning \(STP\) process to identify target markets\.
-   Integrate the four elements of the marketing mix into a balanced, strategic marketing plan for a product/organization\.
-   Understand the capabilities, limitations, and responsible use of generative AI in marketing\.

Corequisite: [COMM\_V 293](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-293) and one of [COMM\_V 295](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-295), ECON\_V 201, ECON\_V 301\. 

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 298 - Introduction to Finance
content_markdown:
## Course Description

This course introduces students to key concepts and practices in corporate finance and investments\. Topics include corporate objectives, debt and equity valuation, market efficiency, risk and return, portfolio diversification, the Capital Asset Pricing Model, capital budgeting, personal financial decision\-making, and international finance\. Content is delivered through in\-person lectures paired with hands\-on activities and discussions, with student engagement fostered through practice quizzes, group case assignments, and peer evaluation\. Emphasis is placed on applied, quantitative problem\-solving, preparing students to apply financial concepts to real\-world corporate and personal decisions\. Assessment methods include a midterm test, a final test, a personal finance case assignment, and an equity research challenge\.

### Responsible Business Content

This course addresses responsible business and sustainable development by examining how financial markets and corporate decision\-making intersect with sustainability outcomes\. Students explore how valuation frameworks can support risk assessment for innovative and sustainability\-linked projects \(Environmental Sustainability\), how investor behavior and asset allocation can drive climate action \(Environmental Sustainability\), and how the alignment of corporate objectives with stockholder interests shapes responsible business practices \(Responsible Business and Ethics\)\.

### Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the knowledge and skills to:

-   Describe the objectives of a corporation, the features of financial markets, and the securities \(debt and equity\) used to finance it\.
-   Apply time value of money and valuation principles to price bonds and stocks\.
-   Analyze risk and return by calculating portfolio risk measures, distinguishing systematic from idiosyncratic risk, and interpreting market efficiency\.
-   Evaluate investment and corporate finance decisions, including risk\-return trade\-offs and capital budgeting\.
-   Apply financial concepts to personal investment decisions and international finance contexts, synthesizing course material for real\-world use\.

 Corequisite: [COMM\_V 293](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-293) and [COMM\_V 190](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/node/5219) \(formerly numbered as COMM 290\)\.

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 306 - Urban Land Economics
content_markdown:
Urban economics examines various urban issues from the economic perspective\. These issues concern urban land and housing market, urban transportation, urban crime, urban sprawl, land use policies, etc, and we study them as social equilibria arising from individual agent’s profit or utility maximizing behavior\.

### Learning objectives

The objectives of this course are to:

-   provide students clearer understanding of traditional urban issues\.
-   provide a logical framework for analyzing new issues students may come across in the future\.
-   make students more familiar with related data source and computer programs to analyze them\.

Prerequisite: One of [COMM 295](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-295), ECON 201, ECON 301\.

Course credits:

3

title: COMM_V 307 - Real Estate Investment
content_markdown:
This course is a one semester study intended to give students the tools for critical analysis of public and private equity positions in existing real estate assets\. Project analysis and evaluation are presented within the context of understanding real estate markets as distinct economic phenomenon\. The course covers the economics of real estate markets, market analysis, investment analysis tools such as pro\-formas \(real estate specific discounted cash flow\), debt financing of real estate, leasing and property management, appraisal and the pricing of heterogeneous goods, real estate securitization, real estate in a diversified portfolio, and information and process technologies and real estate\. Academic lectures are supplemented by a series of guest lectures by local real estate professionals\.

Prerequisite: One of [COMM 295](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-295), ECON 201, ECON 301 and one of COMM 297, [COMM 298](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses/comm-298)\.
